## `apps/web/sw.js`

```javascript
// Forge service worker: shell caching only. API traffic is never cached, so
// answers and citations are always live and never stale.
const SHELL = "forge-shell-v1";
const ASSETS = ["/", "/index.html", "/styles.css", "/app.js", "/icon.svg", "/manifest.webmanifest"];

self.addEventListener("install", (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(caches.open(SHELL).then((c) => c.addAll(ASSETS)).then(() => self.skipWaiting()));
});

self.addEventListener("activate", (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) => Promise.all(keys.filter((k) => k !== SHELL).map((k) => caches.delete(k))))
      .then(() => self.clients.claim())
  );
});

self.addEventListener("fetch", (event) => {
  const url = new URL(event.request.url);
  if (event.request.method !== "GET" || url.origin !== location.origin || url.pathname.startsWith("/api/")) {
    return; // network only for everything that matters
  }
  event.respondWith(
    caches.match(event.request).then((hit) => hit || fetch(event.request).then((res) => {
      const copy = res.clone();
      caches.open(SHELL).then((c) => c.put(event.request, copy)).catch(() => {});
      return res;
    }).catch(() => caches.match("/index.html")))
  );
});
```

## `crates/bininspect/src/apk.rs`

```rust
//! APK analysis: container inventory, manifest, DEX code facts, native libs and
//! signing material ‚Äî assembled into one report.

use crate::axml;
use crate::dex;
use crate::hashes::{entropy, sha1, sha256, strings_of};
use forge_core::ingest::zip;

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct ApkInfo {
    pub package: String,
    pub version_name: String,
    pub version_code: String,
    pub min_sdk: Option<String>,
    pub target_sdk: Option<String>,
    pub permissions: Vec<String>,
    pub activities: Vec<(String, bool)>,
    pub services: Vec<(String, bool)>,
    pub receivers: Vec<(String, bool)>,
    pub providers: Vec<(String, bool)>,
    pub exported_count: usize,
    pub debuggable: bool,
    pub allow_backup: Option<bool>,
    pub cleartext_allowed: Option<bool>,
    pub dex_files: Vec<String>,
    pub class_count: usize,
    pub method_count: usize,
    pub string_count: usize,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub native_libs: Vec<String>,
    pub abis: Vec<String>,
    pub entry_count: usize,
    pub uncompressed_bytes: u64,
    pub largest: Vec<(String, u64, f64)>,
    pub signature_files: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub assets: Vec<String>,
    pub findings: Vec<dex::Finding>,
    pub indicators: Vec<String>,
    pub embedded_urls: Vec<String>,
}

pub fn is_zip(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    data.starts_with(b"PK\x03\x04") || data.starts_with(b"PK\x05\x06")
}

pub fn analyze(data: &[u8]) -> Result<ApkInfo, String> {
    if !is_zip(data) {
        return Err("apk: not a ZIP container".into());
    }
    let entries = zip::entries(data).map_err(|e| format!("apk: {}", e))?;
    let mut info = ApkInfo {
        entry_count: entries.len(),
        ..Default::default()
    };

    let mut sizes: Vec<(String, u64, f64)> = Vec::new();
    for e in &entries {
        info.uncompressed_bytes += e.uncompressed_size;
        let body = zip::read(data, e).unwrap_or_default();
        sizes.push((e.name.clone(), e.uncompressed_size, entropy(&body)));
    }
    sizes.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1));
    info.largest = sizes.into_iter().take(8).collect();

    // ---- manifest
    let manifest_bytes = zip::read_named(data, "AndroidManifest.xml")
        .map_err(|e| format!("apk: {}", e))?
        .ok_or_else(|| "apk: AndroidManifest.xml missing (not an Android package)".to_string())?;
    let elements = axml::parse(&manifest_bytes)?;
    let m = axml::summarize(&elements);
    info.package = m.package;
    info.version_name = m.version_name;
    info.version_code = m.version_code;
    info.min_sdk = m.min_sdk;
    info.target_sdk = m.target_sdk;
    info.permissions = m.permissions;
    info.activities = m.activities;
    info.services = m.services;
    info.receivers = m.receivers;
    info.providers = m.providers;
    info.exported_count = m.exported_count;
    info.debuggable = m.debuggable;
    info.allow_backup = m.allow_backup;
    info.cleartext_allowed = m.uses_cleartext_traffic;

    // ---- dex
    let mut all_findings: Vec<dex::Finding> = Vec::new();
    let mut urls: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for e in &entries {
        if e.name.starts_with("classes") && e.name.ends_with(".dex") {
            let body = zip::read(data, e).unwrap_or_default();
            match dex::parse(&body) {
                Ok(d) => {
                    info.dex_files.push(e.name.clone());
                    info.class_count += d.classes;
                    info.method_count += d.methods;
                    info.string_count += d.strings;
                    for c in d.class_names {
                        if !c.starts_with("Landroid/") && !c.starts_with("Ljava/") {
                            info.classes.push(c);
                        }
                    }
                    all_findings.extend(d.interesting);
                }
                Err(err) => info.indicators.push(format!("{}: {}", e.name, err)),
            }
        }
    }
    info.classes.sort();
    info.classes.dedup();
    info.classes.truncate(200);
    all_findings.sort_by(|a, b| a.category.cmp(b.category).then(a.detail.cmp(&b.detail)));
    all_findings.dedup_by(|a, b| a.detail == b.detail);
    for f in &all_findings {
        if f.category == "cleartext_url" {
            // detail is "hardcoded cleartext URL: `http://...`" ‚Äî keep just the URL
            let url = f
                .detail
                .split('`')
                .nth(1)
                .map(|u| u.to_string())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| f.detail.clone());
            urls.push(url);
        }
    }
    urls.sort();
    urls.dedup();
    urls.truncate(40);
    info.embedded_urls = urls;
    info.findings = all_findings;

    // ---- native + assets + signatures
    for e in &entries {
        if e.name.starts_with("lib/") && e.name.ends_with(".so") {
            info.native_libs.push(e.name.clone());
            if let Some(abi) = e.name.split('/').nth(1) {
                info.abis.push(abi.to_string());
            }
        }
        if e.name.starts_with("assets/") {
            info.assets.push(e.name.clone());
        }
        let upper = e.name.to_uppercase();
        if e.name.starts_with("META-INF/")
            && (upper.ends_with(".RSA") || upper.ends_with(".DSA") || upper.ends_with(".EC"))
        {
            let body = zip::read(data, e).unwrap_or_default();
            let names = strings_of(&body, 4)
                .into_iter()
                .filter(|s| {
                    s.contains("CN=") || s.contains("O=") || s.contains("SHA") || s.contains("Android")
                })
                .take(3)
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join("; ");
            info.signature_files
                .push((e.name.clone(), format!("sha256:{} {}", &sha256(&body)[..16], names)));
        }
    }
    info.abis.sort();
    info.abis.dedup();
    info.assets.truncate(40);

    // ---- indicators
    let mut ind: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    if info.debuggable {
        ind.push("application is marked android:debuggable=\"true\" ‚Äî ships with debugging enabled".into());
    }
    if info.allow_backup == Some(true) {
        ind.push("android:allowBackup=\"true\" ‚Äî app data can be extracted via adb backup/on supported devices".into());
    }
    if info.cleartext_allowed == Some(true) {
        ind.push("android:usesCleartextTraffic=\"true\" ‚Äî plaintext HTTP is permitted".into());
    }
    for (name, exported) in info
        .activities
        .iter()
        .chain(info.services.iter())
        .chain(info.receivers.iter())
        .chain(info.providers.iter())
    {
        if *exported {
            ind.push(format!("exported component (reachable by other apps): {}", name));
        }
    }
    if info.signature_files.is_empty() {
        ind.push("no META-INF signature block (v1) ‚Äî may be unsigned, or v2/v3-only".into());
    }
    if info.native_libs.is_empty() {
        ind.push("no native libraries: pure Java/Kotlin bytecode".into());
    } else {
        ind.push(format!(
            "{} native libraries for ABI(s) {} ‚Äî code analysis needs a native disassembler",
            info.native_libs.len(),
            info.abis.join(", ")
        ));
    }
    if !info.embedded_urls.is_empty() {
        ind.push(format!(
            "{} hardcoded cleartext URL(s) in bytecode strings",
            info.embedded_urls.len()
        ));
    }
    info.indicators = ind;
    Ok(info)
}

/// Public APK verifier heuristics: does the signature block actually cover the file?
/// (Full APK Signature Scheme v2 verification needs CMS parsing ‚Äî reported as a gap.)
pub fn signature_digest(data: &[u8]) -> (String, String) {
    (sha256(data), sha1(data))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn fixture(name: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        std::fs::read(
            std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
                .join("../../tests/fixtures/apk")
                .join(name),
        )
        .expect("apk fixture missing")
    }

    #[test]
    fn analyzes_a_real_apk_container() {
        let info = analyze(&fixture("sample.apk")).expect("apk");
        assert_eq!(info.package, "com.example.forgetest");
        assert_eq!(info.version_name, "1.2.3");
        assert!(info.permissions.contains(&"android.permission.INTERNET".to_string()));
        assert!(info.dex_files.contains(&"classes.dex".to_string()));
        assert!(info.class_count >= 2, "classes: {}", info.class_count);
        assert!(info.classes.iter().any(|c| c.contains("Crypto")));
        assert_eq!(info.abis, vec!["arm64-v8a".to_string()]);
        assert!(info.entry_count >= 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn flags_debuggable_and_exported_components() {
        let info = analyze(&fixture("sample.apk")).expect("apk");
        assert!(info.debuggable);
        assert!(info
            .indicators
            .iter()
            .any(|i| i.contains("debuggable")));
        assert!(info.exported_count >= 1, "indicators: {:?}", info.indicators);
        assert!(info
            .indicators
            .iter()
            .any(|i| i.contains("exported component")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_zip_that_is_not_an_apk() {
        // a plain zip without a manifest
        let err = analyze(&{
            let mut v = vec![0x50, 0x4b, 0x03, 0x04];
            v.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 200]);
            v
        })
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("AndroidManifest") || err.contains("zip"), "{}", err);
    }
}
```

## `crates/bininspect/src/axml.rs`

```rust
//! Android binary XML (`AndroidManifest.xml` inside an APK) parser.
//!
//! Android ships the manifest compiled into a chunked binary format, not text.
//! Structure: file header, a string pool, then a stream of elements with typed
//! attribute values. Reading it properly is the difference between "this is an
//! APK" and "this app declares package X, needs the INTERNET permission, and
//! exports activity Y".

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Attr {
    pub ns: Option<String>,
    pub name: String,
    /// Raw string form when present.
    pub raw: Option<String>,
    /// Decoded typed value as text.
    pub value: String,
    pub type_id: u8,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Element {
    pub name: String,
    pub attributes: Vec<Attr>,
}

impl Element {
    pub fn attr(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&Attr> {
        self.attributes.iter().find(|a| a.name == name)
    }
    pub fn value(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.attr(name).map(|a| a.value.as_str())
    }
}

const RES_STRING_POOL: u16 = 0x0001;
const RES_XML: u16 = 0x0003;
const RES_XML_START_ELEMENT: u16 = 0x0102;

fn u16le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes([*b.get(at)?, *b.get(at + 1)?]))
}
fn u32le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes([
        *b.get(at)?,
        *b.get(at + 1)?,
        *b.get(at + 2)?,
        *b.get(at + 3)?,
    ]))
}

struct Pool {
    strings: Vec<String>,
}

fn read_pool(data: &[u8], at: usize) -> Result<Pool, String> {
    let typ = u16le(data, at).ok_or("pool: truncated")?;
    if typ != RES_STRING_POOL {
        return Err(format!("expected string pool, found chunk type 0x{:04x}", typ));
    }
    let header_size = u16le(data, at + 2).ok_or("pool: truncated")? as usize;
    let count = u32le(data, at + 8).ok_or("pool: truncated")? as usize;
    let flags = u32le(data, at + 16).ok_or("pool: truncated")?;
    let strings_start = u32le(data, at + 20).ok_or("pool: truncated")? as usize;
    let utf8 = flags & 0x100 != 0; // UTF8_FLAG
    let offsets_at = at + header_size;
    let base = at + strings_start;

    let mut strings = Vec::with_capacity(count);
    for i in 0..count {
        let off = u32le(data, offsets_at + i * 4).ok_or("pool: offset table truncated")? as usize;
        let p = base + off;
        if p >= data.len() {
            strings.push(String::new());
            continue;
        }
        if utf8 {
            // u8 utf16 len (with high bit = 2-byte length), then u8 byte len, then bytes
            let (mut q, _) = read_len8(data, p);
            let (mut r, blen) = read_len8(data, q);
            q = r;
            r = q + blen;
            let raw = data.get(q..r.min(data.len())).unwrap_or(&[]);
            strings.push(String::from_utf8_lossy(raw).to_string());
        } else {
            let (q, len16) = read_len16(data, p);
            let start = q;
            let end = start + len16 * 2;
            let raw = data.get(start..end.min(data.len())).unwrap_or(&[]);
            let units: Vec<u16> = raw
                .chunks_exact(2)
                .map(|c| u16::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1]]))
                .collect();
            strings.push(String::from_utf16_lossy(&units));
        }
    }
    Ok(Pool { strings })
}

fn read_len8(data: &[u8], at: usize) -> (usize, usize) {
    let a = data.get(at).copied().unwrap_or(0);
    if a & 0x80 != 0 {
        let b = data.get(at + 1).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        (at + 2, ((a as usize & 0x7f) << 8) | b as usize)
    } else {
        (at + 1, a as usize)
    }
}

fn read_len16(data: &[u8], at: usize) -> (usize, usize) {
    let a = u16le(data, at).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
    if a & 0x8000 != 0 {
        let b = u16le(data, at + 2).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
        (at + 4, ((a & 0x7fff) << 16) | b)
    } else {
        (at + 2, a)
    }
}

fn decode_typed(type_id: u8, data: u32, pool: &Pool) -> String {
    match type_id {
        0x03 => pool.strings.get(data as usize).cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
        0x10 => format!("{}", data as i32),
        0x11 => format!("0x{:x}", data),
        0x12 => {
            if data != 0 {
                "true".into()
            } else {
                "false".into()
            }
        }
        0x01 => format!("@0x{:08x}", data),
        0x04 => format!("{}f", f32::from_bits(data)),
        0x00 => "null".into(),
        _ => format!("0x{:x}", data),
    }
}

/// Parse every element in the document, in order.
pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Element>, String> {
    if data.len() < 8 {
        return Err("axml: file too small".into());
    }
    if u16le(data, 0).ok_or("axml: truncated")? != RES_XML {
        return Err("axml: not a binary XML document (bad magic)".into());
    }
    let total = u32le(data, 4).ok_or("axml: truncated")? as usize;
    let end = total.min(data.len());

    let mut pool: Option<Pool> = None;
    let mut elements = Vec::new();
    let mut p = 8;
    while p + 8 <= end {
        let typ = u16le(data, p).ok_or("axml: truncated chunk")?;
        let header_size = u16le(data, p + 2).ok_or("axml: truncated")? as usize;
        let size = u32le(data, p + 4).ok_or("axml: truncated")? as usize;
        if size < 8 || p + size > data.len() {
            break;
        }
        match typ {
            RES_STRING_POOL => pool = Some(read_pool(data, p)?),
            RES_XML_START_ELEMENT => {
                let Some(ref pool) = pool else {
                    return Err("axml: element before string pool".into());
                };
                let body = p + header_size;
                // ns, name, attributeStart, attributeSize, attributeCount, ...
                let name_idx = u32le(data, body + 4).ok_or("axml: truncated element")? as usize;
                let attr_start = u16le(data, body + 8).ok_or("axml: truncated element")? as usize;
                let attr_size = u16le(data, body + 10).ok_or("axml: truncated element")? as usize;
                let attr_count = u16le(data, body + 12).ok_or("axml: truncated element")? as usize;
                let name = pool
                    .strings
                    .get(name_idx)
                    .cloned()
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("#{}", name_idx));
                let mut attributes = Vec::new();
                for i in 0..attr_count {
                    let a = body + attr_start + i * attr_size.max(20);
                    let ns_idx = u32le(data, a).ok_or("axml: truncated attr")?;
                    let nm_idx = u32le(data, a + 4).ok_or("axml: truncated attr")?;
                    let raw_idx = u32le(data, a + 8).ok_or("axml: truncated attr")?;
                    let type_id = data.get(a + 15).copied().unwrap_or(0);
                    let value_data = u32le(data, a + 16).ok_or("axml: truncated attr")?;
                    let ns = if ns_idx == 0xFFFF_FFFF {
                        None
                    } else {
                        pool.strings.get(ns_idx as usize).cloned()
                    };
                    let raw = if raw_idx == 0xFFFF_FFFF {
                        None
                    } else {
                        pool.strings.get(raw_idx as usize).cloned()
                    };
                    let value = decode_typed(type_id, value_data, pool);
                    attributes.push(Attr {
                        ns,
                        name: pool
                            .strings
                            .get(nm_idx as usize)
                            .cloned()
                            .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("#{}", nm_idx)),
                        raw,
                        value,
                        type_id,
                    });
                }
                elements.push(Element { name, attributes });
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        p += size;
    }
    Ok(elements)
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct ManifestSummary {
    pub package: String,
    pub version_name: String,
    pub version_code: String,
    pub label: String,
    pub permissions: Vec<String>,
    pub activities: Vec<(String, bool)>,
    pub services: Vec<(String, bool)>,
    pub receivers: Vec<(String, bool)>,
    pub providers: Vec<(String, bool)>,
    pub debuggable: bool,
    pub allow_backup: Option<bool>,
    pub uses_cleartext_traffic: Option<bool>,
    pub min_sdk: Option<String>,
    pub target_sdk: Option<String>,
    pub launcher_activity: Option<String>,
    pub exported_count: usize,
}

/// Resolve a component name the way the platform does: `.Foo` is relative to the
/// package, a bare `Foo` is also relative, and a dotted name is already absolute.
pub fn qualify(name: &str, package: &str) -> String {
    if name.is_empty() || package.is_empty() {
        return name.to_string();
    }
    if let Some(rest) = name.strip_prefix('.') {
        format!("{}.{}", package, rest)
    } else if !name.contains('.') {
        format!("{}.{}", package, name)
    } else {
        name.to_string()
    }
}

/// Turn the element stream into the facts an analyst actually wants.
pub fn summarize(elements: &[Element]) -> ManifestSummary {
    let mut s = ManifestSummary::default();
    // kind, explicit exported flag (None = not stated), name, has_intent_filter
    let mut current_component: Option<(String, Option<bool>, String, bool)> = None;

    let flush = |s: &mut ManifestSummary, cur: &mut Option<(String, Option<bool>, String, bool)>| {
        if let Some((kind, explicit, name, has_filter)) = cur.take() {
            // Android's rule: android:exported wins when present; otherwise a component
            // with an intent-filter is exported and one without is not. Providers default
            // to exported on API < 17, but every current platform treats an unstated
            // provider without a filter as non-exported, which is what we report.
            let exported = explicit.unwrap_or(has_filter);
            let name = qualify(&name, &s.package);
            if exported {
                s.exported_count += 1;
            }
            match kind.as_str() {
                "activity" => s.activities.push((name, exported)),
                "service" => s.services.push((name, exported)),
                "receiver" => s.receivers.push((name, exported)),
                "provider" => s.providers.push((name, exported)),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    };

    for el in elements {
        match el.name.as_str() {
            "activity" | "activity-alias" | "service" | "receiver" | "provider" => {
                flush(&mut s, &mut current_component);
                let name = el.value("name").unwrap_or("").to_string();
                let explicit = el.value("exported").map(|v| v == "true");
                let kind = if el.name == "activity-alias" { "activity".to_string() } else { el.name.clone() };
                current_component = Some((kind, explicit, name, false));
            }
            "intent-filter" => {
                if let Some((_, _, _, has_filter)) = current_component.as_mut() {
                    *has_filter = true;
                }
            }
            "action" => {
                if el.value("name") == Some("android.intent.action.MAIN") {
                    if let Some((_, _, name, _)) = &current_component {
                        s.launcher_activity = Some(qualify(name, &s.package));
                    }
                }
            }
            "uses-permission" | "uses-permission-sdk-23" => {
                if let Some(n) = el.value("name") {
                    s.permissions.push(n.to_string());
                }
            }
            "uses-sdk" => {
                if let Some(v) = el.value("minSdkVersion") {
                    s.min_sdk = Some(v.to_string());
                }
                if let Some(v) = el.value("targetSdkVersion") {
                    s.target_sdk = Some(v.to_string());
                }
            }
            "application" => {
                s.debuggable = el.value("debuggable") == Some("true");
                s.allow_backup = el.value("allowBackup").map(|v| v == "true");
                s.uses_cleartext_traffic = el.value("usesCleartextTraffic").map(|v| v == "true");
                if let Some(l) = el.value("label") {
                    if !l.starts_with('@') {
                        s.label = l.to_string();
                    }
                }
            }
            "manifest" => {
                if let Some(v) = el.value("package") {
                    s.package = v.to_string();
                }
                if let Some(v) = el.value("versionName") {
                    s.version_name = v.to_string();
                }
                if let Some(v) = el.value("versionCode") {
                    s.version_code = v.to_string();
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    flush(&mut s, &mut current_component);
    s.permissions.sort();
    s.permissions.dedup();
    s
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn fixture() -> Vec<u8> {
        let p = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
            .join("../../tests/fixtures/apk/AndroidManifest.xml");
        std::fs::read(&p).expect("manifest fixture missing")
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_real_compiled_manifest() {
        let els = parse(&fixture()).expect("parse");
        assert!(els.iter().any(|e| e.name == "manifest"), "elements: {:?}",
            els.iter().map(|e| &e.name).collect::<Vec<_>>());
        let s = summarize(&els);
        assert_eq!(s.package, "com.example.forgetest");
        assert_eq!(s.version_name, "1.2.3");
        assert!(s.permissions.contains(&"android.permission.INTERNET".to_string()));
        assert!(s.activities.iter().any(|(n, _)| n == "com.example.forgetest.MainActivity"));
        assert_eq!(s.target_sdk.as_deref(), Some("34"));
        assert!(s.debuggable, "fixture sets debuggable");
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_non_binary_xml() {
        assert!(parse(b"<?xml version=\"1.0\"?><manifest/>").is_err());
        assert!(parse(b"\x00\x00").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn qualifies_relative_component_names() {
        assert_eq!(qualify(".MainActivity", "com.ex"), "com.ex.MainActivity");
        assert_eq!(qualify("MainActivity", "com.ex"), "com.ex.MainActivity");
        assert_eq!(qualify("com.other.Thing", "com.ex"), "com.other.Thing");
        assert_eq!(qualify("", "com.ex"), "");
    }

    #[test]
    fn exported_defaults_to_whether_an_intent_filter_exists() {
        let els = vec![
            Element { name: "manifest".into(), attributes: vec![attr_for("package", "com.ex")] },
            Element { name: "activity".into(), attributes: vec![attr_for("name", ".Filtered")] },
            Element { name: "intent-filter".into(), attributes: vec![] },
            Element { name: "action".into(), attributes: vec![attr_for("name", "android.intent.action.VIEW")] },
            Element { name: "activity".into(), attributes: vec![attr_for("name", ".Internal")] },
            Element { name: "activity".into(), attributes: vec![attr_for("name", ".Pinned"), attr_for("exported", "false")] },
            Element { name: "intent-filter".into(), attributes: vec![] },
        ];
        let s = summarize(&els);
        let get = |n: &str| s.activities.iter().find(|(x, _)| x == n).map(|(_, e)| *e);
        assert_eq!(get("com.ex.Filtered"), Some(true), "intent-filter implies exported");
        assert_eq!(get("com.ex.Internal"), Some(false), "no filter, no export");
        assert_eq!(get("com.ex.Pinned"), Some(false), "explicit false wins over the filter");
        assert_eq!(s.exported_count, 1);
    }

    fn attr_for(name: &str, value: &str) -> Attr {
        Attr {
            ns: None,
            name: name.to_string(),
            raw: Some(value.to_string()),
            value: value.to_string(),
            type_id: 0x03,
        }
    }
}
```

## `crates/bininspect/src/dex.rs`

```rust
//! Dalvik executable (`classes*.dex`) structural parser.
//!
//! Not a decompiler: it recovers the class/method inventory, the string table and
//! the *references* a class makes (which is what tells you whether an app talks to
//! a network, uses crypto, loads code dynamically, or checks for root).

use std::collections::BTreeSet;

fn u16le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes([*b.get(at)?, *b.get(at + 1)?]))
}
fn u32le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes([
        *b.get(at)?,
        *b.get(at + 1)?,
        *b.get(at + 2)?,
        *b.get(at + 3)?,
    ]))
}

fn uleb128(data: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<(u32, usize)> {
    let mut result: u32 = 0;
    let mut shift = 0;
    let mut p = at;
    loop {
        let byte = *data.get(p)?;
        p += 1;
        result |= ((byte & 0x7f) as u32) << shift;
        if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
            return Some((result, p));
        }
        shift += 7;
        if shift > 28 {
            return None;
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct DexInfo {
    pub file_size: u32,
    pub checksum_ok: Option<bool>,
    pub strings: usize,
    pub types: usize,
    pub methods: usize,
    pub classes: usize,
    pub class_names: Vec<String>,
    pub method_names: Vec<String>,
    pub interesting: Vec<Finding>,
    pub version: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Finding {
    pub category: &'static str,
    pub detail: String,
}

/// MUTF-8 to String (NUL encoded as 0xC0 0x80, surrogate pairs as CESU-8).
fn mutf8_to_string(raw: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < raw.len() {
        let b = raw[i];
        if b == 0 {
            break;
        }
        if b < 0x80 {
            out.push(b as char);
            i += 1;
        } else if b & 0xE0 == 0xC0 {
            if i + 1 >= raw.len() {
                break;
            }
            if b == 0xC0 && raw[i + 1] == 0x80 {
                out.push('\u{0}');
            } else {
                let cp = ((b as u32 & 0x1f) << 6) | (raw[i + 1] as u32 & 0x3f);
                out.push(char::from_u32(cp).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
            }
            i += 2;
        } else if b & 0xF0 == 0xE0 {
            if i + 2 >= raw.len() {
                break;
            }
            let cp = ((b as u32 & 0x0f) << 12)
                | ((raw[i + 1] as u32 & 0x3f) << 6)
                | (raw[i + 2] as u32 & 0x3f);
            out.push(char::from_u32(cp).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
            i += 3;
        } else if b & 0xF8 == 0xF0 {
            if i + 3 >= raw.len() {
                break;
            }
            let cp = ((b as u32 & 0x07) << 18)
                | ((raw[i + 1] as u32 & 0x3f) << 12)
                | ((raw[i + 2] as u32 & 0x3f) << 6)
                | (raw[i + 3] as u32 & 0x3f);
            out.push(char::from_u32(cp).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}'));
            i += 4;
        } else {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

fn read_uleb_string(data: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<String> {
    let (_len, p) = uleb128(data, at)?;
    let mut end = p;
    while *data.get(end)? != 0 {
        end += 1;
    }
    Some(mutf8_to_string(&data[p..end]))
}

const CRYPTO: &[&str] = &[
    "javax/crypto", "java/security", "Cipher", "SecretKey", "AES", "RSA", "DES",
    "MessageDigest", "KeyStore", "KeyGenerator",
];
const NETWORK: &[&str] = &[
    "java/net/Socket", "HttpURLConnection", "okhttp3", "java/net/URL", "retrofit2",
    "WebView", "loadUrl",
];
const DYNAMIC_CODE: &[&str] = &[
    "DexClassLoader", "PathClassLoader", "InMemoryDexClassLoader", "defineClass",
    "java/lang/reflect", "Class/forName", "Runtime/exec", "ProcessBuilder",
];
const ROOT_HINTS: &[&str] = &[
    "/system/xbin/su", "/system/bin/su", "busybox", "Superuser", "magisk", "test-keys",
    "/proc/mounts", "ro.debuggable",
];
const EMULATOR_HINTS: &[&str] = &["goldfish", "generic_x86", "ranchu", "Emulator", "qemu"];

pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<DexInfo, String> {
    if data.len() < 0x70 {
        return Err("dex: file too small".into());
    }
    if &data[0..4] != b"dex\n" {
        return Err("dex: bad magic (not a Dalvik executable)".into());
    }
    let version = String::from_utf8_lossy(&data[4..7]).to_string();
    let file_size = u32le(data, 32).ok_or("dex: truncated header")?;
    let string_ids_size = u32le(data, 56).ok_or("dex: truncated")? as usize;
    let string_ids_off = u32le(data, 60).ok_or("dex: truncated")? as usize;
    let type_ids_size = u32le(data, 64).ok_or("dex: truncated")? as usize;
    let type_ids_off = u32le(data, 68).ok_or("dex: truncated")? as usize;
    let method_ids_size = u32le(data, 88).ok_or("dex: truncated")? as usize;
    let method_ids_off = u32le(data, 92).ok_or("dex: truncated")? as usize;
    let class_defs_size = u32le(data, 96).ok_or("dex: truncated")? as usize;
    let class_defs_off = u32le(data, 100).ok_or("dex: truncated")? as usize;

    // Strings
    let mut strings: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(string_ids_size.min(1 << 20));
    for i in 0..string_ids_size {
        let off = u32le(data, string_ids_off + i * 4)
            .ok_or("dex: string id table truncated")? as usize;
        strings.push(read_uleb_string(data, off).unwrap_or_default());
    }

    // Types -> descriptor strings
    let mut types: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(type_ids_size.min(1 << 20));
    for i in 0..type_ids_size {
        let idx = u32le(data, type_ids_off + i * 4).ok_or("dex: type id table truncated")? as usize;
        types.push(strings.get(idx).cloned().unwrap_or_default());
    }

    // Methods
    let mut method_names: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut method_refs: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();
    for i in 0..method_ids_size {
        let at = method_ids_off + i * 8;
        let class_idx = u16le(data, at).ok_or("dex: method table truncated")? as usize;
        let name_idx = u32le(data, at + 4).ok_or("dex: method table truncated")? as usize;
        let cls = types.get(class_idx).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        let name = strings.get(name_idx).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        method_refs.insert(format!("{}->{}", cls, name));
        method_names.push(name);
    }

    // Classes (through class_data_item for accuracy)
    let mut class_names: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..class_defs_size {
        let at = class_defs_off + i * 32;
        let class_idx = u32le(data, at).ok_or("dex: class defs truncated")? as usize;
        let class_data_off = u32le(data, at + 24).ok_or("dex: class defs truncated")? as usize;
        let desc = types.get(class_idx).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        class_names.push(desc.clone());
        if class_data_off == 0 || class_data_off >= data.len() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut p = class_data_off;
        let Some((sf, np)) = uleb128(data, p) else { continue };
        p = np;
        let Some((inf, np)) = uleb128(data, p) else { continue };
        p = np;
        let Some((dm, np)) = uleb128(data, p) else { continue };
        p = np;
        let Some((vm, _np)) = uleb128(data, p) else { continue };
        // skip fields
        let mut q = p;
        for _ in 0..(sf + inf) {
            let Some((_, n1)) = uleb128(data, q) else { break };
            let Some((_, n2)) = uleb128(data, n1) else { break };
            q = n2;
        }
        for _ in 0..(dm + vm) {
            let Some((_midx, n1)) = uleb128(data, q) else { break };
            let Some((_acc, n2)) = uleb128(data, n1) else { break };
            let Some((_code, n3)) = uleb128(data, n2) else { break };
            q = n3;
        }
    }

    // Findings from the reference graph
    let mut interesting: Vec<Finding> = Vec::new();
    let all_refs = method_refs.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
    let mut add_hits = |cat: &'static str, needles: &[&str], label: &str| {
        let hits: Vec<&str> = needles
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|n| all_refs.contains(n))
            .collect();
        if !hits.is_empty() {
            interesting.push(Finding {
                category: cat,
                detail: format!("{}: {}", label, hits.join(", ")),
            });
        }
    };
    add_hits("crypto", CRYPTO, "crypto APIs referenced");
    add_hits("network", NETWORK, "network APIs referenced");
    add_hits("dynamic_code", DYNAMIC_CODE, "dynamic/reflective code APIs referenced");

    for s in &strings {
        for hint in ROOT_HINTS {
            if s.contains(hint) {
                interesting.push(Finding {
                    category: "root_detection",
                    detail: format!("string looks like a root/emulator check: `{}`", truncate(s, 80)),
                });
            }
        }
        if s.starts_with("http://") && !s.contains("schemas.android.com") && !s.contains("xml.org") {
            interesting.push(Finding {
                category: "cleartext_url",
                detail: format!("hardcoded cleartext URL: `{}`", truncate(s, 120)),
            });
        }
    }
    let _ = EMULATOR_HINTS;

    interesting.sort_by(|a, b| a.category.cmp(b.category).then(a.detail.cmp(&b.detail)));
    interesting.dedup_by(|a, b| a.detail == b.detail);
    interesting.truncate(60);

    Ok(DexInfo {
        file_size,
        checksum_ok: None,
        strings: strings.len(),
        types: types.len(),
        methods: method_ids_size,
        classes: class_defs_size,
        class_names,
        method_names,
        interesting,
        version,
    })
}

fn truncate(s: &str, n: usize) -> String {
    if s.chars().count() <= n {
        s.to_string()
    } else {
        let t: String = s.chars().take(n).collect();
        format!("{}‚Ä¶", t)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn fixture() -> Vec<u8> {
        std::fs::read(
            std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
                .join("../../tests/fixtures/apk/classes.dex"),
        )
        .expect("deck fixture missing")
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_dex_inventory() {
        let d = parse(&fixture()).expect("dex parse");
        assert_eq!(d.version, "035");
        assert!(d.classes >= 3, "classes: {}", d.classes);
        assert!(d.class_names.iter().any(|c| c.contains("MainActivity")));
        assert!(d.strings > 10);
        assert!(d.methods >= 5);
    }

    #[test]
    fn detects_crypto_and_network_references() {
        let d = parse(&fixture()).expect("dex parse");
        let cats: Vec<&str> = d.interesting.iter().map(|f| f.category).collect();
        assert!(cats.contains(&"crypto"), "expected crypto refs, got {:?}", d.interesting);
        assert!(cats.contains(&"network"), "expected network refs, got {:?}", d.interesting);
        assert!(cats.contains(&"cleartext_url"), "expected a cleartext URL finding");
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_non_dex() {
        assert!(parse(b"not a dex file at all").is_err());
        assert!(parse(&[0u8; 200]).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn uleb128_decodes_multibyte() {
        // 0xE5 0x8E 0x26 == 624485
        let d = [0xE5u8, 0x8E, 0x26];
        assert_eq!(uleb128(&d, 0), Some((624485, 3)));
    }
}
```

## `crates/bininspect/src/elf.rs`

```rust
//! Minimal ELF reader ‚Äî enough to identify an architecture, entry point and
//! section layout for `.so` files found inside APKs (or standalone Linux binaries).

fn u16le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes([*b.get(at)?, *b.get(at + 1)?]))
}
fn u32le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes([
        *b.get(at)?,
        *b.get(at + 1)?,
        *b.get(at + 2)?,
        *b.get(at + 3)?,
    ]))
}
fn u64le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u64> {
    let lo = u32le(b, at)? as u64;
    let hi = u32le(b, at + 4)? as u64;
    Some(lo | (hi << 32))
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct ElfInfo {
    pub is_64: bool,
    pub little_endian: bool,
    pub object_type: &'static str,
    pub machine: &'static str,
    pub entry: u64,
    pub sections: Vec<String>,
    /// True when the symbol table is stripped.
    pub stripped: bool,
}

pub fn is_elf(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    data.starts_with(b"\x7fELF")
}

pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<ElfInfo, String> {
    if data.len() < 52 || !is_elf(data) {
        return Err("elf: not an ELF file (or truncated header)".into());
    }
    let class = data[4];
    let is_64 = match class {
        2 => true,
        1 => false,
        _ => return Err("elf: unknown class".into()),
    };
    let little_endian = data[5] == 1;
    if !little_endian {
        return Ok(ElfInfo {
            is_64,
            little_endian,
            object_type: "big-endian ELF (sections not parsed)",
            machine: "unknown",
            entry: 0,
            sections: Vec::new(),
            stripped: false,
        });
    }
    let object_type = match u16le(data, 16).unwrap_or(0) {
        1 => "relocatable",
        2 => "executable",
        3 => "shared object (.so)",
        4 => "core dump",
        _ => "unknown",
    };
    let machine = match u16le(data, 18).unwrap_or(0) {
        0x3e => "x86-64",
        0x03 => "x86",
        0xb7 => "ARM64 (AArch64)",
        0x28 => "ARM",
        0xf3 => "RISC-V",
        0x08 => "MIPS",
        _ => "unknown",
    };
    let entry = if is_64 {
        u64le(data, 24).unwrap_or(0)
    } else {
        u32le(data, 24).unwrap_or(0) as u64
    };

    // section headers
    let (shoff, shentsize, shnum, shstrndx) = if is_64 {
        (
            u64le(data, 0x28).unwrap_or(0) as usize,
            u16le(data, 0x3A).unwrap_or(0) as usize,
            u16le(data, 0x3C).unwrap_or(0) as usize,
            u16le(data, 0x3E).unwrap_or(0) as usize,
        )
    } else {
        (
            u32le(data, 0x20).unwrap_or(0) as usize,
            u16le(data, 0x2E).unwrap_or(0) as usize,
            u16le(data, 0x30).unwrap_or(0) as usize,
            u16le(data, 0x32).unwrap_or(0) as usize,
        )
    };

    let mut sections = Vec::new();
    let mut stripped = true;
    if shoff != 0 && shnum > 0 && shoff < data.len() {
        // string table
        let strtab_off = |idx: usize| -> Option<usize> {
            let at = shoff + idx * shentsize;
            Some(if is_64 {
                u64le(data, at + 0x18)? as usize
            } else {
                u32le(data, at + 0x10)? as usize
            })
        };
        let names_base = strtab_off(shstrndx).unwrap_or(0);
        for i in 0..shnum {
            let at = shoff + i * shentsize;
            let name_off = u32le(data, at).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
            let typ = u32le(data, at + 4).unwrap_or(0);
            let name = {
                let start = names_base + name_off;
                let mut end = start;
                while let Some(&c) = data.get(end) {
                    if c == 0 {
                        break;
                    }
                    end += 1;
                }
                String::from_utf8_lossy(data.get(start..end).unwrap_or(&[])).to_string()
            };
            if typ == 2 || typ == 11 {
                stripped = false; // SYMTAB or DYNSYM
            }
            if !name.is_empty() {
                sections.push(name);
            }
        }
    }
    sections.truncate(60);
    Ok(ElfInfo {
        is_64,
        little_endian,
        object_type,
        machine,
        entry,
        sections,
        stripped,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn identifies_a_real_linux_binary() {
        // /bin/sh is an ELF on this image; skip gracefully if not.
        if let Ok(data) = std::fs::read("/bin/sh") {
            if is_elf(&data) {
                let e = parse(&data).expect("elf");
                assert!(e.is_64);
                assert!(matches!(e.object_type, "executable" | "shared object (.so)"));
                assert!(!e.sections.is_empty());
                return;
            }
        }
        // fallback: header-only synthetic file
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; 64];
        buf[0..4].copy_from_slice(b"\x7fELF");
        buf[4] = 2;
        buf[5] = 1;
        buf[16] = 3;
        buf[18] = 0x3e;
        let e = parse(&buf).expect("elf header");
        assert!(e.is_64);
        assert_eq!(e.machine, "x86-64");
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_non_elf() {
        assert!(parse(b"MZ\x90\x00").is_err());
        assert!(!is_elf(b"PK\x03\x04"));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Structural analysis library for APK, PE and ELF files.
//!
//! Deliberately scoped to *structural* analysis ‚Äî hashing, container inventory,
//! manifest decoding, import/export tables, DEX class inventory, entropy and
//! string extraction. Instruction-level disassembly and decompilation need a real
//! engine (Ghidra/IDA), which is not available here; see docs/BINARY_ANALYSIS.md.

pub mod apk;
pub mod axml;
pub mod dex;
pub mod elf;
/// Re-exported from `forge-core` so there is exactly one hash implementation.
pub use forge_core::hashes;
pub mod report;
pub mod xmltext;
pub mod pe;
```

## `crates/bininspect/src/main.rs`

```rust
//! bininspect ‚Äî structural analysis for APK / EXE / ELF files, with no third-party
//! code and no network.
//!
//! Answers the first questions an analyst asks: what is this, what does it import,
//! is it packed, is it managed code, what components does it expose, what strings
//! and URLs does it carry.
//!
//! Usage:
//!     bininspect <file> [--json] [--strings N]

use bininspect::report::analyze;
use forge_core::json;
use forge_core::json::Value;

fn main() {
    let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1);
    let mut path: Option<String> = None;
    let mut as_json = false;
    let mut string_limit = 40usize;
    while let Some(a) = args.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--json" => as_json = true,
            "--strings" => {
                string_limit = args
                    .next()
                    .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
                    .unwrap_or(40)
            }
            "-h" | "--help" => {
                println!("usage: bininspect <file> [--json] [--strings N]");
                println!("  analyses APK (ZIP+AXML+DEX), PE (EXE/DLL) and ELF files offline");
                return;
            }
            other => path = Some(other.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let Some(path) = path else {
        eprintln!("usage: bininspect <file> [--json] [--strings N]");
        std::process::exit(2);
    };

    let data = match std::fs::read(&path) {
        Ok(d) => d,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("cannot read {}: {}", path, e);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };

    let report = analyze(&path, &data, string_limit);
    if as_json {
        println!("{}", json::to_pretty(&report));
    } else {
        print_human(&path, &data, &report, string_limit);
    }
}

fn section(title: &str) {
    println!("\n== {} ==", title);
}

fn print_human(path: &str, data: &[u8], report: &Value, limit: usize) {
    println!("file      : {}", path);
    println!("size      : {} bytes", data.len());
    println!("sha256    : {}", report.str_of("sha256").unwrap_or(""));
    println!("sha1      : {}", report.str_of("sha1").unwrap_or(""));
    println!("entropy   : {:.2} bits/byte", report.get("entropy").and_then(|e| e.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0));
    println!("format    : {}", report.str_of("format").unwrap_or("unknown"));

    if let Some(err) = report.str_of("error") {
        println!("\nERROR: {}", err);
        return;
    }

    if let Some(p) = report.get("pe") {
        section("PE (Windows executable)");
        println!("arch        : {}-bit {}", p.get("bits").and_then(|b| b.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64, p.str_of("machine").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("subsystem   : {}", p.str_of("subsystem").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("entry point : {}   image base: {}", p.str_of("entry_point_rva").unwrap_or(""), p.str_of("image_base").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("managed     : {}{}", p.get("dotnet").and_then(|d| d.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),
            if p.str_of("dotnet_version").unwrap_or("").is_empty() { String::new() } else { format!(" ({})", p.str_of("dotnet_version").unwrap_or("")) });
        if let Some(secs) = p.get("sections").and_then(|s| s.as_arr()) {
            println!("\n{:<10} {:>10} {:>8}  {:<16} entropy", "section", "vaddr", "size", "flags");
            for s in secs {
                println!(
                    "{:<10} {:>10} {:>8}  {:<16} {:.2}",
                    s.str_of("name").unwrap_or(""),
                    s.str_of("vaddr").unwrap_or(""),
                    s.get("raw_size").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64,
                    s.str_of("flags").unwrap_or(""),
                    s.get("entropy").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0)
                );
            }
        }
        if let Some(imps) = p.get("imports").and_then(|i| i.as_arr()) {
            if !imps.is_empty() {
                section("imports");
                for i in imps {
                    let fns = i.get("functions").and_then(|f| f.as_arr()).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
                    let names: Vec<String> = fns
                        .iter()
                        .take(12)
                        .filter_map(|f| f.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()))
                        .collect();
                    println!("{:<28} {:>3} fn  {}", i.str_of("dll").unwrap_or(""), fns.len(), names.join(", "));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(exps) = p.get("exports").and_then(|e| e.as_arr()) {
            if !exps.is_empty() {
                println!("\nexports: {}", exps.iter().take(20).filter_map(|e| e.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "));
            }
        }
        if let Some(vi) = p.get("version_info").and_then(|v| v.as_arr()) {
            if !vi.is_empty() {
                section("version info");
                for kv in vi {
                    println!("{:<18} {}", kv.str_of("key").unwrap_or(""), kv.str_of("value").unwrap_or(""));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(ind) = p.get("indicators").and_then(|i| i.as_arr()) {
            if !ind.is_empty() {
                section("anomalies / packer signals");
                for i in ind {
                    println!("  ! {}", i.as_str().unwrap_or(""));
                }
            }
        }
        for (label, key) in [("ASCII strings (first {})", "ascii_strings"), ("wide strings (first {})", "wide_strings")] {
            if let Some(list) = p.get(key).and_then(|s| s.as_arr()).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
                section(&label.replace("{}", &limit.min(list.len()).to_string()));
                for x in list.iter().take(limit) {
                    println!("  {}", x.as_str().unwrap_or(""));
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if let Some(a) = report.get("apk") {
        section("APK");
        println!("package     : {}", a.str_of("package").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("version     : {} (code {})", a.str_of("version_name").unwrap_or(""), a.str_of("version_code").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("sdk         : min {} / target {}", a.str_of("min_sdk").unwrap_or("?"), a.str_of("target_sdk").unwrap_or("?"));
        println!("debuggable  : {}", a.get("debuggable").and_then(|d| d.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false));
        println!("allowBackup : {}", a.get("allow_backup").and_then(|d| d.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false));
        println!("cleartext   : {}", a.get("cleartext_traffic").and_then(|d| d.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false));
        println!("dex         : {:?} ‚Äî {} classes, {} methods, {} strings",
            a.get("dex_files").and_then(|d| d.as_arr()).map(|v| v.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string())).collect::<Vec<_>>()).unwrap_or_default(),
            a.get("classes").and_then(|c| c.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64,
            a.get("methods").and_then(|c| c.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64,
            a.get("strings").and_then(|c| c.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64);
        println!("containers  : {} entries, {} bytes uncompressed",
            a.get("entries").and_then(|c| c.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64,
            a.get("uncompressed_bytes").and_then(|c| c.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64);

        if let Some(p) = a.get("permissions").and_then(|p| p.as_arr()) {
            section("permissions");
            for x in p {
                println!("  {}", x.as_str().unwrap_or(""));
            }
        }
        for group in ["activities", "services", "receivers", "providers"] {
            if let Some(list) = a.get(group).and_then(|x| x.as_arr()) {
                if list.is_empty() {
                    continue;
                }
                section(group);
                for c in list {
                    println!(
                        "  {:<55} {}",
                        c.str_of("name").unwrap_or(""),
                        if c.get("exported").and_then(|e| e.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false) { "EXPORTED" } else { "" }
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(n) = a.get("native_libs").and_then(|x| x.as_arr()) {
            if !n.is_empty() {
                section("native libraries");
                for x in n {
                    println!("  {}", x.as_str().unwrap_or(""));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(f) = a.get("code_findings").and_then(|x| x.as_arr()) {
            if !f.is_empty() {
                section("code findings (from the DEX reference graph)");
                for x in f.iter().take(20) {
                    println!("  [{}] {}", x.str_of("category").unwrap_or(""), x.str_of("detail").unwrap_or(""));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(u) = a.get("embedded_urls").and_then(|x| x.as_arr()) {
            if !u.is_empty() {
                section("embedded cleartext URLs");
                for x in u.iter().take(20) {
                    println!("  {}", x.str_of("detail").unwrap_or(""));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(i) = a.get("indicators").and_then(|x| x.as_arr()) {
            if !i.is_empty() {
                section("risk indicators");
                for x in i {
                    println!("  ! {}", x.as_str().unwrap_or(""));
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if let Some(m) = report.get("manifest") {
        let kind = if report.str_of("format") == Some("android_binary_xml") { "compiled" } else { "textual" };
        section(&format!("Android manifest ({})", kind));
        println!("package   : {}", m.str_of("package").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("version   : {} (code {})", m.str_of("version_name").unwrap_or(""), m.str_of("version_code").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("sdk       : min {} / target {}", m.str_of("min_sdk").unwrap_or("?"), m.str_of("target_sdk").unwrap_or("?"));
        println!("debuggable: {}", m.get("debuggable").and_then(|d| d.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false));
        println!("launcher  : {}", m.str_of("launcher_activity").unwrap_or("(none)"));
        if let Some(p) = m.get("permissions").and_then(|p| p.as_arr()).filter(|p| !p.is_empty()) {
            println!("permissions:");
            for x in p { println!("  {}", x.as_str().unwrap_or("")); }
        }
        for group in ["activities", "services", "receivers", "providers"] {
            if let Some(list) = m.get(group).and_then(|x| x.as_arr()).filter(|l| !l.is_empty()) {
                section(group);
                for c in list {
                    println!("  {:<52} {}", c.str_of("name").unwrap_or(""),
                        if c.get("exported").and_then(|e| e.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false) { "EXPORTED" } else { "" });
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if let Some(d) = report.get("dex") {
        section("DEX (Dalvik bytecode, standalone)");
        println!("version   : {}", d.str_of("version").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("declared  : {} bytes (header field)", d.get("declared_size").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64);
        println!("inventory : {} classes, {} methods, {} strings, {} types",
            d.get("classes").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64,
            d.get("methods").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64,
            d.get("strings").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64,
            d.get("types").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64);
        if let Some(f) = d.get("code_findings").and_then(|x| x.as_arr()).filter(|f| !f.is_empty()) {
            section("code findings");
            for x in f.iter().take(20) {
                println!("  [{}] {}", x.str_of("category").unwrap_or(""), x.str_of("detail").unwrap_or(""));
            }
        }
        if let Some(c) = d.get("class_names").and_then(|x| x.as_arr()).filter(|c| !c.is_empty()) {
            section(&format!("application classes ({})", c.len()));
            for x in c.iter().take(20) {
                println!("  {}", x.as_str().unwrap_or(""));
            }
        }
    }

    if let Some(l) = report.get("lfs") {
        section("Git LFS pointer");
        println!("oid   : {}", l.str_of("oid").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("size  : {} bytes (the real binary is not here)", l.get("declared_size").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64);
    }

    if let Some(e) = report.get("elf") {
        section("ELF");
        println!("type    : {}", e.str_of("type").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("machine : {}-bit {}", e.get("bits").and_then(|b| b.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u64, e.str_of("machine").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("entry   : {}", e.str_of("entry").unwrap_or(""));
        println!("stripped: {}", e.get("stripped").and_then(|s| s.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false));
        if let Some(s) = e.get("sections").and_then(|s| s.as_arr()) {
            println!("sections: {}", s.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "));
        }
    }
}
```

## `crates/bininspect/src/pe.rs`

```rust
//! Windows PE/PE32+ analyser: headers, sections, imports, exports, resources,
//! .NET metadata, packer heuristics and string extraction.
//!
//! This is triage, not decompilation: it answers "what is this binary, what DLLs
//! and APIs does it pull in, is it packed, is it managed code, what does it say".
//! Instruction-level analysis needs a disassembler (see docs/BINARY_ANALYSIS.md).

use crate::hashes::{entropy, strings_of, wide_strings_of};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

fn u16le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u16> {
    Some(u16::from_le_bytes([*b.get(at)?, *b.get(at + 1)?]))
}
fn u32le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u32> {
    Some(u32::from_le_bytes([
        *b.get(at)?,
        *b.get(at + 1)?,
        *b.get(at + 2)?,
        *b.get(at + 3)?,
    ]))
}
fn u64le(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> Option<u64> {
    let lo = u32le(b, at)? as u64;
    let hi = u32le(b, at + 4)? as u64;
    Some(lo | (hi << 32))
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Section {
    pub name: String,
    pub virtual_address: u32,
    pub virtual_size: u32,
    pub raw_size: u32,
    pub raw_pointer: u32,
    pub characteristics: u32,
    pub entropy: f64,
}

impl Section {
    pub fn flags(&self) -> String {
        let mut f = Vec::new();
        if self.characteristics & 0x2000_0000 != 0 {
            f.push("exec");
        }
        if self.characteristics & 0x4000_0000 != 0 {
            f.push("read");
        }
        if self.characteristics & 0x8000_0000 != 0 {
            f.push("write");
        }
        if self.characteristics & 0x0000_0020 != 0 {
            f.push("code");
        }
        if self.characteristics & 0x0000_0040 != 0 {
            f.push("idata");
        }
        f.join("|")
    }
    pub fn is_executable(&self) -> bool {
        self.characteristics & 0x2000_0000 != 0
    }
    pub fn is_writable(&self) -> bool {
        self.characteristics & 0x8000_0000 != 0
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct PeInfo {
    pub is_64: bool,
    pub machine: u16,
    pub timestamp: u32,
    pub subsystem: u16,
    pub entry_point_rva: u32,
    pub image_base: u64,
    pub sections: Vec<Section>,
    pub imports: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    pub exports: Vec<String>,
    pub has_resources: bool,
    pub is_dotnet: bool,
    pub dotnet_version: String,
    pub dotnet_strings: Vec<String>,
    pub version_info: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub indicators: Vec<String>,
    pub ascii_strings: Vec<String>,
    pub wide_strings: Vec<String>,
    pub overlay_size: usize,
}

fn rva_to_offset(sections: &[Section], rva: u32) -> Option<usize> {
    for s in sections {
        let start = s.virtual_address;
        let end = start.saturating_add(s.virtual_size.max(s.raw_size));
        if rva >= start && rva < end {
            let delta = rva - start;
            if delta < s.raw_size {
                return Some((s.raw_pointer + delta) as usize);
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

fn cstr(data: &[u8], at: usize, max: usize) -> String {
    let end = data
        .get(at..at.saturating_add(max))
        .and_then(|s| s.iter().position(|&b| b == 0).map(|p| at + p))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| (at + max).min(data.len()));
    if at >= end {
        return String::new();
    }
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&data[at..end]).to_string()
}

/// Quick check: does this look like a PE image (DOS header + `PE\0\0` signature)?
pub fn is_pe(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    if data.len() < 0x40 || &data[0..2] != b"MZ" {
        return false;
    }
    let e_lfanew = u32::from_le_bytes([data[0x3C], data[0x3D], data[0x3E], data[0x3F]]) as usize;
    data.len() > e_lfanew + 4 && &data[e_lfanew..e_lfanew + 4] == b"PE\x00\x00"
}

pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<PeInfo, String> {
    if data.len() < 0x40 || &data[0..2] != b"MZ" {
        return Err("pe: not an MZ/DOS executable".into());
    }
    let e_lfanew = u32le(data, 0x3C).ok_or("pe: truncated DOS header")? as usize;
    if data.get(e_lfanew..e_lfanew + 4) != Some(b"PE\x00\x00") {
        return Err("pe: PE signature missing (DOS stub or not a PE file)".into());
    }
    let coff = e_lfanew + 4;
    let machine = u16le(data, coff).ok_or("pe: truncated COFF header")?;
    let num_sections = u16le(data, coff + 2).ok_or("pe: truncated")? as usize;
    let timestamp = u32le(data, coff + 4).ok_or("pe: truncated")?;
    let size_opt = u16le(data, coff + 16).ok_or("pe: truncated")? as usize;

    let opt = coff + 20;
    let magic = u16le(data, opt).ok_or("pe: truncated optional header")?;
    let is_64 = magic == 0x20B;
    if magic != 0x20B && magic != 0x10B {
        return Err(format!("pe: unknown optional header magic 0x{:x}", magic));
    }
    let entry_point_rva = u32le(data, opt + 16).ok_or("pe: truncated")?;
    let image_base = if is_64 {
        u64le(data, opt + 24).ok_or("pe: truncated")?
    } else {
        u32le(data, opt + 28).ok_or("pe: truncated")? as u64
    };
    let subsystem = u16le(data, opt + 68).ok_or("pe: truncated")?;
    let num_dirs = u32le(data, opt + if is_64 { 108 } else { 92 }).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
    let dirs_at = opt + if is_64 { 112 } else { 96 };

    let mut sections = Vec::new();
    let sec_at = opt + size_opt;
    for i in 0..num_sections {
        let at = sec_at + i * 40;
        let name_raw = data.get(at..at + 8).ok_or("pe: truncated section table")?;
        let name = String::from_utf8_lossy(name_raw)
            .trim_end_matches('\0')
            .to_string();
        let virtual_size = u32le(data, at + 8).ok_or("pe: truncated")?;
        let virtual_address = u32le(data, at + 12).ok_or("pe: truncated")?;
        let raw_size = u32le(data, at + 16).ok_or("pe: truncated")?;
        let raw_pointer = u32le(data, at + 20).ok_or("pe: truncated")?;
        let characteristics = u32le(data, at + 36).ok_or("pe: truncated")?;
        let body = data
            .get(raw_pointer as usize..(raw_pointer as usize + raw_size as usize).min(data.len()))
            .unwrap_or(&[]);
        sections.push(Section {
            name,
            virtual_address,
            virtual_size,
            raw_size,
            raw_pointer,
            characteristics,
            entropy: entropy(body),
        });
    }

    let dir = |idx: usize| -> (u32, u32) {
        if idx >= num_dirs {
            return (0, 0);
        }
        let at = dirs_at + idx * 8;
        (
            u32le(data, at).unwrap_or(0),
            u32le(data, at + 4).unwrap_or(0),
        )
    };

    // ---- imports
    let mut imports: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> = BTreeMap::new();
    let (imp_rva, _imp_size) = dir(1);
    if imp_rva != 0 {
        if let Some(mut off) = rva_to_offset(&sections, imp_rva) {
            for _ in 0..512 {
                let name_rva = u32le(data, off + 12).unwrap_or(0);
                if name_rva == 0 {
                    break;
                }
                let dll = rva_to_offset(&sections, name_rva)
                    .map(|o| cstr(data, o, 128))
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                let thunk_rva = {
                    let oft = u32le(data, off).unwrap_or(0);
                    if oft != 0 {
                        oft
                    } else {
                        u32le(data, off + 16).unwrap_or(0)
                    }
                };
                let mut funcs = Vec::new();
                if let Some(mut t) = rva_to_offset(&sections, thunk_rva) {
                    for _ in 0..1024 {
                        let entry = if is_64 {
                            u64le(data, t).unwrap_or(0)
                        } else {
                            u32le(data, t).unwrap_or(0) as u64
                        };
                        if entry == 0 {
                            break;
                        }
                        let step = if is_64 { 8 } else { 4 };
                        let is_ordinal = if is_64 {
                            entry & (1u64 << 63) != 0
                        } else {
                            entry & (1u64 << 31) != 0
                        };
                        if is_ordinal {
                            funcs.push(format!("#{}", entry & 0xffff));
                        } else if let Some(no) = rva_to_offset(&sections, entry as u32) {
                            funcs.push(cstr(data, no + 2, 128));
                        }
                        t += step;
                    }
                }
                if !dll.is_empty() {
                    imports.insert(dll, funcs);
                }
                off += 20;
            }
        }
    }

    // ---- exports
    let mut exports = Vec::new();
    let (exp_rva, _) = dir(0);
    if exp_rva != 0 {
        if let Some(off) = rva_to_offset(&sections, exp_rva) {
            let num_names = u32le(data, off + 24).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
            let names_rva = u32le(data, off + 32).unwrap_or(0);
            if let Some(mut np) = rva_to_offset(&sections, names_rva) {
                for _ in 0..num_names.min(2000) {
                    let r = u32le(data, np).unwrap_or(0);
                    if let Some(o) = rva_to_offset(&sections, r) {
                        exports.push(cstr(data, o, 256));
                    }
                    np += 4;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // ---- .NET / CLR
    let (clr_rva, clr_size) = dir(14);
    let mut is_dotnet = false;
    let mut dotnet_version = String::new();
    let mut dotnet_strings = Vec::new();
    if clr_rva != 0 && clr_size != 0 {
        if let Some(off) = rva_to_offset(&sections, clr_rva) {
            let md_rva = u32le(data, off + 8).unwrap_or(0);
            if let Some(md) = rva_to_offset(&sections, md_rva) {
                if data.get(md..md + 4) == Some(&b"BSJB"[..]) {
                    is_dotnet = true;
                    let ver_len = u32le(data, md + 12).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
                    dotnet_version = cstr(data, md + 16, ver_len.min(64));
                    // walk streams
                    let mut p = md + 16 + ((ver_len + 3) & !3);
                    let count = u16le(data, p + 2).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
                    p += 4;
                    for _ in 0..count {
                        let s_off = u32le(data, p).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
                        let s_size = u32le(data, p + 4).unwrap_or(0) as usize;
                        let name = cstr(data, p + 8, 32);
                        p += 8 + ((name.len() + 1 + 3) & !3);
                        if name == "#Strings" || name == "#US" {
                            let body = data
                                .get(md + s_off..(md + s_off + s_size).min(data.len()))
                                .unwrap_or(&[]);
                            dotnet_strings.extend(strings_of(body, 4));
                        }
                    }
                    dotnet_strings.truncate(400);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    let (res_rva, _) = dir(2);
    let has_resources = res_rva != 0;

    // ---- strings
    let mut ascii_strings = strings_of(data, 6);
    let mut wide_strings = wide_strings_of(data, 6);
    ascii_strings.truncate(4000);
    wide_strings.truncate(4000);

    // ---- version info (VS_VERSIONINFO in .rsrc, UTF-16 key/value strings)
    let mut version_info = Vec::new();
    let interesting_keys = [
        "CompanyName", "FileDescription", "FileVersion", "InternalName", "LegalCopyright",
        "OriginalFilename", "ProductName", "ProductVersion",
    ];
    for (i, s) in wide_strings.iter().enumerate() {
        if interesting_keys.contains(&s.as_str()) {
            if let Some(v) = wide_strings.get(i + 1) {
                version_info.push((s.clone(), v.clone()));
            }
        }
    }
    version_info.dedup();

    // ---- indicators
    let mut indicators = Vec::new();
    let total_raw: u32 = sections.iter().map(|s| s.raw_size).sum();
    let end_of_sections = sections
        .iter()
        .map(|s| s.raw_pointer + s.raw_size)
        .max()
        .unwrap_or(0) as usize;
    let overlay_size = data.len().saturating_sub(end_of_sections);

    if let Some(upx) = sections.iter().find(|s| s.name.starts_with("UPX")) {
        indicators.push(format!("UPX packer signature in section `{}`", upx.name));
    }
    let high_entropy: Vec<&str> = sections
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| s.raw_size > 512 && s.entropy > 7.2)
        .map(|s| s.name.as_str())
        .collect();
    if !high_entropy.is_empty() {
        indicators.push(format!(
            "high-entropy section(s) {} (>7.2 bits/byte): packed or encrypted payload",
            high_entropy.join(", ")
        ));
    }
    let import_count: usize = imports.values().map(|v| v.len()).sum();
    if import_count > 0 && import_count < 10 && sections.len() <= 3 {
        indicators.push(format!(
            "very small import table ({} functions) with {} sections: typical of a packer stub",
            import_count,
            sections.len()
        ));
    }
    if import_count == 0 {
        indicators.push("no import table at all: unusual for a normal executable".into());
    }
    if let Some(ep_sec) = sections
        .iter()
        .find(|s| entry_point_rva >= s.virtual_address && entry_point_rva < s.virtual_address + s.virtual_size.max(s.raw_size))
    {
        if ep_sec.is_writable() && ep_sec.is_executable() {
            indicators.push(format!(
                "entry point is in a writable+executable section `{}` (common in packers)",
                ep_sec.name
            ));
        }
        let last = sections.last().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
        if ep_sec.name == last && sections.len() > 3 {
            indicators.push(format!("entry point is in the last section `{}`", ep_sec.name));
        }
    }
    if let Some(wx) = sections.iter().find(|s| s.is_writable() && s.is_executable()) {
        indicators.push(format!("W+X section `{}` present", wx.name));
    }
    if is_dotnet {
        indicators.push(".NET assembly: managed code (IL can be read with a metadata viewer)".into());
    }
    if overlay_size > 4096 {
        indicators.push(format!(
            "{} bytes of overlay data after the last section (installer or appended payload)",
            overlay_size
        ));
    }
    if total_raw == 0 {
        indicators.push("no raw section data: header-only or fragmented file".into());
    }
    for s in &sections {
        for needle in ["This program cannot be run in DOS mode", ""] {
            let _ = needle;
        }
        let _ = s;
    }

    Ok(PeInfo {
        is_64,
        machine,
        timestamp,
        subsystem,
        entry_point_rva,
        image_base,
        sections,
        imports,
        exports,
        has_resources,
        is_dotnet,
        dotnet_version,
        dotnet_strings,
        version_info,
        indicators,
        ascii_strings,
        wide_strings,
        overlay_size,
    })
}

pub fn machine_name(m: u16) -> &'static str {
    match m {
        0x014c => "x86 (i386)",
        0x8664 => "x86-64",
        0xaa64 => "ARM64",
        0x01c0 => "ARM",
        0x01c4 => "ARMv7 (Thumb-2)",
        0x0200 => "IA64",
        _ => "unknown",
    }
}

pub fn subsystem_name(s: u16) -> &'static str {
    match s {
        1 => "native (driver)",
        2 => "Windows GUI",
        3 => "Windows console",
        5 => "OS/2 console",
        7 => "POSIX console",
        9 => "Windows CE",
        10 => "EFI application",
        16 => "Windows boot",
        _ => "unknown",
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn fixture() -> Vec<u8> {
        std::fs::read(
            std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../tests/fixtures/sample.exe"),
        )
        .expect("exe fixture missing")
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_headers_and_sections() {
        let p = parse(&fixture()).expect("pe parse");
        assert!(p.is_64, "fixture is PE32+");
        assert_eq!(machine_name(p.machine), "x86-64");
        assert_eq!(p.sections.len(), 4);
        assert_eq!(p.sections[0].name, ".text");
        assert!(p.sections[0].is_executable());
        assert!(p.sections[2].is_writable());
        let evil = p.sections.iter().find(|s| s.name == ".evil").expect(".evil section");
        assert!(evil.is_executable() && evil.is_writable(), "fixture W+X section");
        assert!(evil.entropy > 7.2, "fixture high-entropy payload: {}", evil.entropy);
        assert_eq!(subsystem_name(p.subsystem), "Windows console");
        assert_eq!(p.image_base, 0x140000000);
    }

    #[test]
    fn extracts_imports() {
        let p = parse(&fixture()).expect("pe parse");
        let total: usize = p.imports.values().map(|v| v.len()).sum();
        assert!(total > 0, "expected an import table, got {:?}", p.imports);
    }

    #[test]
    fn extracts_strings_and_flags_suspicious_sections() {
        let p = parse(&fixture()).expect("pe parse");
        assert!(p.ascii_strings.iter().any(|s| s.contains("CreateFileW") || s.contains("kernel32")));
        // the .data fixture is a repeating pattern -> high entropy in a W+X section
        assert!(p.indicators.iter().any(|i| i.contains("entropy") || i.contains("W+X")),
            "indicators: {:?}", p.indicators);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_non_pe() {
        assert!(parse(b"MZ").is_err());
        assert!(parse(b"not an exe").is_err());
        assert!(parse(&[0u8; 300]).is_err());
    }
}
```
