## `crates/bininspect/src/report.rs`

```rust
//! Unified report: format detection + per-format analysis, emitted as JSON.
//!
//! Lives in the library (not the binary) so the HTTP server can call it directly.

use crate::{apk, axml, elf, hashes, pe, xmltext};
use forge_core::json::Value;
use forge_core::obj;
use std::path::Path;

/// Detect and analyse. Returns a JSON report in every case, including failure.
pub fn analyze(path: &str, data: &[u8], string_limit: usize) -> Value {
    let sha256 = hashes::sha256(data);
    let sha1 = hashes::sha1(data);
    let name = Path::new(path)
        .file_name()
        .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().to_string())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| path.to_string());

    let mut base = obj! {
        "file" => name.as_str(),
        "bytes" => data.len() as u64,
        "sha256" => sha256.as_str(),
        "sha1" => sha1.as_str(),
        "entropy" => (hashes::entropy(data) * 1000.0).round() / 1000.0,
    };

    // Git LFS pointers are 130-byte text stubs, not binaries. Saying so beats
    // reporting "unknown" and letting someone think they analysed the file.
    if let Some(lfs) = lfs_pointer(data) {
        set(&mut base, "format", Value::from("git_lfs_pointer"));
        set(&mut base, "lfs", obj! {
            "oid" => lfs.0.as_str(),
            "declared_size" => lfs.1 as u64,
            "note" => "this file is a Git LFS pointer; the real binary was never downloaded",
        });
        return base;
    }

    let format;
    if is_binary_xml(data) || xmltext::is_text_manifest(data) {
        // A manifest on its own, compiled (AXML) or textual (build intermediates).
        format = if is_binary_xml(data) { "android_binary_xml" } else { "android_text_manifest" };
        let parsed = if is_binary_xml(data) {
            axml::parse(data)
        } else {
            xmltext::parse(data)
        };
        match parsed.map(|els| axml::summarize(&els)) {
            Ok(m) => {
                let comp = |list: &Vec<(String, bool)>| -> Value {
                    Value::Arr(list.iter().map(|(n, e)| obj! { "name" => n.as_str(), "exported" => *e }).collect())
                };
                set(&mut base, "manifest", obj! {
                    "package" => m.package.as_str(),
                    "version_name" => m.version_name.as_str(),
                    "version_code" => m.version_code.as_str(),
                    "min_sdk" => m.min_sdk.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
                    "target_sdk" => m.target_sdk.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
                    "debuggable" => m.debuggable,
                    "exported_components" => m.exported_count as u64,
                    "permissions" => Value::Arr(m.permissions.iter().map(|p| Value::from(p.as_str())).collect()),
                    "activities" => comp(&m.activities),
                    "services" => comp(&m.services),
                    "receivers" => comp(&m.receivers),
                    "providers" => comp(&m.providers),
                    "launcher_activity" => m.launcher_activity.unwrap_or_default(),
                });
            }
            Err(e) => set(&mut base, "error", Value::from(e)),
        }
    } else if data.starts_with(b"dex\n") {
        // A bare classes.dex, e.g. extracted from an APK.
        format = "dex";
        match crate::dex::parse(data) {
            Ok(d) => {
                let mut findings: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
                for f in &d.interesting {
                    findings.push(obj! { "category" => f.category, "detail" => f.detail.as_str() });
                }
                set(&mut base, "dex", obj! {
                    "version" => d.version.as_str(),
                    "declared_size" => d.file_size as u64,
                    "strings" => d.strings as u64,
                    "types" => d.types as u64,
                    "methods" => d.methods as u64,
                    "classes" => d.classes as u64,
                    "class_names" => Value::Arr(d.class_names.iter().take(200).map(|c| Value::from(c.as_str())).collect()),
                    "code_findings" => Value::Arr(findings),
                });
            }
            Err(e) => set(&mut base, "error", Value::from(e)),
        }
    } else if pe::parse(data).is_ok() || data.starts_with(b"MZ") {
        format = "pe";
        match pe::parse(data) {
            Ok(p) => {
                let mut imports: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
                for (dll, funcs) in &p.imports {
                    imports.push(obj! {
                        "dll" => dll.as_str(),
                        "functions" => Value::Arr(funcs.iter().map(|f| Value::from(f.as_str())).collect()),
                    });
                }
                let mut secs: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
                for s in &p.sections {
                    secs.push(obj! {
                        "name" => s.name.as_str(),
                        "vaddr" => format!("0x{:x}", s.virtual_address),
                        "raw_size" => s.raw_size as u64,
                        "flags" => s.flags(),
                        "entropy" => (s.entropy * 100.0).round() / 100.0,
                    });
                }
                let mut vers: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
                for (k, v) in &p.version_info {
                    vers.push(obj! { "key" => k.as_str(), "value" => v.as_str() });
                }
                set(&mut base, "pe", obj! {
                    "bits" => if p.is_64 { 64u64 } else { 32u64 },
                    "machine" => pe::machine_name(p.machine),
                    "subsystem" => pe::subsystem_name(p.subsystem),
                    "entry_point_rva" => format!("0x{:x}", p.entry_point_rva),
                    "image_base" => format!("0x{:x}", p.image_base),
                    "sections" => Value::Arr(secs),
                    "imports" => Value::Arr(imports),
                    "exports" => Value::Arr(p.exports.iter().map(|e| Value::from(e.as_str())).collect()),
                    "dotnet" => p.is_dotnet,
                    "dotnet_version" => p.dotnet_version.as_str(),
                    "has_resources" => p.has_resources,
                    "overlay_bytes" => p.overlay_size as u64,
                    "version_info" => Value::Arr(vers),
                    "indicators" => Value::Arr(p.indicators.iter().map(|i| Value::from(i.as_str())).collect()),
                    "ascii_strings" => Value::Arr(p.ascii_strings.iter().take(string_limit).map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
                    "wide_strings" => Value::Arr(p.wide_strings.iter().take(string_limit).map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
                });
            }
            Err(e) => set(&mut base, "error", Value::from(e)),
        }
    } else if apk::is_zip(data) {
        format = "apk_or_zip";
        match apk::analyze(data) {
            Ok(a) => {
                let mut perms: Vec<Value> = a.permissions.iter().map(|p| Value::from(p.as_str())).collect();
                perms.sort_by_key(|v| v.as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string());
                let comp = |list: &Vec<(String, bool)>| -> Value {
                    Value::Arr(
                        list.iter()
                            .map(|(n, e)| obj! { "name" => n.as_str(), "exported" => *e })
                            .collect(),
                    )
                };
                let mut findings: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
                for f in &a.findings {
                    findings.push(obj! { "category" => f.category, "detail" => f.detail.as_str() });
                }
                let mut largest: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
                for (n, sz, ent) in &a.largest {
                    largest.push(obj! {
                        "entry" => n.as_str(),
                        "bytes" => *sz,
                        "entropy" => (ent * 100.0).round() / 100.0,
                    });
                }
                let mut sigs: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
                for (n, d) in &a.signature_files {
                    sigs.push(obj! { "file" => n.as_str(), "detail" => d.as_str() });
                }
                set(&mut base, "apk", obj! {
                    "package" => a.package.as_str(),
                    "version_name" => a.version_name.as_str(),
                    "version_code" => a.version_code.as_str(),
                    "min_sdk" => a.min_sdk.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
                    "target_sdk" => a.target_sdk.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
                    "debuggable" => a.debuggable,
                    "allow_backup" => a.allow_backup.unwrap_or(false),
                    "cleartext_traffic" => a.cleartext_allowed.unwrap_or(false),
                    "permissions" => Value::Arr(perms),
                    "activities" => comp(&a.activities),
                    "services" => comp(&a.services),
                    "receivers" => comp(&a.receivers),
                    "providers" => comp(&a.providers),
                    "exported_components" => a.exported_count as u64,
                    "dex_files" => Value::Arr(a.dex_files.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
                    "classes" => a.class_count as u64,
                    "methods" => a.method_count as u64,
                    "strings" => a.string_count as u64,
                    "class_names" => Value::Arr(a.classes.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
                    "native_libs" => Value::Arr(a.native_libs.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
                    "abis" => Value::Arr(a.abis.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
                    "entries" => a.entry_count as u64,
                    "uncompressed_bytes" => a.uncompressed_bytes,
                    "largest_entries" => Value::Arr(largest),
                    "signatures" => Value::Arr(sigs),
                    "assets" => Value::Arr(a.assets.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
                    "code_findings" => Value::Arr(findings),
                    "indicators" => Value::Arr(a.indicators.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
                    "embedded_urls" => Value::Arr(a.embedded_urls.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
                });
            }
            Err(e) => set(&mut base, "error", Value::from(e)),
        }
    } else if elf::is_elf(data) {
        format = "elf";
        match elf::parse(data) {
            Ok(e) => set(&mut base, "elf", obj! {
                "bits" => if e.is_64 { 64u64 } else { 32u64 },
                "machine" => e.machine,
                "type" => e.object_type,
                "entry" => format!("0x{:x}", e.entry),
                "stripped" => e.stripped,
                "sections" => Value::Arr(e.sections.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect()),
            }),
            Err(err) => set(&mut base, "error", Value::from(err)),
        }
    } else {
        format = "unknown";
    }
    set(&mut base, "format", Value::from(format));
    base
}

/// Parse a Git LFS pointer: `oid sha256:...\nsize N\n`. Returns (oid, size).
pub fn lfs_pointer(data: &[u8]) -> Option<(String, u64)> {
    if data.len() > 1024 || !data.starts_with(b"version https://git-lfs") {
        return None;
    }
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(data);
    let mut oid = String::new();
    let mut size = 0u64;
    for line in text.lines() {
        if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix("oid ") {
            oid = v.trim().to_string();
        } else if let Some(v) = line.strip_prefix("size ") {
            size = v.trim().parse().unwrap_or(0);
        }
    }
    if oid.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some((oid, size))
    }
}

/// Android binary XML starts with a `RES_XML` chunk header (type 0x0003, size 8).
pub fn is_binary_xml(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    data.len() > 8 && data[0] == 0x03 && data[1] == 0x00 && data[2] == 0x08 && data[3] == 0x00
}

fn set(v: &mut Value, key: &str, value: Value) {
    if let Value::Obj(ref mut m) = v {
        m.insert(key.to_string(), value);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn detects_a_bare_dex_file() {
        let data = std::fs::read(
            std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../tests/fixtures/apk/classes.dex"),
        )
        .expect("dex fixture");
        let r = analyze("classes.dex", &data, 20);
        assert_eq!(r.str_of("format"), Some("dex"));
        assert_eq!(r.get("dex").and_then(|d| d.str_of("version")), Some("035"));
        assert!(r.get("dex").and_then(|d| d.get("classes")).and_then(|c| c.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) >= 3.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn recognises_a_git_lfs_pointer() {
        let stub = b"version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1\noid sha256:ce06c531ab5beebfd915ea74a7c08956340861946c8a104993ba633f2cbcfd54\nsize 6656\n";
        let r = analyze("tool.exe", stub, 20);
        assert_eq!(r.str_of("format"), Some("git_lfs_pointer"));
        assert_eq!(r.get("lfs").and_then(|l| l.get("declared_size")).and_then(|s| s.as_f64()), Some(6656.0));
        assert!(r.get("lfs").and_then(|l| l.str_of("note")).unwrap_or("").contains("LFS"));
    }

    #[test]

        assert_eq!(r.str_of("format"), Some("pe"));
        assert!(r.str_of("error").is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn detects_a_standalone_binary_manifest() {
        let data = std::fs::read(
            std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../tests/fixtures/apk/AndroidManifest.xml"),
        )
        .expect("manifest fixture");
        assert!(is_binary_xml(&data));
        let r = analyze("AndroidManifest.xml", &data, 20);
        assert_eq!(r.str_of("format"), Some("android_binary_xml"));
        let m = r.get("manifest").expect("manifest section");
        assert_eq!(m.str_of("package"), Some("com.example.forgetest"));
        assert_eq!(m.str_of("launcher_activity"), Some("com.example.forgetest.MainActivity"));
        assert!(m.get("exported_components").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) >= 1.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_file_is_unknown_not_a_crash() {
        let r = analyze("empty.bin", b"", 20);
        assert_eq!(r.str_of("format"), Some("unknown"));
        assert_eq!(r.get("bytes").and_then(|b| b.as_f64()), Some(0.0));
    }
}
```

## `crates/bininspect/src/xmltext.rs`

```rust
//! Plain-text Android manifest support.
//!
//! Build intermediates (`merged_manifest/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`) ship the manifest as
//! ordinary XML rather than compiled AXML. Rather than write a second summariser, this
//! converts text XML into the same `axml::Element` stream so both paths share one set of
//! semantics (package qualification, exported defaults, permissions, launcher detection).

use crate::axml::{Attr, Element};

/// Cheap sniff: does this look like a text XML manifest?
pub fn is_text_manifest(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let head = &data[..data.len().min(512)];
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(head);
    let t = text.trim_start_matches('\u{feff}').trim_start();
    t.starts_with("<?xml") || t.starts_with("<manifest")
}

fn decode_entities(s: &str) -> String {
    s.replace("&amp;", "&")
        .replace("&lt;", "<")
        .replace("&gt;", ">")
        .replace("&quot;", "\"")
        .replace("&apos;", "'")
}

/// Scan text XML into elements. Deliberately minimal: tags and attributes only ‚Äî no
/// namespace resolution, no text nodes, no validation. Comments, CDATA, processing
/// instructions and doctypes are skipped.
pub fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Element>, String> {
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(data);
    let b = text.as_bytes();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0usize;

    while i < b.len() {
        if b[i] != b'<' {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        // skip comments / CDATA / declarations
        if text[i..].starts_with("<!--") {
            match text[i..].find("-->") {
                Some(p) => {
                    i += p + 3;
                    continue;
                }
                None => break,
            }
        }
        if text[i..].starts_with("<![CDATA[") {
            match text[i..].find("]]>") {
                Some(p) => {
                    i += p + 3;
                    continue;
                }
                None => break,
            }
        }
        if text[i..].starts_with("<?") || text[i..].starts_with("<!") {
            match text[i..].find('>') {
                Some(p) => {
                    i += p + 1;
                    continue;
                }
                None => break,
            }
        }
        if text[i..].starts_with("</") {
            match text[i..].find('>') {
                Some(p) => {
                    i += p + 1;
                    continue;
                }
                None => break,
            }
        }

        // opening tag: read the name
        i += 1;
        let start = i;
        while i < b.len() && !b[i].is_ascii_whitespace() && b[i] != b'>' && b[i] != b'/' {
            i += 1;
        }
        let name = text[start..i].to_string();
        if name.is_empty() {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }

        // attributes until '>' (respecting quoted values)
        let mut attributes = Vec::new();
        loop {
            while i < b.len() && b[i].is_ascii_whitespace() {
                i += 1;
            }
            if i >= b.len() || b[i] == b'>' {
                i += 1;
                break;
            }
            if b[i] == b'/' {
                i += 1;
                continue;
            }
            let astart = i;
            while i < b.len() && b[i] != b'=' && !b[i].is_ascii_whitespace() && b[i] != b'>' && b[i] != b'/' {
                i += 1;
            }
            let full = text[astart..i].to_string();
            if full.is_empty() {
                i += 1;
                continue;
            }
            while i < b.len() && b[i].is_ascii_whitespace() {
                i += 1;
            }
            let mut value = String::new();
            if i < b.len() && b[i] == b'=' {
                i += 1;
                while i < b.len() && b[i].is_ascii_whitespace() {
                    i += 1;
                }
                if i < b.len() && (b[i] == b'"' || b[i] == b'\'') {
                    let quote = b[i];
                    i += 1;
                    let vstart = i;
                    while i < b.len() && b[i] != quote {
                        i += 1;
                    }
                    value = decode_entities(&text[vstart..i]);
                    i += 1;
                }
            }
            let (ns, local) = match full.rsplit_once(':') {
                Some((ns, local)) => (Some(ns.to_string()), local.to_string()),
                None => (None, full),
            };
            attributes.push(Attr {
                ns,
                name: local,
                raw: Some(value.clone()),
                value,
                type_id: 0x03,
            });
        }
        out.push(Element { name, attributes });
    }

    if out.is_empty() {
        Err("text manifest: no elements found".into())
    } else {
        Ok(out)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::axml;

    const SAMPLE: &str = r#"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    package="com.example.text" android:versionName="2.0" android:versionCode="7">
  <!-- a comment <activity android:name=".Nope"/> -->
  <uses-sdk android:minSdkVersion="21" android:targetSdkVersion="33"/>
  <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/>
  <application android:debuggable="true">
    <activity android:name=".Main" android:exported="true">
      <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.MAIN"/>
      </intent-filter>
    </activity>
    <service android:name=".Sync"/>
  </application>
</manifest>
"#;

    #[test]
    fn sniffs_text_manifests() {
        assert!(is_text_manifest(SAMPLE.as_bytes()));
        assert!(is_text_manifest(b"\xef\xbb\xbf<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>"));
        assert!(!is_text_manifest(b"\x03\x00\x08\x00"));
        assert!(!is_text_manifest(b"PK\x03\x04"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn text_manifest_reuses_the_axml_summariser() {
        let els = parse(SAMPLE.as_bytes()).expect("parse");
        let s = axml::summarize(&els);
        assert_eq!(s.package, "com.example.text");
        assert_eq!(s.version_name, "2.0");
        assert_eq!(s.version_code, "7");
        assert_eq!(s.min_sdk.as_deref(), Some("21"));
        assert_eq!(s.target_sdk.as_deref(), Some("33"));
        assert!(s.debuggable);
        assert!(s.permissions.contains(&"android.permission.INTERNET".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(s.launcher_activity.as_deref(), Some("com.example.text.Main"));
        assert!(s.activities.iter().any(|(n, e)| n == "com.example.text.Main" && *e));
        assert!(s.services.iter().any(|(n, e)| n == "com.example.text.Sync" && !*e));
        assert_eq!(s.exported_count, 1, "comment must not be parsed as an element");
    }

    #[test]
    fn handles_entities_and_single_quotes() {
        let els = parse(b"<manifest package='a.b'><application android:label='Tom &amp; Jerry'/></manifest>")
            .expect("parse");
        let app = els.iter().find(|e| e.name == "application").expect("app");
        assert_eq!(app.value("label"), Some("Tom & Jerry"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_non_xml() {
        assert!(parse(b"\x00\x01\x02binary garbage").is_err());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! HTTP API: the single boundary between the web UI and the Rust core.
//!
//! Every handler validates input, enforces notebook scoping and returns honest
//! error codes. No handler invents data: unsupported operations return 4xx with
//! a machine-readable reason.

use crate::artifacts;
use crate::domain::*;
use crate::fetch::{self, FetchedMeta};
use crate::grounded;
use crate::hashes;
use crate::http::{percent_decode, Reply, Request, Response, StreamReply};
use crate::ingest;
use crate::json::{self, Value};
use crate::notebooklm;
use crate::providers::{self, ProviderConfig};
use crate::obj;
use crate::security;
use crate::store::{Db, Store};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::PathBuf;

pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");

pub struct Api {
    pub store: Store,
}

/// A duplicate is not an error the user caused; report which source already exists.
fn err_dup(existing_id: &str, title: &str, url: &str) -> Response {
    let body = obj! {
        "error" => format!("this URL is already a source in this notebook: {}", title),
        "code" => "duplicate_source",
        "status" => 409u64,
        "existing_source_id" => existing_id,
        "url" => url,
    };
    Response::json(409, &body)
}

fn clip(s: &str, max: usize) -> String {
    let s = s.trim();
    if s.chars().count() <= max {
        return s.to_string();
    }
    s.chars().take(max.saturating_sub(1)).collect::<String>() + "‚Ä¶"
}

/// Copy fetch provenance onto a source record.
fn apply_fetch_meta(src: &mut Source, fetched: &Option<FetchedMeta>) {
    if let Some(f) = fetched {
        src.canonical_url = f.canonical_url.clone();
        src.fetched_at = f.fetched_at.clone();
        src.meta.insert("http_status".into(), f.status.to_string());
        src.meta.insert("content_type".into(), f.content_type.clone());
        if f.redirects > 0 {
            src.meta.insert("redirects".into(), f.redirects.to_string());
        }
    }
}

fn err(status: u16, code: &str, msg: &str) -> Response {
    Response::json(
        status,
        &obj! { "error" => msg, "code" => code, "status" => status as u64 },
    )
}

fn ok(v: Value) -> Response {
    Response::json(200, &v)
}

fn created(v: Value) -> Response {
    Response::json(201, &v)
}

/// One computed chat turn: everything needed to render the answer and, separately, to store
/// it. `Clone` so a streaming reply can carry it into the post-delivery callback.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct ChatTurn {
    notebook_id: String,
    question: String,
    user_msg: Message,
    assistant_msg: Message,
    engine: String,
    engine_note: String,
    coverage: usize,
    problems: Vec<String>,
    settings: grounded::AnswerOptions,
    instructions: String,
    conv_id: Option<String>,
    sources_considered: usize,
    chunks_considered: usize,
    tables_considered: usize,
}

/// Append a turn to its conversation, creating the conversation when required. Pure with
/// respect to the store, so it serves both the buffered route and the stream's callback.
fn persist_into(db: &mut Db, turn: &ChatTurn) -> String {
    let nb = turn.notebook_id.clone();
    let cid = match turn.conv_id.clone() {
        Some(c) if db.conversations.iter().any(|x| x.id == c && x.notebook_id == nb) => c,
        _ => {
            let c = new_id("conv");
            db.conversations.push(Conversation {
                id: c.clone(),
                notebook_id: nb,
                title: turn.question.chars().take(60).collect(),
                messages: vec![],
                created_at: turn.assistant_msg.created_at.clone(),
                updated_at: turn.assistant_msg.created_at.clone(),
            });
            c
        }
    };
    if let Some(conv) = db.conversations.iter_mut().find(|c| c.id == cid) {
        conv.messages.push(turn.user_msg.clone());
        conv.messages.push(turn.assistant_msg.clone());
        conv.updated_at = now_iso();
    }
    cid
}

/// The JSON body shared by `POST .../chat` and the final frame of `POST .../chat/stream`.
fn chat_json(turn: &ChatTurn, conversation_id: &str, persisted: bool) -> Value {
    obj! {
        "conversation_id" => conversation_id,
        "message_id" => turn.assistant_msg.id.clone(),
        "answer" => turn.assistant_msg.text.clone(),
        "citations" => Value::Arr(turn.assistant_msg.citations.iter().map(|c| c.to_json()).collect()),
        "abstained" => turn.assistant_msg.abstained,
        "grounded" => true,
        "engine" => turn.engine.clone(),
        "engine_note" => turn.engine_note.clone(),
        "settings" => obj! {
            "style" => turn.settings.style.as_str(),
            "length" => turn.settings.length.as_str(),
            "max_citations" => turn.settings.length.max_citations() as u64,
        },
        "coverage" => turn.coverage as u64,
        "citation_problems" => Value::Arr(turn.problems.iter().map(|p| Value::from(p.as_str())).collect()),
        "sources_considered" => turn.sources_considered as u64,
        "chunks_considered" => turn.chunks_considered as u64,
        "tables_considered" => turn.tables_considered as u64,
        "computed" => turn.engine == "table",
        "note" => turn.assistant_msg.note.clone(),
        "notebook_instructions" => turn.instructions.clone(),
        "persisted" => persisted,
    }
}

/// Split an answer into delivery frames at line and sentence boundaries. Every piece is a
/// substring of the real answer, in order; nothing is added, dropped or reworded.
fn answer_pieces(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for line in text.split_inclusive('\n') {
        let mut cur = String::new();
        for ch in line.chars() {
            cur.push(ch);
            if matches!(ch, '.' | '?' | '!' | ':' | '\n') && cur.trim().len() > 24 {
                out.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
            }
        }
        if !cur.trim().is_empty() {
            out.push(cur);
        }
    }
    out.into_iter().filter(|p| !p.trim().is_empty()).collect()
}

impl Api {
    pub fn new(store: Store) -> Api {
        Api { store }
    }

    /// Entry point for the server. Buffered for every route except the chat stream, which
    /// needs chunked delivery (`Reply::Stream`). `handle()` stays available for tests and
    /// callers that want the buffered shape.
    pub fn route(&self, req: &Request) -> Reply {
        let path = req.path.trim_end_matches('/').to_string();
        let segs: Vec<&str> = path
            .trim_start_matches('/')
            .split('/')
            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
            .collect();
        if req.method == "POST" {
            if let ["api", "notebooks", id, "chat", "stream"] = segs.as_slice() {
                return self.chat_stream(id, req);
            }
        }
        Reply::Full(self.handle(req))
    }

    pub fn handle(&self, req: &Request) -> Response {
        let path = req.path.trim_end_matches('/').to_string();
        let path = if path.is_empty() { "/".to_string() } else { path };
        let segs: Vec<&str> = path.trim_start_matches('/').split('/').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect();

        let result = match (req.method.as_str(), segs.as_slice()) {
            ("GET", ["api", "health"]) => Ok(self.health()),
            ("GET", ["api", "capabilities"]) => Ok(ok(self.capabilities())),
            ("GET", ["api", "notebooks"]) => Ok(ok(self.list_notebooks())),
            ("POST", ["api", "notebooks"]) => self.create_notebook(req),
            ("GET", ["api", "notebooks", id]) => Ok(self.get_notebook(id)),
            ("PATCH", ["api", "notebooks", id]) => self.update_notebook(id, req),
            ("DELETE", ["api", "notebooks", id]) => Ok(self.delete_notebook(id)),
            ("GET", ["api", "notebooks", id, "sources"]) => Ok(ok(self.list_sources(id))),
            ("POST", ["api", "notebooks", id, "sources", "text"]) => self.add_text_source(id, req),
            ("POST", ["api", "notebooks", id, "sources", "upload"]) => self.add_upload_source(id, req),
            ("POST", ["api", "notebooks", id, "sources", "url"]) => self.add_url_source(id, req),
            ("GET", ["api", "notebooks", id, "chunks"]) => Ok(ok(self.list_chunks(id))),
            ("POST", ["api", "notebooks", id, "chat"]) => self.chat(id, req),
            ("GET", ["api", "notebooks", id, "conversations"]) => Ok(ok(self.list_conversations(id))),
            ("GET", ["api", "conversations", cid]) => Ok(self.get_conversation(cid)),
            ("POST", ["api", "notebooks", id, "notes"]) => self.create_note(id, req),
            ("GET", ["api", "notebooks", id, "notes"]) => Ok(ok(self.list_notes(id))),
            ("PATCH", ["api", "notes", nid]) => self.update_note(nid, req),
            ("DELETE", ["api", "notes", nid]) => Ok(self.delete_note(nid)),
            ("POST", ["api", "notes", nid, "to-source"]) => self.note_to_source(nid),
            ("POST", ["api", "notebooks", id, "artifacts"]) => self.create_artifact(id, req),
            ("GET", ["api", "notebooks", id, "artifacts"]) => Ok(ok(self.list_artifacts(id))),
            ("GET", ["api", "artifacts", aid]) => Ok(self.get_artifact(aid)),
            ("GET", ["api", "sources", sid]) => Ok(self.get_source(sid)),
            ("GET", ["api", "sources", sid, "chunks"]) => Ok(self.source_chunks(sid, req)),
            ("GET", ["api", "sources", sid, "tables"]) => Ok(self.source_tables(sid, req)),
            ("GET", ["api", "sources", sid, "guide"]) => Ok(self.source_guide(sid)),
            ("DELETE", ["api", "sources", sid]) => Ok(self.delete_source(sid)),
            ("PATCH", ["api", "sources", sid]) => self.update_source(sid, req),
            ("POST", ["api", "sources", sid, "refresh"]) => self.refresh_source(sid),
            ("GET", ["api", "notebooks", id, "export"]) => Ok(self.export_notebook(id)),
            ("POST", ["api", "import"]) => self.import_notebook(req),
            ("GET", ["api", "search"]) => Ok(self.search(req)),
            ("GET", ["api", "providers"]) => Ok(self.list_providers()),
            ("POST", ["api", "providers"]) => self.add_provider(req),
            ("DELETE", ["api", "providers", pid]) => Ok(self.delete_provider(pid)),
            ("POST", ["api", "backup"]) => self.create_backup(),
            ("GET", ["api", "backups"]) => Ok(self.list_backups()),
            ("POST", ["api", "media", "inspect"]) => self.media_inspect(req),
            ("GET", ["api", "notebooklm", "status"]) => Ok(ok(notebooklm::status())),
            ("POST", ["api", "notebooklm", "preview"]) => self.notebooklm_preview(req),
            _ => Err(err(404, "not_found", &format!("no route for {} {}", req.method, req.path))),
        };

        match result {
            Ok(r) => r,
            Err(r) => r,
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ health
    fn health(&self) -> Response {
        let (nb, src, chunks, conv, notes, arts, tables) = self.store.read(|db| {
            (db.notebooks.len(), db.sources.len(), db.chunks.len(), db.conversations.len(), db.notes.len(), db.artifacts.len(), db.tables.len())
        });
        ok(obj! {
            "status" => "ok",
            "version" => VERSION,
            "schema" => "forge.db/1",
            "counts" => obj! {
                "notebooks" => nb as u64,
                "sources" => src as u64,
                "chunks" => chunks as u64,
                "conversations" => conv as u64,
                "notes" => notes as u64,
                "artifacts" => arts as u64,
                "tables" => tables as u64,
            },
        })
    }

            "media" => obj! {
                "status" => "partial",
                "endpoint" => "/api/media/inspect",

            "sources" => obj! {
                "text" => obj!{ "status" => "supported", "locator" => "paragraph" },

                "video" => obj!{ "status" => "unsupported", "note" => "no video ingestion: downloading platform video needs an authorized extractor and per-source permission; container metadata can be inspected with POST /api/media/inspect" },
```
