## `crates/forge-core/src/artifacts.rs`

```rust
//! Study and research artifacts generated strictly from notebook evidence.
//!
//! Every generator is deterministic and citation-bearing: cards, questions and
//! reports carry the chunk they came from so the UI can jump to the evidence.
//! Nothing here invents content.

use crate::domain::{Chunk, Citation, Source};
use crate::json::Value;
use crate::obj;
use crate::retrieve;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, HashMap};

fn citation_for(chunk: &Chunk, sources: &[Source], n: usize) -> Citation {
    Citation {
        citation_id: format!("c{}", n),
        source_id: chunk.source_id.clone(),
        chunk_id: chunk.id.clone(),
        quote: chunk.text.chars().take(240).collect(),
        locator: chunk.locator.clone(),
        score: 0.0,
        source_title: sources
            .iter()
            .find(|s| s.id == chunk.source_id)
            .map(|s| s.title.clone())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "source".into()),
    }
}

fn sentences(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    crate::retrieve::split_sentences(text)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|s| s.len() >= 25)
        .collect()
}

/// "X is Y" / "X refers to Y" / "X means Y" -> (term, definition)
fn definitional(sentence: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {
    for marker in [" refers to ", " is defined as ", " means ", " is a ", " is an ", " are "] {
        if let Some(pos) = sentence.find(marker) {
            let term = sentence[..pos].trim();
            let def = sentence[pos + marker.len()..].trim();
            if term.len() >= 3 && term.len() <= 80 && def.len() >= 12 {
                let term = term
                    .trim_start_matches(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric())
                    .trim()
                    .to_string();
                if !term.is_empty() {
                    return Some((term, def.trim_end_matches('.').to_string()));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

pub fn flashcards(chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], limit: usize) -> Value {
    let mut cards: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    let mut seen: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();
    for chunk in chunks {
        for s in sentences(&chunk.text) {
            if cards.len() >= limit {
                break;
            }
            if let Some((term, def)) = definitional(&s) {
                if !seen.insert(term.to_lowercase()) {
                    continue;
                }
                let cit = citation_for(chunk, sources, cards.len() + 1);
                cards.push(obj! {
                    "id" => format!("card-{}", cards.len() + 1),
                    "front" => format!("What {}?", if term.to_lowercase().starts_with("what") { term.clone() } else { format!("is {}", term) }),
                    "back" => def,
                    "citation" => cit.to_json(),
                });
            }
        }
        if cards.len() >= limit {
            break;
        }
    }
    // Cloze fallback so a notebook of plain prose still yields study material.
    if cards.len() < limit {
        for chunk in chunks {
            for s in sentences(&chunk.text) {
                if cards.len() >= limit {
                    break;
                }
                if definitional(&s).is_some() {
                    continue;
                }
                let words = retrieve::terms(&s);
                let Some(key) = words.iter().max_by_key(|w| w.len()) else { continue };
                if key.len() < 5 || !seen.insert(format!("cloze:{}", key)) {
                    continue;
                }
                let masked = s.replacen(key.as_str(), "_____", 1);
                let cit = citation_for(chunk, sources, cards.len() + 1);
                cards.push(obj! {
                    "id" => format!("card-{}", cards.len() + 1),
                    "front" => masked,
                    "back" => key.clone(),
                    "citation" => cit.to_json(),
                });
            }
        }
    }
    obj! { "kind" => "flashcards", "count" => cards.len(), "cards" => Value::Arr(cards) }
}

pub fn quiz(chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], limit: usize) -> Value {
    let mut questions: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    // Distractor pools are drawn from the corpus itself, never invented.
    let mut freq: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for c in chunks {
        for t in retrieve::terms(&c.text) {
            if t.len() >= 4 {
                *freq.entry(t).or_insert(0) += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    let mut pool: Vec<(String, usize)> = freq.into_iter().collect();
    pool.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1).then(a.0.cmp(&b.0)));
    let pool_terms: Vec<String> = pool.iter().map(|(t, _)| t.clone()).collect();
    let pool_nums: Vec<String> = pool_terms
        .iter()
        .filter(|t| t.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) && t.len() <= 6)
        .cloned()
        .collect();

    let mut used_answers: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();

    for chunk in chunks {
        for s in sentences(&chunk.text) {
            if questions.len() >= limit {
                break;
            }
            let words = retrieve::terms(&s);
            // Prefer numeric facts; fall back to a key-term cloze so prose-only
            // notebooks still get a usable quiz.
            let numeric = words
                .iter()
                .find(|t| t.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) && t.len() <= 6)
                .cloned();
            let (correct, from_numbers) = match numeric {
                Some(n) => (n, true),
                None => {
                    let pick = words.iter().find(|w| w.len() >= 5 && pool_terms.contains(w)).cloned();
                    match pick {
                        Some(w) => (w, false),
                        None => continue,
                    }
                }
            };
            if s.len() < 40 || !used_answers.insert(correct.to_lowercase()) {
                continue;
            }

            let mut options: Vec<String> = vec![correct.clone()];
            let candidates: Vec<&String> = if from_numbers {
                pool_nums.iter().collect()
            } else {
                pool_terms
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|t| !t.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()))
                    .filter(|t| (t.len() as i64 - correct.len() as i64).abs() <= 4)
                    .collect()
            };
            for cand in candidates {
                if options.len() >= 4 {
                    break;
                }
                if cand != &correct && !options.iter().any(|o| o.eq_ignore_ascii_case(cand)) {
                    options.push(cand.clone());
                }
            }
            if options.len() < 2 {
                continue;
            }
            options.sort();
            let answer_index = options.iter().position(|o| o == &correct).unwrap_or(0);
            let stem = s.replacen(&correct, "_____", 1);
            let cit = citation_for(chunk, sources, questions.len() + 1);
            questions.push(obj! {
                "id" => format!("q-{}", questions.len() + 1),
                "question" => stem,
                "options" => Value::Arr(options.iter().map(|o| Value::from(o.as_str())).collect()),
                "answer_index" => answer_index,
                "answer" => correct.clone(),
                "explanation" => s.clone(),
                "citation" => cit.to_json(),
            });
        }
        if questions.len() >= limit {
            break;
        }
    }
    obj! { "kind" => "quiz", "count" => questions.len(), "questions" => Value::Arr(questions) }
}

pub fn report(chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], topic: &str) -> Value {
    let mut by_source: BTreeMap<String, Vec<&Chunk>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for c in chunks {
        by_source.entry(c.source_id.clone()).or_default().push(c);
    }
    let mut sections: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    let mut finding_no = 0;
    for (sid, list) in by_source.iter() {
        let title = sources
            .iter()
            .find(|s| &s.id == sid)
            .map(|s| s.title.clone())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| sid.clone());
        let mut points: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
        for c in list.iter().take(4) {
            for s in sentences(&c.text).into_iter().take(2) {
                finding_no += 1;
                let cit = citation_for(c, sources, finding_no);
                points.push(obj! {
                    "text" => s,
                    "citation" => cit.to_json(),
                });
            }
        }
        sections.push(obj! {
            "source_id" => sid.as_str(),
            "source_title" => title,
            "points" => Value::Arr(points),
        });
    }
    obj! {
        "kind" => "report",
        "title" => if topic.trim().is_empty() { "Research report".to_string() } else { format!("Research report: {}", topic.trim()) },
        "source_count" => sources.len() as u64,
        "sections" => Value::Arr(sections),
    }
}

pub fn mindmap(chunks: &[Chunk], limit_terms: usize) -> Value {
    // Term frequency across the corpus, excluding the boilerplate stopwords.
    let mut freq: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for c in chunks {
        let mut seen: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();
        for t in retrieve::terms(&c.text) {
            if t.len() > 4 && seen.insert(t.clone()) {
                *freq.entry(t).or_insert(0) += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    let mut ranked: Vec<(String, usize)> = freq.into_iter().collect();
    ranked.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1).then(a.0.cmp(&b.0)));
    ranked.truncate(limit_terms);
    let keep: BTreeSet<String> = ranked.iter().map(|(t, _)| t.clone()).collect();

    // Edge weight = number of chunks where two kept terms co-occur.
    let mut edges: HashMap<(String, String), usize> = HashMap::new();
    for c in chunks {
        let mut present: Vec<String> = retrieve::terms(&c.text)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|t| keep.contains(t))
            .collect();
        present.sort();
        present.dedup();
        for i in 0..present.len() {
            for j in (i + 1)..present.len() {
                *edges.entry((present[i].clone(), present[j].clone())).or_insert(0) += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    let mut edge_list: Vec<((String, String), usize)> =
        edges.into_iter().filter(|(_, w)| *w > 0).collect();
    edge_list.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1).then(a.0.cmp(&b.0)));
    edge_list.truncate(limit_terms * 3);

    obj! {
        "kind" => "mindmap",
        "nodes" => Value::Arr(ranked.iter().map(|(t, n)| obj! {
            "id" => t.as_str(),
            "label" => t.as_str(),
            "weight" => *n as u64,
        }).collect()),
        "edges" => Value::Arr(edge_list.iter().map(|((a, b), w)| obj! {
            "from" => a.as_str(),
            "to" => b.as_str(),
            "weight" => *w as u64,
        }).collect()),
    }
}

pub fn study_guide(chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], topic: &str) -> Value {
    let rep = report(chunks, sources, topic);
    let cards = flashcards(chunks, sources, 8);
    let mut key_terms: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    let mm = mindmap(chunks, 10);
    if let Some(nodes) = mm.get("nodes").and_then(|n| n.as_arr()) {
        for n in nodes {
            key_terms.push(obj! {
                "term" => n.str_of("label").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
                "weight" => n.get("weight").and_then(|w| w.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0),
            });
        }
    }
    obj! {
        "kind" => "study_guide",
        "title" => if topic.trim().is_empty() { "Study guide".to_string() } else { format!("Study guide: {}", topic.trim()) },
        "key_points" => rep.get("sections").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null),
        "key_terms" => Value::Arr(key_terms),
        "flashcards" => cards.get("cards").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null),
    }
}

pub fn faq(chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], limit: usize) -> Value {
    let mut items: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    let mut n = 0;
    for chunk in chunks {
        for s in sentences(&chunk.text) {
            if items.len() >= limit {
                break;
            }
            if let Some((term, def)) = definitional(&s) {
                n += 1;
                let cit = citation_for(chunk, sources, n);
                items.push(obj! {
                    "question" => format!("What {}?", term),
                    "answer" => def,
                    "citation" => cit.to_json(),
                });
            }
        }
        if items.len() >= limit {
            break;
        }
    }
    obj! { "kind" => "faq", "count" => items.len(), "items" => Value::Arr(items) }
}

pub fn summary(chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source]) -> Value {
    obj! {
        "kind" => "summary",
        "source_count" => sources.len() as u64,
        "chunk_count" => chunks.len() as u64,
        "per_source" => Value::Arr(sources.iter().map(|s| {
            let own: Vec<&Chunk> = chunks.iter().filter(|c| c.source_id == s.id).collect();
            let lead = own.first().map(|c| c.text.chars().take(280).collect::<String>()).unwrap_or_default();
            obj! {
                "source_id" => s.id.as_str(),
                "title" => s.title.as_str(),
                "status" => s.status.as_str(),
                "chunks" => own.len() as u64,
                "lead" => lead,
            }
        }).collect()),
    }
}

/// A spoken-word **script**, not audio. This build has no text-to-speech engine,
/// so the honest deliverable is a narration script with citations and a runtime
/// estimate. The capabilities endpoint labels it `audio_script`, never
/// `audio_overview`.
pub fn audio_script(chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], topic: &str) -> Value {
    let mut segments: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    let mut total_words = 0usize;

    let intro = if topic.trim().is_empty() {
        format!(
            "Welcome. This is a short briefing built from {} source{} in this notebook. Everything you are about to hear comes from those sources, and each point carries a citation.",
            sources.len(),
            if sources.len() == 1 { "" } else { "s" }
        )
    } else {
        format!(
            "Welcome. This briefing covers {} using {} source{} from this notebook.",
            topic.trim(),
            sources.len(),
            if sources.len() == 1 { "" } else { "s" }
        )
    };
    total_words += intro.split_whitespace().count();
    segments.push(obj! { "speaker" => "host", "text" => intro, "citation" => Value::Null });

    let mut n = 0;
    for src in sources {
        let own: Vec<&Chunk> = chunks.iter().filter(|c| c.source_id == src.id).take(3).collect();
        if own.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        for c in own {
            let lead = sentences(&c.text).into_iter().next().unwrap_or_else(|| c.text.chars().take(280).collect());
            n += 1;
            total_words += lead.split_whitespace().count();
            let cit = citation_for(c, sources, n);
            segments.push(obj! {
                "speaker" => "host",
                "text" => lead.clone(),
                "citation" => cit.to_json(),
            });
        }
        let bridge = format!(
            "That was from {}. ",
            src.title
        );
        total_words += bridge.split_whitespace().count();
        segments.push(obj! { "speaker" => "host", "text" => bridge, "citation" => Value::Null });
    }

    let outro = "That is the end of this briefing. Every statement above is quoted from the notebook's evidence; open the citations to check them yourself.".to_string();
    total_words += outro.split_whitespace().count();
    segments.push(obj! { "speaker" => "host", "text" => outro, "citation" => Value::Null });

    let seconds = (total_words as f64 / 150.0 * 60.0).round() as u64;
    obj! {
        "kind" => "audio_script",
        "title" => if topic.trim().is_empty() { "Narration script".to_string() } else { format!("Narration script: {}", topic.trim()) },
        "voice" => "single host",
        "word_count" => total_words as u64,
        "estimated_seconds" => seconds,
        "segments" => Value::Arr(segments),
        "note" => "Script only: this build contains no text-to-speech engine, so no audio file is produced.",
    }
}

pub fn generate(
    kind: &str,
    chunks: &[Chunk],
    sources: &[Source],
    topic: &str,
) -> Result<(String, Value), String> {
    let title = match kind {
        "flashcards" => ("Forge flashcards".to_string(), flashcards(chunks, sources, 12)),
        "quiz" => ("Forge quiz".to_string(), quiz(chunks, sources, 8)),
        "report" => {
            let t = if topic.trim().is_empty() { "Research report".to_string() } else { format!("Research report: {}", topic.trim()) };
            (t.clone(), report(chunks, sources, topic))
        }
        "mindmap" => ("Concept map".to_string(), mindmap(chunks, 16)),
        "study_guide" => ("Study guide".to_string(), study_guide(chunks, sources, topic)),
        "faq" => ("Notebook FAQ".to_string(), faq(chunks, sources, 8)),
        "summary" => ("Source summary".to_string(), summary(chunks, sources)),
        "audio_script" => {
            let t = if topic.trim().is_empty() { "Narration script".to_string() } else { format!("Narration script: {}", topic.trim()) };
            (t.clone(), audio_script(chunks, sources, topic))
        }
        other => return Err(format!("unknown artifact kind: {}", other)),
    };
    Ok(title)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::domain::Locator;

    fn src(id: &str) -> Source {
        Source {
            id: id.into(),
            notebook_id: "nb".into(),
            title: format!("Source {}", id),
            kind: "text".into(),
            origin: String::new(),
            byte_len: 1,
            status: "ready".into(),
            error: String::new(),
            warnings: vec![],
            added_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z".into(),
            page_count: 0,
            chunk_count: 1,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    fn chunk(id: &str, sid: &str, text: &str, page: u32) -> Chunk {
        Chunk {
            id: id.into(),
            source_id: sid.into(),
            notebook_id: "nb".into(),
            ordinal: 0,
            text: text.into(),
            locator: Locator::page(page, 0, text.len() as u32),
        }
    }

    fn corpus() -> (Vec<Chunk>, Vec<Source>) {
        (
            vec![
                chunk("k1", "s1", "BM25 is a ranking function used by search engines to estimate relevance.", 1),
                chunk("k2", "s1", "The retrieval system returned 42 candidate spans for the query.", 2),
                chunk("k3", "s2", "A citation is a reference to a specific piece of evidence in a source.", 3),
            ],
            vec![src("s1"), src("s2")],
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn flashcards_are_grounded_and_cited() {
        let (chunks, sources) = corpus();
        let v = flashcards(&chunks, &sources, 10);
        let cards = v.get("cards").and_then(|c| c.as_arr()).unwrap();
        assert!(!cards.is_empty());
        for c in cards {
            let cit = c.get("citation").expect("citation");
            assert!(!cit.str_of("source_id").unwrap().is_empty());
            assert!(!c.str_of("back").unwrap().is_empty());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn quiz_options_contain_the_answer() {
        let (chunks, sources) = corpus();
        let v = quiz(&chunks, &sources, 5);
        let qs = v.get("questions").and_then(|c| c.as_arr()).unwrap();
        assert!(!qs.is_empty());
        for q in qs {
            let opts = q.get("options").and_then(|o| o.as_arr()).unwrap();
            let idx = q.get("answer_index").and_then(|i| i.as_f64()).unwrap() as usize;
            assert!(opts.len() >= 2);
            assert!(idx < opts.len(), "answer index within options");
            assert!(q.str_of("explanation").is_some());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn report_covers_every_source() {
        let (chunks, sources) = corpus();
        let v = report(&chunks, &sources, "retrieval");
        let sections = v.get("sections").and_then(|s| s.as_arr()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(sections.len(), 2);
        let title = v.str_of("title").unwrap();
        assert!(title.contains("retrieval"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn mindmap_has_nodes_and_edges() {
        let (chunks, _) = corpus();
        let v = mindmap(&chunks, 10);
        let nodes = v.get("nodes").and_then(|n| n.as_arr()).unwrap();
        assert!(!nodes.is_empty());
        let edges = v.get("edges").and_then(|e| e.as_arr()).unwrap();
        assert!(!edges.is_empty(), "co-occurring terms should produce edges");
    }

    #[test]
    fn audio_script_is_a_script_not_audio() {
        let (chunks, sources) = corpus();
        let v = audio_script(&chunks, &sources, "");
        assert_eq!(v.str_of("kind"), Some("audio_script"));
        let segs = v.get("segments").and_then(|s| s.as_arr()).unwrap();
        assert!(segs.len() >= 4);
        assert!(v.str_of("note").unwrap().contains("no audio"));
        assert!(v.get("estimated_seconds").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap() > 0.0);
        // at least one segment carries a citation
        assert!(segs.iter().any(|s| s.get("citation").map(|c| !matches!(c, Value::Null)).unwrap_or(false)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_kind_is_rejected() {
        let (chunks, sources) = corpus();
        assert!(generate("podcast", &chunks, &sources, "").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn all_supported_kinds_generate() {
        let (chunks, sources) = corpus();
        for k in ["flashcards", "quiz", "report", "mindmap", "study_guide", "faq", "summary", "audio_script"] {
            assert!(generate(k, &chunks, &sources, "topic").is_ok(), "kind {}", k);
        }
    }
}
```

## `crates/forge-core/src/domain.rs`

```rust
//! Domain model for a source-grounded research notebook.
//!
//! Invariants enforced here (and covered by tests):
//!  * every chunk belongs to exactly one source and carries a stable locator;
//!  * a citation must reference a chunk that exists in the same notebook;
//!  * IDs are opaque and stable across restarts.

use crate::json::Value;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// Stable, content-derived 16-hex-digit id fragment. Used for table ids so that
/// re-ingesting identical bytes yields identical ids.
pub fn short_hash(input: &str) -> String {
    crate::hashes::sha256(input.as_bytes())[..16].to_string()
}

pub fn new_id(prefix: &str) -> String {
    // Time-ordered, collision-resistant enough for a local single-user app.
    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
    let nanos = SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let mut x = nanos as u64 ^ (std::process::id() as u64) << 32;
    // xorshift for a deterministic-but-varying suffix
    x ^= x << 13;
    x ^= x >> 7;
    x ^= x << 17;
    format!("{}-{:012x}{:06x}", prefix, nanos as u64 & 0xffffffffffff, x & 0xffffff)
}

pub fn now_iso() -> String {
    let secs = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_secs() as i64)
        .unwrap_or(0);
    iso_from_unix(secs)
}

/// ISO-8601 UTC timestamp from unix seconds (days-from-civil inverse algorithm).
pub fn iso_from_unix(secs: i64) -> String {
    let days = secs.div_euclid(86_400);
    let rem = secs.rem_euclid(86_400);
    let (y, m, d) = civil_from_days(days);
    format!(
        "{:04}-{:02}-{:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z",
        y,
        m,
        d,
        rem / 3600,
        (rem % 3600) / 60,
        rem % 60
    )
}

fn civil_from_days(z: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    let z = z + 719_468;
    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;
    let doe = (z - era * 146_097) as u64; // [0, 146096]
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365; // [0, 399]
    let y = yoe as i64 + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100); // [0, 365]
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153; // [0, 11]
    let d = (doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1) as u32; // [1, 31]
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 } as u32; // [1, 12]
    (if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y }, m, d)
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SourceKind {
    Text,
    Markdown,
    Html,
    Csv,
    Pdf,
    Docx,
    Pptx,
    Xlsx,
    Url,
    Note,
}

impl SourceKind {
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            SourceKind::Text => "text",
            SourceKind::Markdown => "markdown",
            SourceKind::Html => "html",
            SourceKind::Csv => "csv",
            SourceKind::Pdf => "pdf",
            SourceKind::Docx => "docx",
            SourceKind::Pptx => "pptx",
            SourceKind::Xlsx => "xlsx",
            SourceKind::Url => "url",
            SourceKind::Note => "note",
        }
    }

    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<SourceKind> {
        Some(match s {
            "text" | "txt" => SourceKind::Text,
            "markdown" | "md" => SourceKind::Markdown,
            "html" | "htm" => SourceKind::Html,
            "csv" | "tsv" => SourceKind::Csv,
            "pdf" => SourceKind::Pdf,
            "docx" | "doc" => SourceKind::Docx,
            "pptx" | "ppt" => SourceKind::Pptx,
            "xlsx" | "xls" | "spreadsheet" => SourceKind::Xlsx,
            "url" => SourceKind::Url,
            "note" => SourceKind::Note,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }

    pub fn from_filename(name: &str) -> SourceKind {
        let lower = name.to_ascii_lowercase();
        if lower.ends_with(".pdf") {
            SourceKind::Pdf
        } else if lower.ends_with(".docx") {
            SourceKind::Docx
        } else if lower.ends_with(".pptx") {
            SourceKind::Pptx
        } else if lower.ends_with(".xlsx") {
            SourceKind::Xlsx
        } else if lower.ends_with(".md") || lower.ends_with(".markdown") {
            SourceKind::Markdown
        } else if lower.ends_with(".html") || lower.ends_with(".htm") {
            SourceKind::Html
        } else if lower.ends_with(".csv") || lower.ends_with(".tsv") {
            SourceKind::Csv
        } else {
            SourceKind::Text
        }
    }
}

/// Where a piece of evidence sits inside its source. Kept structured so the UI
/// can navigate to the exact page/row/paragraph instead of a loose text match.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Locator {
    /// "page" | "paragraph" | "row" | "section" | "line" | "cell" | "slide" | "timestamp"
    pub kind: String,
    pub page: Option<u32>,
    pub paragraph: Option<u32>,
    pub row: Option<u32>,
    pub section: Option<String>,
    /// Worksheet name for spreadsheet cells (also used for slide names).
    pub sheet: Option<String>,
    /// A1 reference or A1 range, e.g. `B7` or `B2:B19`.
    pub cell: Option<String>,
    /// 1-based column index; set only when the evidence is a whole column.
    pub col: Option<u32>,
    /// Offset into the media timeline, in milliseconds (`kind = "timestamp"`).
    pub at_ms: Option<u32>,
    pub start: u32,
    pub end: u32,
}

impl Locator {
    pub fn page(p: u32, start: u32, end: u32) -> Locator {
        Locator { kind: "page".into(), page: Some(p), paragraph: None, row: None, section: None, sheet: None, cell: None, col: None, at_ms: None, start, end }
    }
    pub fn paragraph(idx: u32, start: u32, end: u32) -> Locator {
        Locator { kind: "paragraph".into(), page: None, paragraph: Some(idx), row: None, section: None, sheet: None, cell: None, col: None, at_ms: None, start, end }
    }
    pub fn row(idx: u32, start: u32, end: u32) -> Locator {
        Locator { kind: "row".into(), page: None, paragraph: None, row: Some(idx), section: None, sheet: None, cell: None, col: None, at_ms: None, start, end }
    }
    /// A spreadsheet row: keeps `kind = "row"` (existing contracts) while adding the
    /// sheet and the exact A1 range, so the row can be found in the grid.
    pub fn sheet_row(sheet: &str, row: u32, reference: &str) -> Locator {
        Locator {
            kind: "row".into(),
            page: None,
            paragraph: None,
            row: Some(row),
            section: None,
            sheet: Some(sheet.to_string()),
            cell: Some(reference.to_string()),
            col: None,
            at_ms: None,
            start: 0,
            end: 0,
        }
    }

    pub fn section(name: impl Into<String>, start: u32, end: u32) -> Locator {
        Locator { kind: "section".into(), page: None, paragraph: None, row: None, section: Some(name.into()), sheet: None, cell: None, col: None, at_ms: None, start, end }
    }
    pub fn line(idx: u32, start: u32, end: u32) -> Locator {
        Locator { kind: "line".into(), page: None, paragraph: None, row: None, section: Some(idx.to_string()), sheet: None, cell: None, col: None, at_ms: None, start, end }
    }

    /// A spreadsheet cell or cell range: `Locator::cell("Q1", "B2:B19", 2)`.
    /// The row is the first row of the range, so a single-cell citation and a
    /// column citation share one representation.
    pub fn cell(sheet: &str, reference: &str, row: u32) -> Locator {
        // the reference may arrive sheet-qualified ("Sales!C2:C6"); the column letters
        // start after the last '!'
        let bare = reference.rsplit('!').next().unwrap_or(reference);
        let col = bare
            .chars()
            .take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
            .fold(0u32, |acc, c| acc * 26 + (c.to_ascii_uppercase() as u32 - 64));
        Locator {
            kind: "cell".into(),
            page: None,
            paragraph: None,
            row: Some(row),
            section: None,
            sheet: Some(sheet.to_string()),
            cell: Some(reference.to_string()),
            col: if col > 0 { Some(col) } else { None },
            at_ms: None,
            start: 0,
            end: 0,
        }
    }

    /// A point on a media timeline (milliseconds).
    pub fn timestamp(ms: u32) -> Locator {
        Locator {
            kind: "timestamp".into(),
            page: None,
            paragraph: None,
            row: None,
            section: None,
            sheet: None,
            cell: None,
            col: None,
            at_ms: Some(ms),
            start: 0,
            end: 0,
        }
    }

    pub fn human(&self) -> String {
        match self.kind.as_str() {
            "page" => format!("page {}", self.page.unwrap_or(0)),
            "row" => match &self.sheet {
                Some(sheet) => format!("{} row {}", sheet, self.row.unwrap_or(0)),
                None => format!("row {}", self.row.unwrap_or(0)),
            },
            "section" => format!("section {}", self.section.clone().unwrap_or_default()),
            "cell" => {
                let cell = self.cell.clone().unwrap_or_default();
                if cell.contains('!') {
                    cell // already sheet-qualified, e.g. "Sales!C2:C6"
                } else {
                    format!("{}!{}", self.sheet.clone().unwrap_or_default(), cell)
                }
            }
            "timestamp" => {
                let ms = self.at_ms.unwrap_or(0);
                let total = ms / 1000;
                format!("{:02}:{:02}", total / 60, total % 60)
            }
            _ => format!("paragraph {}", self.paragraph.unwrap_or(0)),
        }
    }

    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
        let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
        m.insert("kind".into(), Value::from(self.kind.as_str()));
        if let Some(p) = self.page {
            m.insert("page".into(), Value::from(p as u64));
        }
        if let Some(p) = self.paragraph {
            m.insert("paragraph".into(), Value::from(p as u64));
        }
        if let Some(r) = self.row {
            m.insert("row".into(), Value::from(r as u64));
        }
        if let Some(s) = &self.section {
            m.insert("section".into(), Value::from(s.as_str()));
        }
        if let Some(s) = &self.sheet {
            m.insert("sheet".into(), Value::from(s.as_str()));
        }
        if let Some(c) = &self.cell {
            m.insert("cell".into(), Value::from(c.as_str()));
        }
        if let Some(c) = self.col {
            m.insert("col".into(), Value::from(c as u64));
        }
        if let Some(ms) = self.at_ms {
            m.insert("at_ms".into(), Value::from(ms as u64));
        }
        m.insert("start".into(), Value::from(self.start as u64));
        m.insert("end".into(), Value::from(self.end as u64));
        Value::Obj(m)
    }

    pub fn from_json(v: &Value) -> Locator {
        Locator {
            kind: v.str_of("kind").unwrap_or("paragraph").to_string(),
            page: v.get("page").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).map(|x| x as u32),
            paragraph: v.get("paragraph").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).map(|x| x as u32),
            row: v.get("row").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).map(|x| x as u32),
            section: v.str_of("section").map(|s| s.to_string()),
            sheet: v.str_of("sheet").map(|s| s.to_string()),
            cell: v.str_of("cell").map(|s| s.to_string()),
            col: v.get("col").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).map(|x| x as u32),
            at_ms: v.get("at_ms").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).map(|x| x as u32),
            start: v.get("start").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u32,
            end: v.get("end").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u32,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Notebook {

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Source {
    pub id: String,
    pub notebook_id: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub kind: String,
    /// Where it came from: "upload", "paste", "url", "note".
    pub origin: String,
    pub byte_len: usize,
    pub status: String, // ready | failed
    pub error: String,
    pub warnings: Vec<String>,
    pub added_at: String,
    pub page_count: u32,
    pub chunk_count: u32,
    /// SHA-256 of the bytes that were parsed. Detects duplicates and source changes.
    pub content_hash: String,
    /// Normalised URL for fetched sources (empty otherwise).
    pub canonical_url: String,
    /// When a URL source was last retrieved (empty for local sources).
    pub fetched_at: String,
    /// User labels, used for filtering. Free-form, case-preserved.
    pub labels: Vec<String>,
    /// Extensible metadata: http_status, content_type, converted_from, ...
    pub meta: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

impl Default for Source {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Source {
            id: String::new(),
            notebook_id: String::new(),
            title: String::new(),
            kind: String::new(),
            origin: String::new(),
            byte_len: 0,
            status: String::new(),
            error: String::new(),
            warnings: Vec::new(),
            added_at: String::new(),
            page_count: 0,
            chunk_count: 0,
            content_hash: String::new(),
            canonical_url: String::new(),
            fetched_at: String::new(),
            labels: Vec::new(),
            meta: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
        }
    }
}

impl Source {
    pub fn meta_of(&self, key: &str) -> &str {
        self.meta.get(key).map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("")
    }
}

    pub source_ids: Vec<String>,
    pub payload: Value,
    /// Set when a source it was built from changed after generation.
    pub stale: bool,
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ JSON

impl Citation {
    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
        let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
        m.insert("citation_id".into(), Value::from(self.citation_id.as_str()));
        // Display index, e.g. "c3" -> 3, so the UI can render [3] without parsing.
        let n: u64 = self
            .citation_id
            .trim_start_matches(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())
            .parse()
            .unwrap_or(0);
        m.insert("n".into(), Value::from(n as f64));
        m.insert("source_id".into(), Value::from(self.source_id.as_str()));
        m.insert("chunk_id".into(), Value::from(self.chunk_id.as_str()));
        m.insert("quote".into(), Value::from(self.quote.as_str()));
        m.insert("locator".into(), self.locator.to_json());
        m.insert("locator_label".into(), Value::from(self.locator.human()));
        m.insert("score".into(), Value::from(self.score));
        m.insert("source_title".into(), Value::from(self.source_title.as_str()));
        Value::Obj(m)
    }

    pub fn from_json(v: &Value) -> Citation {
        Citation {
            citation_id: v.str_of("citation_id").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
            source_id: v.str_of("source_id").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
            chunk_id: v.str_of("chunk_id").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
            quote: v.str_of("quote").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
            locator: v.get("locator").map(Locator::from_json).unwrap_or(Locator::paragraph(0, 0, 0)),
            score: v.get("score").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0),
            source_title: v.str_of("source_title").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
        }
    }
}

impl Message {
    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
        let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
        m.insert("id".into(), Value::from(self.id.as_str()));
        m.insert("role".into(), Value::from(self.role.as_str()));
        m.insert("text".into(), Value::from(self.text.as_str()));
        m.insert(
            "citations".into(),
            Value::Arr(self.citations.iter().map(|c| c.to_json()).collect()),
        );
        m.insert("created_at".into(), Value::from(self.created_at.as_str()));
        m.insert("grounded".into(), Value::Bool(self.grounded));
        m.insert("abstained".into(), Value::Bool(self.abstained));
        m.insert("note".into(), Value::from(self.note.as_str()));
        Value::Obj(m)
    }

    pub fn from_json(v: &Value) -> Message {
        Message {
            id: v.str_of("id").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
            role: v.str_of("role").unwrap_or("assistant").to_string(),
            text: v.str_of("text").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
            citations: v
                .get("citations")
                .and_then(|c| c.as_arr())
                .map(|arr| arr.iter().map(Citation::from_json).collect())
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            created_at: v.str_of("created_at").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
            grounded: v.get("grounded").and_then(|b| b.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),
            abstained: v.get("abstained").and_then(|b| b.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),
            note: v.str_of("note").unwrap_or("").to_string(),
        }
    }
}

pub fn json_str_list(items: &[String]) -> Value {
    Value::Arr(items.iter().map(|s| Value::from(s.as_str())).collect())
}

pub fn parse_str_list(v: Option<&Value>) -> Vec<String> {
    v.and_then(|x| x.as_arr())
        .map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string())).collect())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {

        assert_eq!(iso_from_unix(1_700_000_000), "2023-11-14T22:13:20Z");
        assert_eq!(iso_from_unix(951_782_400), "2000-02-29T00:00:00Z"); // leap day
    }

    #[test]
    fn ids_are_unique_and_prefixed() {
        let a = new_id("nb");
        let b = new_id("nb");
        assert!(a.starts_with("nb-"));

    }

    #[test]

        let back = Locator::from_json(&l.to_json());
        assert_eq!(back.page, Some(7));
        assert_eq!(back.kind, "page");
        assert_eq!(l.human(), "page 7");
    }

    #[test]
    fn cell_locators_carry_sheet_reference_and_column() {
        let l = Locator::cell("Sales", "Sales!C2:C6", 2);
        assert_eq!(l.kind, "cell");
        assert_eq!(l.sheet.as_deref(), Some("Sales"));
        assert_eq!(l.cell.as_deref(), Some("Sales!C2:C6"));
        assert_eq!(l.col, Some(3), "C is column 3, sheet name must not be parsed as letters");
        assert_eq!(l.row, Some(2));
        assert_eq!(l.human(), "Sales!C2:C6");
        let back = Locator::from_json(&l.to_json());
        assert_eq!(back.cell, l.cell);
        assert_eq!(back.col, l.col);

        // a row locator can also be sheet-qualified and keep its range
        let r = Locator::sheet_row("Sales", 4, "A4-D4");
        assert_eq!(r.kind, "row");
        assert_eq!(r.human(), "Sales row 4");

        let t = Locator::timestamp(75_000);
        assert_eq!(t.kind, "timestamp");
        assert_eq!(t.human(), "01:15");
        assert_eq!(Locator::from_json(&t.to_json()).at_ms, Some(75_000));
    }

    #[test]
    fn kind_detection_from_filename() {
        assert_eq!(SourceKind::from_filename("a.PDF"), SourceKind::Pdf);
        assert_eq!(SourceKind::from_filename("b.md"), SourceKind::Markdown);
        assert_eq!(SourceKind::from_filename("c.csv"), SourceKind::Csv);
        assert_eq!(SourceKind::from_filename("d.unknown"), SourceKind::Text);
    }

    #[test]
    fn json_roundtrip_message() {

            id: "m1".into(),
            role: "assistant".into(),
            text: "hi".into(),
            citations: vec![Citation {
                citation_id: "c1".into(),
                source_id: "s1".into(),
                chunk_id: "k1".into(),
                quote: "q".into(),
                locator: Locator::page(2, 0, 5),
                score: 1.5,

            created_at: now_iso(),
            grounded: true,

        };
        let back = Message::from_json(&m.to_json());
        assert_eq!(back.text, "hi");
        assert_eq!(back.citations.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(back.citations[0].locator.page, Some(2));
        assert!(back.grounded);
    }
}
```

## `crates/forge-core/src/fetch.rs`

```rust
//! Outbound URL fetching, with the SSRF policy enforced at every hop.
//!
//! Why `curl` and not a Rust client: this build has no TLS crate (crates.io is
//! unreachable ‚Äî `docs/DECISIONS.md` D1), and the reference product's URL sources
//! are overwhelmingly https. `curl` is a mature, ubiquitous HTTP client, invoked
//! here as a subprocess with an explicit argument vector ‚Äî never through a shell ‚Äî
//! and never with credentials, cookies, or a proxy configuration.
//!
//! The security properties are ours, not curl's:
//!
//! 1. the URL is parsed by `security::parse_url` (scheme, userinfo, control chars);
//! 2. the host is resolved by us, and **every** address must be public;
//! 3. curl is pinned with `--resolve host:port:ip` so its own DNS lookup cannot
//!    disagree with ours (this is what defeats DNS rebinding);
//! 4. redirects are *not* followed by curl (`--max-redirs 0`); each `Location` is
//!    re-validated and re-pinned, with a hop cap;
//! 5. body size and time are capped, and `--proto`/`--proto-redir` restrict the
//!    scheme set even if a Location points somewhere unexpected.

use crate::security::{self, ParsedUrl};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::Command;
use std::time::Duration;

/// Default ceilings for a single fetch.
pub const MAX_FETCH_BYTES: usize = 20 * 1024 * 1024;
pub const MAX_HOPS: usize = 5;
pub const FETCH_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);

pub const USER_AGENT: &str = "ForgeBot/0.1 (local research workspace; +https://example.invalid/forge)";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum FetchError {
    /// The URL was refused before any network activity.
    Rejected(String),
    /// No transport could be started (curl missing, spawn failure).
    NoTransport(String),
    /// The transport ran but the request failed or returned a non-success status.
    Failed(String),
    /// The response was too large or took too long.
    Limit(String),
}

impl FetchError {
    pub fn message(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            FetchError::Rejected(m) => format!("refused: {}", m),
            FetchError::NoTransport(m) => format!("no fetch transport: {}", m),
            FetchError::Failed(m) => format!("fetch failed: {}", m),
            FetchError::Limit(m) => format!("limit exceeded: {}", m),
        }
    }

    pub fn code(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            FetchError::Rejected(_) => "url_rejected",
            FetchError::NoTransport(_) => "fetch_transport_unavailable",
            FetchError::Failed(_) => "fetch_failed",
            FetchError::Limit(_) => "fetch_limit_exceeded",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Fetched {
    /// The URL that produced the body after following redirects.
    pub final_url: String,
    /// Normalised identity of `final_url`, used for duplicate detection.
    pub canonical_url: String,
    pub status: u16,
    pub content_type: String,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
    pub redirects: Vec<(u16, String)>,
}

impl Fetched {
    /// Media type without parameters, lower-cased (`text/html; charset=utf-8` ‚Üí `text/html`).
    pub fn media_type(&self) -> String {
        self.content_type
            .split(';')
            .next()
            .unwrap_or("")
            .trim()
            .to_ascii_lowercase()
    }

    /// Best guess at the ingest kind for `ingest::extract`, from Content-Type first
    /// and the URL path second.
    pub fn ingest_kind(&self) -> &'static str {
        let mt = self.media_type();
        let path = self.final_url.split(['?', '#']).next().unwrap_or("").to_ascii_lowercase();
        let ends = |ext: &str| path.ends_with(&format!(".{}", ext));
        if mt == "application/pdf" || ends("pdf") || self.body.starts_with(b"%PDF") {
            return "pdf";
        }
        if mt == "text/html" || mt == "application/xhtml+xml" || ends("html") || ends("htm") {
            return "html";
        }
        if mt == "text/markdown" || ends("md") || ends("markdown") {
            return "markdown";
        }
        if mt == "text/csv" || ends("csv") {
            return "csv";
        }
        if mt == "text/tab-separated-values" || ends("tsv") {
            return "tsv";
        }
        // JSON, plain text, and anything unrecognised are treated as text: better to
        // index a readable body than to reject a source the user asked for.
        "text"
    }
}

/// Provenance for a source created by fetching a URL.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct FetchedMeta {
    pub canonical_url: String,
    pub fetched_at: String,
    pub status: u16,
    pub content_type: String,
    pub redirects: usize,
}

/// Is a working HTTP transport present?
pub fn transport_available() -> bool {
    Command::new("curl")
        .arg("--version")
        .output()
        .map(|o| o.status.success())
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

fn temp_paths() -> (PathBuf, PathBuf) {
    let stamp = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let pid = std::process::id();
    let base = std::env::temp_dir();
    (
        base.join(format!("forge-fetch-{}-{}.body", pid, stamp)),
        base.join(format!("forge-fetch-{}-{}.hdr", pid, stamp)),
    )
}

/// One request, no redirect following. Returns (status, headers text, body).
fn request_once(url: &ParsedUrl, ip: std::net::IpAddr, max_bytes: usize) -> Result<(u16, String, Vec<u8>), FetchError> {
    let (body_path, hdr_path) = temp_paths();
    let pin = if url.host.contains(':') {
        format!("[{}]:{}:{}", url.host, url.port, ip)
    } else {
        format!("{}:{}:{}", url.host, url.port, ip)
    };
    let output = Command::new("curl")
        .args([
            "--silent",
            "--show-error",
            "--no-progress-meter",
            "--proto",
            "=http,https",
            "--proto-redir",
            "=http,https",
            "--max-redirs",
            "0",
            "--max-time",
            &FETCH_TIMEOUT.as_secs().to_string(),
            "--max-filesize",
            &max_bytes.to_string(),
            "--user-agent",
            USER_AGENT,
            "--header",
            "Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,text/plain;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.5",
            "--resolve",
            &pin,
            "--dump-header",
            &hdr_path.to_string_lossy(),
            "--output",
            &body_path.to_string_lossy(),
            "--write-out",
            "%{http_code}",
            &url.to_url(),
        ])
        .output();

    let cleanup = || {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&body_path);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&hdr_path);
    };

    let out = match output {
        Ok(o) => o,
        Err(e) => {
            cleanup();
            return Err(FetchError::NoTransport(format!("cannot run curl: {}", e)));
        }
    };
    let headers = std::fs::read_to_string(&hdr_path).unwrap_or_default();
    let body = std::fs::read(&body_path).unwrap_or_default();
    cleanup();

    if !out.status.success() {
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim().to_string();
        // curl exit code 63 = max-filesize exceeded
        return if out.status.code() == Some(63) {
            Err(FetchError::Limit(format!(
                "response body exceeds {} bytes",
                max_bytes
            )))
        } else if out.status.code() == Some(28) {
            Err(FetchError::Limit(format!(
                "request exceeded {}s",
                FETCH_TIMEOUT.as_secs()
            )))
        } else {
            Err(FetchError::Failed(if stderr.is_empty() {
                format!("curl exited {:?}", out.status.code())
            } else {
                stderr
            }))
        };
    }
    let status: u16 = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout)
        .trim()
        .parse()
        .unwrap_or(0);
    Ok((status, headers, body))
}

fn header_value(headers: &str, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let want = format!("{}:", name.to_ascii_lowercase());
    // Last occurrence wins: with `--dump-header` a redirect chain can appear, and we
    // only ever issue single-hop requests, so the last block is the real one.
    headers
        .lines()
        .filter(|l| l.to_ascii_lowercase().starts_with(&want))
        .last()
        .map(|l| l[want.len()..].trim().to_string())
}

fn resolve_location(base: &ParsedUrl, location: &str) -> Result<ParsedUrl, FetchError> {
    let loc = location.trim();
    if loc.starts_with("http://") || loc.starts_with("https://") {
        return security::parse_url(loc).map_err(FetchError::Rejected);
    }
    if loc.starts_with("//") {
        return security::parse_url(&format!("{}:{}", base.scheme, loc)).map_err(FetchError::Rejected);
    }
    if loc.starts_with('/') {
        let (path, query) = match loc.split_once('?') {
            Some((p, q)) => (p, format!("?{}", q)),
            None => (loc, String::new()),
        };
        return Ok(ParsedUrl {
            scheme: base.scheme.clone(),
            host: base.host.clone(),
            port: base.port,
            path_query: format!("{}{}", path, query),
        });
    }
    // Relative to the current directory
    let base_dir = base.path_query.rsplit_once('/').map(|(d, _)| d).unwrap_or("");
    Ok(ParsedUrl {
        scheme: base.scheme.clone(),
        host: base.host.clone(),
        port: base.port,
        path_query: format!("{}/{}", base_dir, loc),
    })
}

/// Fetch a URL, validating policy at every hop.
pub fn fetch(raw_url: &str) -> Result<Fetched, FetchError> {
    fetch_with_limits(raw_url, MAX_FETCH_BYTES)
}

pub fn fetch_with_limits(raw_url: &str, max_bytes: usize) -> Result<Fetched, FetchError> {
    let mut url = security::parse_url(raw_url).map_err(FetchError::Rejected)?;
    let mut redirects: Vec<(u16, String)> = Vec::new();

    for hop in 0..=MAX_HOPS {
        if hop == MAX_HOPS {
            return Err(FetchError::Rejected(format!(
                "more than {} redirects",
                MAX_HOPS
            )));
        }
        let ips = security::resolve_public(&url.host, url.port).map_err(|e| match e {
            security::ResolveError::Blocked(m) => FetchError::Rejected(m),
            security::ResolveError::Dns(m) => FetchError::Failed(m),
        })?;
        let ip = ips[0];
        let (status, headers, body) = request_once(&url, ip, max_bytes)?;

        if (300..400).contains(&status) {
            let location = header_value(&headers, "location")
                .ok_or_else(|| FetchError::Failed(format!("HTTP {} without Location", status)))?;
            let next = resolve_location(&url, &location)?;
            redirects.push((status, next.to_url()));
            url = next;
            continue;
        }
        if !(200..300).contains(&status) {
            return Err(FetchError::Failed(format!(
                "HTTP {} for {}",
                status,
                url.to_url()
            )));
        }
        if body.len() > max_bytes {
            return Err(FetchError::Limit(format!(
                "body of {} bytes exceeds {}",
                body.len(),
                max_bytes
            )));
        }
        let content_type = header_value(&headers, "content-type").unwrap_or_default();
        return Ok(Fetched {
            final_url: url.to_url(),
            canonical_url: url.canonical(),
            status,
            content_type,
            body,
            redirects,
        });
    }
    unreachable!("loop always returns")
}

/// Remove a fragment and normalise a URL for duplicate detection without network access.
pub fn canonicalize(raw: &str) -> Option<String> {
    security::parse_url(raw).ok().map(|u| u.canonical())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read, Write};
    use std::net::TcpListener;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

    // ---- one shared loopback fixture server -------------------------------
    //
    // Private-range fetching is off by default; the test opts in explicitly for the
    // duration of the test. Because the flag is process-global and tests run in
    // parallel, every test that needs the server goes through `with_server`, which
    // holds a lock.
    static SERVER_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());
    static HITS: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

    fn with_server<T>(f: impl FnOnce(u16) -> T) -> T {
        let _guard = SERVER_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        std::env::set_var("FORGE_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE", "1");
        let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").expect("bind");
        let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            for stream in listener.incoming().take(6) {
                let mut stream = match stream {
                    Ok(s) => s,
                    Err(_) => continue,
                };
                HITS.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream.try_clone().unwrap());
                let mut first = String::new();
                let _ = reader.read_line(&mut first);
                let path = first.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap_or("/").to_string();
                // drain headers
                loop {
                    let mut line = String::new();
                    if reader.read_line(&mut line).unwrap_or(0) == 0 || line.trim().is_empty() {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                let (status, ctype, body): (u16, &str, Vec<u8>) = match path.as_str() {
                    "/page" => (
                        200,
                        "text/html; charset=utf-8",
                        b"<html><head><title>Fixture Page</title></head><body>\
                          <h1>Retrieval</h1><p>Hybrid retrieval combines lexical and dense signals.</p>\
                          <h2>Grounding</h2><p>Every claim must cite an evidence span.</p></body></html>"
                            .to_vec(),
                    ),
                    "/doc.pdf" => (200, "application/pdf", b"%PDF-1.4\n%fake\n".to_vec()),
                    "/redirect" => (302, "text/plain", b"".to_vec()),
                    "/loop" => (302, "text/plain", b"".to_vec()),
                    "/big" => (200, "text/plain", vec![b'x'; 3 * 1024 * 1024]),
                    "/missing" => (404, "text/plain", b"nope".to_vec()),
                    _ => (200, "text/plain", b"plain text body about widgets".to_vec()),
                };
                let location = match path.as_str() {
                    "/redirect" => "Location: /page\r\n",
                    "/loop" => "Location: /loop\r\n",
                    _ => "",
                };
                let head = format!(
                    "HTTP/1.1 {} X\r\nContent-Type: {}\r\n{}Content-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n",
                    status, ctype, location, body.len()
                );
                let _ = stream.write_all(head.as_bytes());
                let _ = stream.write_all(&body);
                let _ = stream.flush();
            }
        });
        let out = f(port);
        // let the thread finish its accept loop
        drop(handle);
        std::env::remove_var("FORGE_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE");
        out
    }

    #[test]
    fn transport_is_present_in_this_image() {
        assert!(transport_available(), "curl must be available for URL ingestion");
    }

    #[test]
    fn fetches_html_and_classifies_it() {
        with_server(|port| {
            let got = fetch(&format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}/page", port)).expect("fetch");
            assert_eq!(got.status, 200);
            assert_eq!(got.media_type(), "text/html");
            assert_eq!(got.ingest_kind(), "html");
            assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&got.body).contains("Hybrid retrieval"));
            assert_eq!(got.canonical_url, format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}/page", port));
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn follows_redirects_hop_by_hop_and_records_them() {
        with_server(|port| {
            let got = fetch(&format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}/redirect", port)).expect("fetch");
            assert_eq!(got.status, 200);
            assert!(got.final_url.ends_with("/page"), "final: {}", got.final_url);
            assert_eq!(got.redirects.len(), 1);
            assert_eq!(got.redirects[0].0, 302);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_a_redirect_loop() {
        with_server(|port| {
            let err = fetch(&format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}/loop", port)).unwrap_err();
            assert!(matches!(err, FetchError::Rejected(_)), "{:?}", err);
            assert!(err.message().contains("redirects"), "{}", err.message());
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn enforces_the_size_cap() {
        with_server(|port| {
            let err = fetch_with_limits(&format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}/big", port), 1024 * 1024)
                .unwrap_err();
            assert!(matches!(err, FetchError::Limit(_)), "{:?}", err);
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_non_success_status() {
        with_server(|port| {
            let err = fetch(&format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}/missing", port)).unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.message().contains("404"), "{}", err.message());
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn detects_pdf_by_magic_even_without_a_content_type() {
        with_server(|port| {
            let got = fetch(&format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}/doc.pdf", port)).expect("fetch");
            assert_eq!(got.ingest_kind(), "pdf");
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn private_addresses_are_refused_when_the_override_is_off() {
        // holds SERVER_LOCK because it mutates the same process-global flag
        let _guard = SERVER_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        std::env::remove_var("FORGE_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE");
        assert!(!security::allow_private());
        let err = fetch("http://127.0.0.1:9/nope").unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(err, FetchError::Rejected(_)), "{:?}", err);
        // and the classic metadata endpoint
        let err = fetch("http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/").unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(err, FetchError::Rejected(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_bad_schemes_and_credentials() {
        assert!(matches!(fetch("file:///etc/passwd").unwrap_err(), FetchError::Rejected(_)));
        assert!(matches!(fetch("gopher://x/").unwrap_err(), FetchError::Rejected(_)));
        let err = fetch("https://user:pass@example.com/").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.message().contains("credentials"), "{}", err.message());
    }

    #[test]
    fn canonicalization_matches_equivalent_urls() {
        let a = canonicalize("HTTP://Example.COM:80/a/b#frag").unwrap();
        let b = canonicalize("http://example.com/a/b").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a, b, "scheme/host case, default port and fragment must normalise");
        let c = canonicalize("https://example.com").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c, "https://example.com/");
        // query strings are preserved (they often select different content)
        assert_ne!(
            canonicalize("https://e.com/x?a=1").unwrap(),
            canonicalize("https://e.com/x?a=2").unwrap()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reads_bodies_and_ignores_short_reads() {
        // a guard against regressing to a fixed-size read
        with_server(|port| {
            let got = fetch(&format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}/page", port)).expect("fetch");
            let mut buf = Vec::new();
            got.body.as_slice().read_to_end(&mut buf).unwrap();
            assert!(buf.len() > 100);
        });
    }
}
```
