## `crates/forge-core/src/grounded.rs`

```rust
//! Grounded answering with verified citations and explicit abstention.
//!
//! Default engine is **extractive**: it composes an answer only out of retrieved
//! source passages, so every sentence is traceable to evidence and it cannot
//! hallucinate. That is a deliberate choice, not a limitation hidden from the
//! user: cloud model providers need HTTPS + network + API keys, none of which
//! this environment provides (docs/DECISIONS.md D4, docs/UNKNOWN_AND_LIMITATIONS.md).
//!
//! The `Answerer` trait is the seam where a model-backed provider plugs in later;
//! citation validation stays in this module so an LLM's output is checked the
//! same way.

use crate::domain::{Chunk, Citation, Locator, Source};
use crate::retrieve;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Answer {
    pub text: String,
    pub citations: Vec<Citation>,
    pub abstained: bool,
    pub engine: String,
    pub coverage: usize,
}

/// How the verified evidence is presented. Style never changes *which* evidence is used ‚Äî
/// only how it is laid out ‚Äî so every style is checkable against the same citations.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Style {
    /// Quoted lines with numbered markers and a closing provenance note (the default).
    Evidence,
    /// One short paragraph of quotations, for skimming.
    Concise,
    /// Each quotation followed by its source title and locator, plus a sources-consulted line.
    Detailed,
}

/// How much verified evidence to include. The number is a real citation count, not a
/// prose hint: a shorter answer cites fewer passages.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Length {
    Brief,
    Standard,
    Thorough,
}

impl Style {
    pub fn parse(raw: &str) -> Option<Style> {
        match raw.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "" | "evidence" => Some(Style::Evidence),
            "concise" | "short" => Some(Style::Concise),
            "detailed" | "explained" => Some(Style::Detailed),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Style::Evidence => "evidence",
            Style::Concise => "concise",
            Style::Detailed => "detailed",
        }
    }
}

impl Length {
    pub fn parse(raw: &str) -> Option<Length> {
        match raw.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
            "" | "standard" => Some(Length::Standard),
            "brief" | "shorter" => Some(Length::Brief),
            "thorough" | "longer" => Some(Length::Thorough),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Length::Brief => "brief",
            Length::Standard => "standard",
            Length::Thorough => "thorough",
        }
    }
    /// Maximum citations this length may use.
    pub fn max_citations(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Length::Brief => 1,
            Length::Standard => 2,
            Length::Thorough => 4,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AnswerOptions {
    pub style: Style,
    pub length: Length,
}

impl Default for AnswerOptions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        AnswerOptions { style: Style::Evidence, length: Length::Standard }
    }
}

/// Minimum BM25 score for a passage to count as evidence at all.
pub const EVIDENCE_FLOOR: f64 = 0.35;

/// Minimum share of the question's content words that the chosen sentence must
/// contain. Queries with only one or two content words require half of them.
pub const SENTENCE_OVERLAP_FLOOR: f64 = 0.30;

pub fn answer(question: &str, chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], max_citations: usize) -> Answer {
    answer_limited(question, chunks, sources, max_citations, Style::Evidence)
}

/// Answer with an explicit presentation style and citation budget.
pub fn answer_with(
    question: &str,
    chunks: &[Chunk],
    sources: &[Source],
    opts: AnswerOptions,
) -> Answer {
    answer_limited(question, chunks, sources, opts.length.max_citations(), opts.style)
}

fn answer_limited(
    question: &str,
    chunks: &[Chunk],
    sources: &[Source],
    max_citations: usize,
    style: Style,
) -> Answer {
    let hits = retrieve::search(chunks, question, 12);
    let strong: Vec<_> = hits.into_iter().filter(|h| h.score >= EVIDENCE_FLOOR).collect();

    if strong.is_empty() {
        return Answer {
            text: abstain_text(question),
            citations: Vec::new(),
            abstained: true,
            engine: "extractive".into(),
            coverage: 0,
        };
    }

    // Collect the best sentence per chunk, then keep only sentences that actually
    // share enough of the question's content words. A chunk can score on a single
    // word while its best sentence is unrelated; citing that would be noise.
    let query_terms = retrieve::terms(question).len();
    let min_overlap = if query_terms >= 3 { SENTENCE_OVERLAP_FLOOR } else { 0.5 };
    let mut candidates: Vec<(f64, f64, usize, String)> = Vec::new();
    for hit in strong.iter() {
        let chunk = &chunks[hit.chunk_index];
        if let Some((overlap, sentence)) = retrieve::scored_sentences(&chunk.text, question, 3)
            .into_iter()
            .find(|(o, _)| *o >= min_overlap)
        {
            // Guard: a quote must be literally present in its chunk.
            if !chunk.text.contains(sentence.trim()) {
                continue;
            }
            candidates.push((overlap, hit.score, hit.chunk_index, sentence));
        }
    }
    candidates.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0)
            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
            .then(b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
    });

    let mut citations: Vec<Citation> = Vec::new();
    let mut sentences: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut seen_quotes: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (overlap, score, chunk_index, quote) in candidates {
        if citations.len() >= max_citations {
            break;
        }
        let chunk = &chunks[chunk_index];
        let trimmed = quote.trim().to_string();
        if seen_quotes.iter().any(|q| q == &trimmed) {
            continue;
        }
        seen_quotes.push(trimmed.clone());
        let source_title = sources
            .iter()
            .find(|s| s.id == chunk.source_id)
            .map(|s| s.title.clone())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown source".into());
        let marker = format!("[{}]", citations.len() + 1);
        let citation = Citation {
            citation_id: format!("c{}", citations.len() + 1),
            source_id: chunk.source_id.clone(),
            chunk_id: chunk.id.clone(),
            quote: trimmed.clone(),
            locator: chunk.locator.clone(),
            score,
            source_title,
        };
        let _ = overlap;
        sentences.push(format!("{}{}", citation.quote, marker));
        citations.push(citation);
    }

    if citations.is_empty() {
        return Answer {
            text: abstain_text(question),
            citations: Vec::new(),
            abstained: true,
            engine: "extractive".into(),
            coverage: 0,
        };
    }

    let distinct_sources = {
        let mut ids: Vec<&str> = citations.iter().map(|c| c.source_id.as_str()).collect();
        ids.sort_unstable();
        ids.dedup();
        ids.len()
    };

    let mut text = String::new();
    match style {
        Style::Evidence => {
            if distinct_sources > 1 {
                text.push_str(&format!(
                    "From {} sources, the passages that bear on this question are:\n\n",
                    distinct_sources
                ));
            } else {
                text.push_str("Based on the selected sources:\n\n");
            }
            for s in &sentences {
                text.push_str("- ");
                text.push_str(s);
                text.push('\n');
            }
            text.push_str(&format!(
                "\nEvery statement above is quoted from the notebook's evidence ({} citation{}). \
                 Forge does not add outside knowledge in grounded mode.",
                citations.len(),
                if citations.len() == 1 { "" } else { "s" }
            ));
        }
        Style::Concise => {
            // same quotations, laid out as one paragraph; no framing claim is added
            text.push_str(&sentences.join(" "));
            text.push_str(&format!(
                "\n\n‚Äî quoted from {} passage{} of the notebook's evidence.",
                citations.len(),
                if citations.len() == 1 { "" } else { "s" }
            ));
        }
        Style::Detailed => {
            text.push_str(&format!(
                "{} passage{} on this question. Each is quoted below with its location; \
                 nothing is paraphrased.\n",
                citations.len(),
                if citations.len() == 1 { " bears" } else { "s bear" }
            ));
            for (i, c) in citations.iter().enumerate() {
                text.push_str(&format!(
                    "\n{}. ‚Äú{}‚Äù\n   ‚Äî {} ¬∑ {}\n",
                    i + 1,
                    c.quote,
                    c.source_title,
                    c.locator.human()
                ));
            }
            let mut used: Vec<&str> = citations.iter().map(|c| c.source_title.as_str()).collect();
            used.dedup();
            text.push_str(&format!(
                "\nSources consulted: {}. Quotation only ‚Äî Forge adds no outside knowledge while \
                 grounded mode is on.",
                used.join("; ")
            ));
        }
    }

    Answer {
        text,
        coverage: citations.len(),
        citations,
        abstained: false,
        engine: "extractive".into(),
    }
}

fn abstain_text(question: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "I can't answer that from the selected sources. No passage in the notebook's evidence \
         matches \"{}\" closely enough to support an answer.\n\n\
         What you can do: select more sources, add a source that covers this topic, or rephrase \
         using terms that appear in the documents. Forge will not answer from outside knowledge \
         while grounded mode is on.",
        question.trim()
    )
}

/// Verify that every citation points at real evidence in the same notebook.
/// Used both for our own answers and for any future model-backed answer.
pub fn validate_citations(citations: &[Citation], chunks: &[Chunk]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut problems = Vec::new();
    for c in citations {
        match chunks.iter().find(|k| k.id == c.chunk_id) {
            None => problems.push(format!("{}: chunk {} does not exist", c.citation_id, c.chunk_id)),
            Some(chunk) => {
                if chunk.source_id != c.source_id {
                    problems.push(format!(
                        "{}: chunk belongs to source {}, citation claims {}",
                        c.citation_id, chunk.source_id, c.source_id
                    ));
                }
                if !chunk.text.contains(c.quote.trim()) && !c.quote.trim().is_empty() {
                    problems.push(format!(
                        "{}: quote is not present verbatim in the cited chunk",
                        c.citation_id
                    ));
                }
                let same_locator = chunk.locator.page == c.locator.page
                    && chunk.locator.paragraph == c.locator.paragraph
                    && chunk.locator.row == c.locator.row;
                if !same_locator {
                    problems.push(format!("{}: locator does not match the chunk", c.citation_id));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    problems
}

/// A location the UI can jump to when a citation is clicked.
pub fn citation_target(citation: &Citation) -> crate::json::Value {
    crate::obj! {
        "source_id" => citation.source_id.as_str(),
        "chunk_id" => citation.chunk_id.as_str(),
        "locator" => citation.locator.to_json(),
        "label" => citation.locator.human(),
    }
}

pub fn locator_from(kind: &str, index: u32) -> Locator {
    match kind {
        "page" => Locator::page(index, 0, 0),
        "row" => Locator::row(index, 0, 0),
        _ => Locator::paragraph(index, 0, 0),
    }
}

/// True when the question contains no content words at all.
pub fn is_degenerate_question(q: &str) -> bool {
    retrieve::terms(q).is_empty()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::domain::Locator;

    fn src(id: &str, title: &str) -> Source {
        Source {
            id: id.into(),
            notebook_id: "nb".into(),
            title: title.into(),
            kind: "text".into(),
            origin: String::new(),
            byte_len: 10,
            status: "ready".into(),
            error: String::new(),
            warnings: vec![],
            added_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z".into(),
            page_count: 0,
            chunk_count: 1,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    fn chunk(id: &str, sid: &str, text: &str, page: u32) -> Chunk {
        Chunk {
            id: id.into(),
            source_id: sid.into(),
            notebook_id: "nb".into(),
            ordinal: 0,
            text: text.into(),
            locator: Locator::page(page, 0, text.len() as u32),
        }
    }

    fn three_passage_corpus() -> (Vec<Chunk>, Vec<Source>) {
        let chunks = vec![
            chunk(
                "k1",
                "s1",
                "The retrieval pipeline ranks candidate spans with BM25 and then builds bounded model context. Ranking happens before any generation step.",
                1,
            ),
            chunk(
                "k2",
                "s2",
                "Candidate spans are ranked by BM25 so that the model only sees context that matched the question. Ranking is deterministic and testable.",
                2,
            ),
            chunk(
                "k3",
                "s1",
                "A bounded context window keeps retrieval ranking honest: spans compete for a fixed budget. Retrieval evidence is quoted verbatim.",
                3,
            ),
        ];
        (chunks, vec![src("s1", "Retrieval notes"), src("s2", "Pipeline paper")])
    }

    #[test]
    fn length_changes_how_many_passages_are_cited() {
        let (chunks, sources) = three_passage_corpus();
        let mut counts = Vec::new();
        for length in [Length::Brief, Length::Standard, Length::Thorough] {
            let a = answer_with(
                "how are candidate spans ranked by BM25 for retrieval",
                &chunks,
                &sources,
                AnswerOptions { style: Style::Evidence, length },
            );
            assert!(!a.abstained, "{:?}: {}", length, a.text);
            counts.push(a.citations.len());
        }
        assert_eq!(counts[0], 1, "brief means one citation");
        assert!(counts[1] <= 2 && counts[1] >= counts[0], "standard: {:?}", counts);
        assert!(counts[2] >= counts[1], "thorough cites at least as much: {:?}", counts);
        assert_eq!(Length::Brief.max_citations(), 1);
        assert_eq!(Length::Thorough.max_citations(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn style_changes_presentation_and_never_the_evidence() {
        let (chunks, sources) = three_passage_corpus();
        let q = "how are candidate spans ranked by BM25 for retrieval";
        let opts = |style| AnswerOptions { style, length: Length::Standard };
        let evidence = answer_with(q, &chunks, &sources, opts(Style::Evidence));
        let concise = answer_with(q, &chunks, &sources, opts(Style::Concise));
        let detailed = answer_with(q, &chunks, &sources, opts(Style::Detailed));

        // identical evidence: same citations, same order, same quotes
        let quotes = |a: &Answer| a.citations.iter().map(|c| (c.chunk_id.clone(), c.quote.clone())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        assert_eq!(quotes(&evidence), quotes(&concise), "style must not change the evidence");
        assert_eq!(quotes(&evidence), quotes(&detailed), "style must not change the evidence");

        // but the rendering is visibly different
        assert!(evidence.text.contains("\n- "), "evidence style lists quotes");
        assert!(!concise.text.contains("\n- "), "concise has no bullet list");
        assert!(concise.text.len() < evidence.text.len(), "concise must be shorter");
        assert!(detailed.text.contains("Sources consulted:"), "{}", detailed.text);
        assert!(detailed.text.contains(&detailed.citations[0].locator.human()), "detailed shows locations");
        assert!(detailed.text.contains(&detailed.citations[0].source_title), "detailed names the source");

        // every style stays verifiable: quotes are in their chunks, citations resolve
        for a in [&evidence, &concise, &detailed] {
            assert!(validate_citations(&a.citations, &chunks).is_empty());
            for c in &a.citations {
                let chunk = chunks.iter().find(|k| k.id == c.chunk_id).unwrap();
                assert!(chunk.text.contains(&c.quote));
                assert!(a.text.contains(&c.quote), "each quote appears in the rendered text");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn unknown_style_and_length_values_are_rejected() {
        assert_eq!(Style::parse("bullets"), None);
        assert_eq!(Style::parse("Evidence"), Some(Style::Evidence));
        assert_eq!(Style::parse(""), Some(Style::Evidence));
        assert_eq!(Length::parse("long"), None);
        assert_eq!(Length::parse("thorough"), Some(Length::Thorough));
        assert_eq!(Length::parse("shorter"), Some(Length::Brief));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_styled_answer_still_abstains_without_evidence() {
        let (chunks, sources) = three_passage_corpus();
        let a = answer_with(
            "what is the capital of France",
            &chunks,
            &sources,
            AnswerOptions { style: Style::Concise, length: Length::Thorough },
        );
        assert!(a.abstained);
        assert!(a.citations.is_empty());
        assert!(!a.text.contains("Sources consulted"), "no skeleton answer when abstaining");
    }

    #[test]
    fn answers_with_a_valid_citation() {
        let chunks = vec![chunk(
            "k1",
            "s1",
            "The retrieval pipeline ranks candidate spans with BM25 and then builds bounded model context.",
            4,
        )];
        let sources = vec![src("s1", "Design notes")];
        let a = answer("how does the retrieval pipeline rank spans", &chunks, &sources, 3);
        assert!(!a.abstained);
        assert_eq!(a.citations.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(a.citations[0].locator.page, Some(4));
        assert!(a.text.contains("[1]"));
        assert!(a.citations[0].quote.to_lowercase().contains("retrieval"));
        assert!(validate_citations(&a.citations, &chunks).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn abstains_when_evidence_is_absent() {
        let chunks = vec![chunk("k1", "s1", "The office coffee machine is on the second floor.", 1)];
        let sources = vec![src("s1", "Office")];
        let a = answer("what is the capital of Mongolia", &chunks, &sources, 3);
        assert!(a.abstained);
        assert!(a.citations.is_empty());
        assert!(a.text.contains("can't answer"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn abstains_on_empty_notebook() {
        let a = answer("anything at all", &[], &[], 3);
        assert!(a.abstained);
    }

    #[test]
    fn synthesises_across_two_sources() {
        let chunks = vec![
            chunk("k1", "s1", "Citation validation rejects quotes that are not verbatim evidence.", 2),
            chunk("k2", "s2", "Every citation must be validated against the evidence store before display.", 7),
        ];
        let sources = vec![src("s1", "A"), src("s2", "B")];
        let a = answer("citation evidence validated quotes", &chunks, &sources, 4);
        assert!(!a.abstained);
        assert_eq!(a.citations.len(), 2);
        assert!(a.text.contains("2 sources"));
        let pages: Vec<u32> = a.citations.iter().filter_map(|c| c.locator.page).collect();
        assert!(pages.contains(&2) && pages.contains(&7));
    }

    #[test]
    fn boilerplate_in_a_scoring_chunk_is_not_cited() {
        // The chunk matches on its first line, but the sentence chosen must still
        // relate to the question; unrelated lines in the same chunk must not appear.
        let chunks = vec![chunk(
            "k1",
            "s1",
            "Evidence floor tuning matters.\nDocument title page.\nUnrelated legal boilerplate follows here for filler.",
            1,
        )];
        let sources = vec![src("s1", "Doc")];
        let a = answer("how is the evidence floor tuned", &chunks, &sources, 3);
        assert!(!a.abstained);
        assert_eq!(a.citations.len(), 1);
        assert!(a.citations[0].quote.to_lowercase().contains("evidence floor"));
        assert!(!a.text.to_lowercase().contains("legal boilerplate"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn citation_numbers_are_contiguous() {
        let chunks = vec![
            chunk("k1", "s1", "Cite validation rejects fabricated quotes immediately.", 1),
            chunk("k2", "s2", "Fabricated quotes fail validation every single time.", 2),
        ];
        let sources = vec![src("s1", "A"), src("s2", "B")];
        let a = answer("fabricated quotes validation", &chunks, &sources, 4);
        let nums: Vec<usize> = a
            .citations
            .iter()
            .map(|c| c.citation_id.trim_start_matches('c').parse().unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(nums, (1..=nums.len()).collect::<Vec<_>>());
        assert!(a.text.contains("[2]") || nums.len() == 1);
    }

    #[test]
    fn validator_catches_fabricated_quotes_and_ids() {
        let chunks = vec![chunk("k1", "s1", "Real evidence text about retrieval.", 1)];
        let fake = Citation {
            citation_id: "c1".into(),
            source_id: "s1".into(),
            chunk_id: "ghost".into(),
            quote: "invented".into(),
            locator: Locator::page(1, 0, 1),
            score: 1.0,
            source_title: "A".into(),
        };
        assert!(validate_citations(&[fake], &chunks)[0].contains("does not exist"));

        let wrong_quote = Citation {
            citation_id: "c2".into(),
            source_id: "s1".into(),
            chunk_id: "k1".into(),
            quote: "text that is not there".into(),
            locator: Locator::page(1, 0, 1),
            score: 1.0,
            source_title: "A".into(),
        };
        assert!(validate_citations(&[wrong_quote], &chunks)[0].contains("not present verbatim"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn degenerate_question_is_detected() {
        assert!(is_degenerate_question("the of and"));
        assert!(!is_degenerate_question("what is BM25"));
    }
}
```

## `crates/forge-core/src/guide.rs`

```rust
//! Source Guide: a per-source orientation built **only** from the source itself.
//!
//! The reference product shows a guide/summary when a source is opened. Forge cannot
//! reach a model provider (no TLS client, no key), so pretending to summarise with an
//! LLM would be a lie. What this module produces instead is a deterministic,
//! extractive guide:
//!
//! * every sentence in the summary is **quoted verbatim** from one chunk and carries
//!   that chunk's id and human locator, so the user can jump to it and check;
//! * topics are term frequencies with the chunk where each first appears;
//! * the outline comes from real structure the parser recorded (sections, sheets,
//!   pages), never from guesswork;
//! * suggested questions are templates over observed topics, labelled as suggestions.
//!
//! The output always says `generated_by: "extractive"` and `model: null`. Nothing here
//! paraphrases, and nothing is inferred about the source's meaning.

use crate::domain::{Chunk, Source};
use crate::json::Value;
use crate::obj;
use crate::retrieve;
use crate::tables::Table;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// Default shape of a guide. Small on purpose: a guide that restates the whole source is
/// just the source again.
pub const MAX_SUMMARY_SENTENCES: usize = 5;
pub const MAX_TOPICS: usize = 8;
pub const MAX_QUESTIONS: usize = 5;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct GuideSentence {
    pub text: String,
    pub chunk_id: String,
    pub locator: String,
    pub ordinal: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct GuideTopic {
    /// Surface form shown to the user (most frequent original casing). For a phrase this
    /// is the words joined, e.g. "Calvin cycle".
    pub term: String,
    /// Stemmed words the term is made of (one for a single word, two for a phrase).
    pub stems: Vec<String>,
    pub count: usize,
    /// Chunks containing the term.
    pub chunks: usize,
    pub first_chunk_id: String,
    pub first_locator: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Guide {
    pub source_id: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub kind: String,
    pub headline: Option<GuideSentence>,
    pub summary: Vec<GuideSentence>,
    pub topics: Vec<GuideTopic>,
    pub outline: Vec<String>,
    pub questions: Vec<String>,
    pub word_count: usize,
    pub chunk_count: usize,
    pub table_count: usize,
    pub table_row_count: usize,
    pub warnings: Vec<String>,
}

impl Guide {
    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
        let sentence_json = |s: &GuideSentence| {
            obj! {
                "text" => s.text.as_str(),
                "chunk_id" => s.chunk_id.as_str(),
                "locator" => s.locator.as_str(),
                "ordinal" => s.ordinal as u64,
            }
        };
        obj! {
            "source_id" => self.source_id.as_str(),
            "title" => self.title.as_str(),
            "kind" => self.kind.as_str(),
            // Honesty fields, read by the UI: this text is quoted, not generated.
            "generated_by" => "extractive",
            "model" => Value::Null,
            "deterministic" => true,
            "headline" => match &self.headline { Some(s) => sentence_json(s), None => Value::Null },
            "summary" => Value::Arr(self.summary.iter().map(sentence_json).collect()),
            "topics" => Value::Arr(self.topics.iter().map(|t| obj! {
                "term" => t.term.as_str(),
                "count" => t.count as u64,
                "chunks" => t.chunks as u64,
                "chunk_id" => t.first_chunk_id.as_str(),
                "locator" => t.first_locator.as_str(),
            }).collect()),
            "outline" => Value::Arr(self.outline.iter().map(|o| Value::from(o.as_str())).collect()),
            "questions" => Value::Arr(self.questions.iter().map(|q| Value::from(q.as_str())).collect()),
            "stats" => obj! {
                "words" => self.word_count as u64,
                "chunks" => self.chunk_count as u64,
                "tables" => self.table_count as u64,
                "table_rows" => self.table_row_count as u64,
            },
            "warnings" => Value::Arr(self.warnings.iter().map(|w| Value::from(w.as_str())).collect()),
        }
    }
}

/// A sentence candidate: score, chunk index, position inside the chunk, text.
struct Candidate {
    score: f64,
    chunk_idx: usize,
    text: String,
}

fn jaccard(a: &[String], b: &[String]) -> f64 {
    if a.is_empty() || b.is_empty() {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let mut inter = 0usize;
    for x in a {
        if b.contains(x) {
            inter += 1;
        }
    }
    let union = a.len() + b.len() - inter;
    if union == 0 {
        0.0
    } else {
        inter as f64 / union as f64
    }
}

/// Choose the surface form to display for a stemmed term: most frequent original casing,
/// preferring a capitalised form when counts tie (so "BM25" beats "bm25").
fn surface_forms(chunks: &[Chunk]) -> BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, usize>> {
    let mut forms: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, usize>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for c in chunks {
        for raw in retrieve::tokenize(&c.text) {
            if raw.len() < 3 {
                continue;
            }
            let stem = retrieve::stem(&raw);
            *forms.entry(stem).or_default().entry(raw.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
        }
    }
    forms
}

/// Count content words (stemmed) and adjacent two-word phrases, with chunk coverage.
fn ngram_counts(chunks: &[Chunk], n: usize) -> BTreeMap<String, (usize, usize)> {
    // stem-key -> (total occurrences, chunks containing it)
    let mut totals: BTreeMap<String, (usize, usize)> = BTreeMap::new();
    for c in chunks {
        let stems: Vec<String> = retrieve::terms(&c.text).into_iter().map(|t| retrieve::stem(&t)).collect();
        let mut seen: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        for i in 0..stems.len() {
            if i + n > stems.len() {
                break;
            }
            let key = stems[i..i + n].join(" ");
            let e = totals.entry(key.clone()).or_insert((0, 0));
            e.0 += 1;
            if !seen.contains(&key) {
                seen.push(key);
                e.1 += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    totals
}

fn surface_of(stem: &str, forms: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, usize>>) -> String {
    forms
        .get(stem)
        .and_then(|m| m.iter().max_by(|a, b| a.1.cmp(b.1).then_with(|| b.0.cmp(a.0))).map(|(k, _)| k.clone()))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| stem.to_string())
}

/// Topics for display, and the unigram weights used to score sentences.
///
/// A phrase ("calvin cycle") is preferred over its parts when it recurs: a guide that
/// lists "calvin" and "cycle" separately is less useful than one that lists the phrase.
fn topic_terms(chunks: &[Chunk]) -> (Vec<GuideTopic>, Vec<(String, f64)>) {
    let forms = surface_forms(chunks);
    let min_chunks = if chunks.len() > 1 { 2 } else { 1 };
    let unigrams = ngram_counts(chunks, 1);
    let bigrams = ngram_counts(chunks, 2);

    let mut topics: Vec<GuideTopic> = Vec::new();
    let mut absorbed: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut phrases: Vec<(String, usize, usize, Vec<String>)> = Vec::new();
    for (key, (count, chunk_count)) in &bigrams {
        if *chunk_count < min_chunks || *count < 2 {
            continue;
        }
        let parts: Vec<String> = key.split(' ').map(|x| x.to_string()).collect();
        // a phrase made of one-word parts that never occur alone would be noise
        if parts.iter().any(|p| p.len() < 3) {
            continue;
        }
        phrases.push((key.clone(), *count, *chunk_count, parts));
    }
    phrases.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1).then_with(|| a.0.cmp(&b.0)));
    phrases.truncate(4);

    for (key, count, chunk_count, parts) in &phrases {
        let surface: Vec<String> = parts.iter().map(|p| surface_of(p, &forms)).collect();
        for p in parts {
            // the phrase usually accounts for this word; listing both would be repetition
            if let Some((uni_count, _)) = unigrams.get(p) {
                if count * 2 >= *uni_count {
                    absorbed.push(p.clone());
                }
            }
        }
        topics.push(GuideTopic {
            term: surface.join(" "),
            stems: parts.clone(),
            count: *count,
            chunks: *chunk_count,
            first_chunk_id: String::new(),
            first_locator: String::new(),
        });
        let _ = key;
    }

    for (stem, (count, chunk_count)) in &unigrams {
        if *chunk_count < min_chunks || stem.len() < 3 || absorbed.contains(stem) {
            continue;
        }
        topics.push(GuideTopic {
            term: surface_of(stem, &forms),
            stems: vec![stem.clone()],
            count: *count,
            chunks: *chunk_count,
            first_chunk_id: String::new(),
            first_locator: String::new(),
        });
    }

    topics.sort_by(|a, b| b.count.cmp(&a.count).then_with(|| a.term.cmp(&b.term)));
    topics.truncate(MAX_TOPICS);

    // sentence scoring keeps every unigram, including ones absorbed into a phrase
    let mut weights: Vec<(String, f64)> = unigrams
        .iter()
        .filter(|(stem, (count, chunk_count))| *chunk_count >= min_chunks && stem.len() >= 3 && *count > 0)
        .map(|(stem, (count, _))| (stem.clone(), (*count as f64).sqrt()))
        .collect();
    weights.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal).then_with(|| a.0.cmp(&b.0)));
    (topics, weights)
}

/// Does this chunk mention the topic (all words of a phrase, in any order)?
fn mentions(chunk: &Chunk, topic: &GuideTopic) -> bool {
    let stems: Vec<String> = retrieve::terms(&chunk.text).into_iter().map(|t| retrieve::stem(&t)).collect();
    topic.stems.iter().all(|want| stems.contains(want))
}

fn sentences_in(chunk: &Chunk) -> Vec<String> {
    retrieve::split_sentences(&chunk.text)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|s| {
            let words = s.split_whitespace().count();
            (4..=60).contains(&words)
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Rank sentences by how much of the source's core vocabulary they carry, but keep them
/// in document order in the output so the guide reads like the source, not like a ranking.
fn ranked_sentences(chunks: &[Chunk], weights: &[(String, f64)]) -> Vec<Candidate> {
    let weight: BTreeMap<String, f64> = weights.iter().cloned().collect();

    let mut out: Vec<Candidate> = Vec::new();
    for (idx, c) in chunks.iter().enumerate() {
        for s in sentences_in(c) {
            let toks: Vec<String> = retrieve::terms(&s).into_iter().map(|t| retrieve::stem(&t)).collect();
            if toks.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut score = 0.0f64;
            let mut covered = 0usize;
            for t in &toks {
                if let Some(w) = weight.get(t) {
                    score += w;
                    covered += 1;
                }
            }
            if covered == 0 {
                continue; // a sentence sharing nothing with the source's vocabulary is noise
            }
            let distinct: Vec<String> = {
                let mut d = toks.clone();
                d.sort();
                d.dedup();
                d
            };
            // length normalisation + a bonus for covering many distinct core terms
            score *= 1.0 + (distinct.len() as f64).sqrt() / 4.0;
            score /= (toks.len() as f64).sqrt();
            out.push(Candidate { score, chunk_idx: idx, text: s });
        }
    }
    out.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b.score
            .partial_cmp(&a.score)
            .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
            .then(a.chunk_idx.cmp(&b.chunk_idx))
            .then(a.text.cmp(&b.text))
    });
    out
}

fn pick_summary(chunks: &[Chunk], candidates: Vec<Candidate>, limit: usize) -> Vec<GuideSentence> {
    let mut chosen: Vec<(u32, usize, GuideSentence)> = Vec::new();
    let mut seen: Vec<Vec<String>> = Vec::new();
    for cand in candidates {
        if chosen.len() >= limit {
            break;
        }
        let toks: Vec<String> = retrieve::terms(&cand.text).into_iter().map(|t| retrieve::stem(&t)).collect();
        // near-duplicates make a summary look padded; one paraphrase per idea is enough
        if seen.iter().any(|s| jaccard(s, &toks) > 0.55) {
            continue;
        }
        seen.push(toks);
        let c = &chunks[cand.chunk_idx];
        let at = c.text.find(&cand.text).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
        chosen.push((
            c.ordinal,
            at,
            GuideSentence {
                text: cand.text,
                chunk_id: c.id.clone(),
                locator: c.locator.human(),
                ordinal: c.ordinal,
            },
        ));
    }
    // read in document order: a score ranking jumps around and reads like a list of
    // unrelated lines; the source's own order keeps the meaning intact
    chosen.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0).then(a.1.cmp(&b.1)));
    chosen.into_iter().map(|(_, _, s)| s).collect()
}

/// Real structure the parser recorded: sections/slides, then sheets, then pages.
fn outline_of(source: &Source, chunks: &[Chunk], tables: &[Table]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for c in chunks {
        if let Some(section) = &c.locator.section {
            if !section.trim().is_empty() && !out.iter().any(|x| x.eq_ignore_ascii_case(section)) {
                out.push(section.clone());
            }
        }
    }
    for t in tables {
        out.push(format!(
            "sheet {} ({} row{}{})",
            t.sheet,
            t.rows.len(),
            if t.rows.len() == 1 { "" } else { "s" },
            if t.hidden { ", hidden" } else { "" }
        ));
    }
    if out.is_empty() && source.page_count > 1 {
        out.push(format!("{} pages", source.page_count));
    }
    out.truncate(40);
    out
}

fn questions_for(topics: &[GuideTopic], tables: &[Table]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for t in tables.iter().filter(|t| !t.hidden) {
        // suggest a computation only when a numeric column actually exists
        for (i, header) in t.headers.iter().enumerate() {
            let numeric = t
                .rows
                .iter()
                .filter(|r| t.cell(r, i).map(|c| c.is_number()).unwrap_or(false))
                .count();
            if numeric >= 2 && out.len() < MAX_QUESTIONS {
                out.push(format!("What is the total {} in {}?", header, t.sheet));
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    for topic in topics {
        if out.len() >= MAX_QUESTIONS {
            break;
        }
        out.push(format!("What does {} say about {}?", "this source", topic.term));
    }
    out.truncate(MAX_QUESTIONS);
    out
}

/// Build the guide for one source.
///
/// Returns an error when there is nothing to orient the user in ‚Äî an empty guide would be
/// worse than no guide.
pub fn build(source: &Source, chunks: &[Chunk], tables: &[Table]) -> Result<Guide, String> {
    let mut own: Vec<Chunk> = chunks.iter().filter(|c| c.source_id == source.id).cloned().collect();
    own.sort_by_key(|c| c.ordinal);
    if own.is_empty() {
        return Err("this source has no indexed passages yet".into());
    }
    let mine: Vec<Table> = tables.iter().filter(|t| t.source_id == source.id).cloned().collect();

    let word_count = own.iter().map(|c| retrieve::tokenize(&c.text).len()).sum();
    let (mut topics, weights) = topic_terms(&own);
    for t in topics.iter_mut() {
        if let Some(c) = own.iter().find(|c| mentions(c, t)) {
            t.first_chunk_id = c.id.clone();
            t.first_locator = c.locator.human();
        }
    }

    let candidates = ranked_sentences(&own, &weights);
    let mut summary = pick_summary(&own, candidates, MAX_SUMMARY_SENTENCES);
    // The highest-ranked line is the headline; the rest are the summary.
    let headline = if summary.is_empty() { None } else { Some(summary.remove(0)) };

    let mut warnings: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    if own.len() == 1 {
        warnings.push("single passage: topics cannot be cross-checked across the source".into());
    }
    if word_count < 40 {
        warnings.push("very short source: the guide is close to quoting it in full".into());
    }
    let mut guide = Guide {
        source_id: source.id.clone(),
        title: source.title.clone(),
        kind: source.kind.clone(),
        headline,
        summary,
        topics,
        outline: outline_of(source, &own, &mine),
        questions: Vec::new(),
        word_count,
        chunk_count: own.len(),
        table_count: mine.len(),
        table_row_count: mine.iter().map(|t| t.rows.len()).sum(),
        warnings: Vec::new(),
    };
    guide.questions = questions_for(&guide.topics, &mine);
    for w in source.warnings.iter().chain(warnings.iter()) {
        if !guide.warnings.contains(w) {
            guide.warnings.push(w.clone());
        }
    }
    Ok(guide)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::domain::Locator;

    fn src(id: &str, kind: &str) -> Source {
        Source { id: id.into(), kind: kind.into(), title: "Doc".into(), status: "ready".into(), ..Default::default() }
    }

    fn chunk(id: &str, sid: &str, ordinal: u32, text: &str) -> Chunk {
        Chunk {
            id: id.into(),
            source_id: sid.into(),
            notebook_id: "nb".into(),
            ordinal,
            text: text.into(),
            locator: Locator::paragraph(ordinal, 0, 0),
        }
    }

    fn corpus() -> Vec<Chunk> {
        vec![
            chunk(
                "c1",
                "s1",
                0,
                "Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy inside chloroplasts. \
                 Chlorophyll absorbs light most strongly in the blue and red bands. \
                 The Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into glucose using ATP and NADPH.",
            ),
            chunk(
                "c2",
                "s1",
                1,
                "Chlorophyll reflects green light, which is why leaves look green. \
                 The Calvin cycle runs in the stroma and does not require light directly. \
                 Carbon dioxide enters through stomata.",
            ),
            chunk(
                "c3",
                "s1",
                2,
                "Light reactions produce ATP and NADPH for the Calvin cycle. \
                 Stomata close under drought stress, limiting carbon dioxide uptake.",
            ),
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_summary_sentence_is_a_verbatim_quote_with_a_real_locator() {
        let chunks = corpus();
        let g = build(&src("s1", "text"), &chunks, &[]).unwrap();
        let all: Vec<&GuideSentence> = g.headline.iter().chain(g.summary.iter()).collect();
        assert!(!all.is_empty());
        for s in all {
            let c = chunks.iter().find(|c| c.id == s.chunk_id).expect("chunk exists");
            assert!(c.text.contains(&s.text), "quote must appear verbatim in its chunk: {}", s.text);
            assert_eq!(s.locator, c.locator.human());
        }
        let json = g.to_json();
        assert_eq!(json.str_of("generated_by"), Some("extractive"), "never claims to be a model summary");
        assert!(json.get("model").map(|m| m.is_null()).unwrap_or(false));
    }

    #[test]
    fn summary_prefers_distinct_ideas_over_repeats() {
        let chunks = corpus();
        let g = build(&src("s1", "text"), &chunks, &[]).unwrap();
        let texts: Vec<String> = g.summary.iter().map(|s| s.text.clone()).collect();
        assert!(texts.len() >= 2, "summary too short: {:?}", texts);
        for i in 0..texts.len() {
            for j in (i + 1)..texts.len() {
                let a: Vec<String> = retrieve::terms(&texts[i]).into_iter().map(|t| retrieve::stem(&t)).collect();
                let b: Vec<String> = retrieve::terms(&texts[j]).into_iter().map(|t| retrieve::stem(&t)).collect();
                assert!(jaccard(&a, &b) <= 0.55, "near-duplicates kept: {} / {}", texts[i], texts[j]);
            }
        }
        // and the summary is not just chunk 1: a guide should cover the source
        let distinct_chunks: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> =
            g.summary.iter().map(|s| s.chunk_id.as_str()).collect();
        assert!(distinct_chunks.len() >= 2, "summary stayed in one chunk");
    }

    #[test]
    fn topics_are_content_words_with_locations_and_a_stable_order() {
        let chunks = corpus();
        let g1 = build(&src("s1", "text"), &chunks, &[]).unwrap();
        let g2 = build(&src("s1", "text"), &chunks, &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            g1.topics.iter().map(|t| t.term.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            g2.topics.iter().map(|t| t.term.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            "same input must give the same guide"
        );
        assert!(g1.topics.len() >= 3, "{:?}", g1.topics.iter().map(|t| &t.term).collect::<Vec<_>>());
        for t in &g1.topics {
            assert!(!t.first_chunk_id.is_empty(), "topic {} has no location", t.term);
            let lower = t.term.to_lowercase();
            for stop in ["the", "and", "into", "which", "does"] {
                assert_ne!(lower, stop, "stopword leaked into topics: {}", t.term);
            }
            assert!(t.chunks >= 2 || chunks.len() == 1, "topic {} appears in one chunk only", t.term);
        }
        // "Calvin cycle" is the recurring idea in this corpus: it must surface as the phrase,
        // not as two unrelated words
        assert!(
            g1.topics.iter().any(|t| t.term.eq_ignore_ascii_case("calvin cycle")),
            "expected a Calvin-cycle phrase, got {:?}",
            g1.topics.iter().map(|t| &t.term).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        );
        assert!(
            !g1.topics.iter().any(|t| t.term.eq_ignore_ascii_case("calvin")
                || t.term.eq_ignore_ascii_case("cycle")),
            "the absorbed words must not be listed twice: {:?}",
            g1.topics.iter().map(|t| &t.term).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_single_short_source_says_so_instead_of_padding() {
        let chunks = vec![chunk("c1", "s1", 0, "Only one line about ATP.")];
        let g = build(&src("s1", "text"), &chunks, &[]).unwrap();
        assert!(g.warnings.iter().any(|w| w.contains("single passage")), "{:?}", g.warnings);
        assert!(g.warnings.iter().any(|w| w.contains("very short")), "{:?}", g.warnings);
        assert!(g.summary.is_empty(), "one sentence cannot be a multi-sentence summary");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_source_without_passages_refuses() {
        assert!(build(&src("s1", "text"), &[], &[]).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn outline_uses_real_structure_only() {
        let chunks = vec![
            Chunk { locator: Locator::section("Intro", 0, 0), ..chunk("c1", "s1", 0, "Intro text about ATP hydrolysis in cells.") },
            Chunk { locator: Locator::section("Methods", 0, 0), ..chunk("c2", "s1", 1, "Methods text about ATP assays in cells.") },
        ];
        let g = build(&src("s1", "markdown"), &chunks, &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(g.outline, vec!["Intro", "Methods"]);

        let mut parsed = crate::tables::parse_xlsx(
            &std::fs::read(
                std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../tests/fixtures/sales.xlsx"),
            )
            .unwrap(),
            "s1",
            "nb",
        )
        .unwrap();
        parsed[1].hidden = true;
        let g = build(&src("s1", "xlsx"), &corpus(), &parsed).unwrap();
        assert!(g.outline.iter().any(|o| o.contains("sheet Sales")), "{:?}", g.outline);
        assert!(g.outline.iter().any(|o| o.contains("Meta (1 row, hidden)")), "{:?}", g.outline);
        assert_eq!(g.table_count, 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn suggested_questions_are_grounded_in_observed_topics_and_columns() {
        let mut tables = crate::tables::parse_xlsx(
            &std::fs::read(
                std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../tests/fixtures/sales.xlsx"),
            )
            .unwrap(),
            "s1",
            "nb",
        )
        .unwrap();
        tables[1].hidden = true;
        let g = build(&src("s1", "xlsx"), &corpus(), &tables).unwrap();
        assert!(g.questions.len() <= MAX_QUESTIONS);
        assert!(
            g.questions.iter().any(|q| q.contains("total") && q.contains("Sales")),
            "expected a table question, got {:?}",
            g.questions
        );
        for q in &g.questions {
            assert!(!q.contains("Meta"), "hidden sheets must not be suggested: {}", q);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_guide_json_is_complete_and_serialisable() {
        let g = build(&src("s1", "text"), &corpus(), &[]).unwrap();
        let json = g.to_json();
        let text = crate::json::to_string(&json);
        let back = crate::json::parse(&text).expect("guide json parses");
        for key in ["source_id", "headline", "summary", "topics", "outline", "questions", "stats", "warnings"] {
            assert!(back.get(key).is_some(), "missing {} in guide json", key);
        }
        assert_eq!(
            back.get("stats").and_then(|s| s.get("chunks")).and_then(|x| x.as_f64()),
            Some(3.0)
        );
    }
}
```

```rust
//! SHA-256 and SHA-1, hand-written (no crates available).
//!
//! Both are implemented from their specifications and tested against published
//! vectors ‚Äî an analyser whose hashes are wrong is worse than none.

const K256: [u32; 64] = [
    0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5, 0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5,
    0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3, 0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174,
    0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da,
    0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7, 0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967,
    0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13, 0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85,
    0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,
    0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3,
    0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208, 0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2,
];

pub fn sha256(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut h: [u32; 8] = [
        0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19,
    ];
    let mut msg = data.to_vec();
    let bit_len = (data.len() as u64).wrapping_mul(8);
    msg.push(0x80);
    while msg.len() % 64 != 56 {
        msg.push(0);
    }
    msg.extend_from_slice(&bit_len.to_be_bytes());

    for chunk in msg.chunks_exact(64) {
        let mut w = [0u32; 64];
        for i in 0..16 {
            w[i] = u32::from_be_bytes([
                chunk[i * 4],
                chunk[i * 4 + 1],
                chunk[i * 4 + 2],
                chunk[i * 4 + 3],
            ]);
        }
        for i in 16..64 {
            let s0 = w[i - 15].rotate_right(7) ^ w[i - 15].rotate_right(18) ^ (w[i - 15] >> 3);
            let s1 = w[i - 2].rotate_right(17) ^ w[i - 2].rotate_right(19) ^ (w[i - 2] >> 10);
            w[i] = w[i - 16]
                .wrapping_add(s0)
                .wrapping_add(w[i - 7])
                .wrapping_add(s1);
        }
        let (mut a, mut b, mut c, mut d, mut e, mut f, mut g, mut hh) =
            (h[0], h[1], h[2], h[3], h[4], h[5], h[6], h[7]);
        for i in 0..64 {
            let s1 = e.rotate_right(6) ^ e.rotate_right(11) ^ e.rotate_right(25);
            let ch = (e & f) ^ ((!e) & g);
            let t1 = hh
                .wrapping_add(s1)
                .wrapping_add(ch)
                .wrapping_add(K256[i])
                .wrapping_add(w[i]);
            let s0 = a.rotate_right(2) ^ a.rotate_right(13) ^ a.rotate_right(22);
            let maj = (a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c);
            let t2 = s0.wrapping_add(maj);
            hh = g;
            g = f;
            f = e;
            e = d.wrapping_add(t1);
            d = c;
            c = b;
            b = a;
            a = t1.wrapping_add(t2);
        }
        h[0] = h[0].wrapping_add(a);
        h[1] = h[1].wrapping_add(b);
        h[2] = h[2].wrapping_add(c);
        h[3] = h[3].wrapping_add(d);
        h[4] = h[4].wrapping_add(e);
        h[5] = h[5].wrapping_add(f);
        h[6] = h[6].wrapping_add(g);
        h[7] = h[7].wrapping_add(hh);
    }
    h.iter().map(|x| format!("{:08x}", x)).collect()
}

pub fn sha1(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut h: [u32; 5] = [0x67452301, 0xEFCDAB89, 0x98BADCFE, 0x10325476, 0xC3D2E1F0];
    let mut msg = data.to_vec();
    let bit_len = (data.len() as u64).wrapping_mul(8);
    msg.push(0x80);
    while msg.len() % 64 != 56 {
        msg.push(0);
    }
    msg.extend_from_slice(&bit_len.to_be_bytes());

    for chunk in msg.chunks_exact(64) {
        let mut w = [0u32; 80];
        for i in 0..16 {
            w[i] = u32::from_be_bytes([
                chunk[i * 4],
                chunk[i * 4 + 1],
                chunk[i * 4 + 2],
                chunk[i * 4 + 3],
            ]);
        }
        for i in 16..80 {
            w[i] = (w[i - 3] ^ w[i - 8] ^ w[i - 14] ^ w[i - 16]).rotate_left(1);
        }
        let (mut a, mut b, mut c, mut d, mut e) = (h[0], h[1], h[2], h[3], h[4]);
        for i in 0..80 {
            let (f, k) = match i {
                0..=19 => ((b & c) | ((!b) & d), 0x5A827999u32),
                20..=39 => (b ^ c ^ d, 0x6ED9EBA1),
                40..=59 => ((b & c) | (b & d) | (c & d), 0x8F1BBCDC),
                _ => (b ^ c ^ d, 0xCA62C1D6),
            };
            let tmp = a
                .rotate_left(5)
                .wrapping_add(f)
                .wrapping_add(e)
                .wrapping_add(k)
                .wrapping_add(w[i]);
            e = d;
            d = c;
            c = b.rotate_left(30);
            b = a;
            a = tmp;
        }
        h[0] = h[0].wrapping_add(a);
        h[1] = h[1].wrapping_add(b);
        h[2] = h[2].wrapping_add(c);
        h[3] = h[3].wrapping_add(d);
        h[4] = h[4].wrapping_add(e);
    }
    h.iter().map(|x| format!("{:08x}", x)).collect()
}

/// Extract printable ASCII runs of at least `min` bytes.
pub fn strings_of(data: &[u8], min: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    for &b in data {
        if (0x20..0x7f).contains(&b) {
            cur.push(b as char);
        } else {
            if cur.len() >= min {
                out.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
            } else {
                cur.clear();
            }
        }
    }
    if cur.len() >= min {
        out.push(cur);
    }
    out
}

/// Wide (UTF-16LE) printable runs, which is how Windows binaries store text.
pub fn wide_strings_of(data: &[u8], min: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i + 1 < data.len() {
        let lo = data[i];
        let hi = data[i + 1];
        if hi == 0 && (0x20..0x7f).contains(&lo) {
            cur.push(lo as char);
            i += 2;
        } else {
            if cur.len() >= min {
                out.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
            } else {
                cur.clear();
            }
            i += 2;
        }
    }
    if cur.len() >= min {
        out.push(cur);
    }
    out
}

/// Shannon entropy in bits per byte (0..8). High entropy over a whole file is
/// the classic packing/encryption signal.
pub fn entropy(data: &[u8]) -> f64 {
    if data.is_empty() {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let mut counts = [0usize; 256];
    for &b in data {
        counts[b as usize] += 1;
    }
    let len = data.len() as f64;
    let mut e = 0.0;
    for c in counts {
        if c > 0 {
            let p = c as f64 / len;
            e -= p * p.log2();
        }
    }
    e
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn sha256_matches_published_vectors() {
        assert_eq!(
            sha256(b""),
            "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sha256(b"abc"),
            "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sha256(b"abcdbcdecdefdefgefghfghighijhijkijkljklmklmnlmnomnopnopq"),
            "248d6a61d20638b8e5c026930c3e6039a33ce45964ff2167f6ecedd419db06c1"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sha1_matches_published_vectors() {
        assert_eq!(sha1(b""), "da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709");
        assert_eq!(sha1(b"abc"), "a9993e364706816aba3e25717850c26c9cd0d89d");
        assert_eq!(
            sha1(b"abcdbcdecdefdefgefghfghighijhijkijkljklmklmnlmnomnopnopq"),
            "84983e441c3bd26ebaae4aa1f95129e5e54670f1"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn strings_extraction_is_bounded() {
        let data = b"\x00\x01hello world\x00ab\x00another string here\xff";
        let s = strings_of(data, 5);
        assert_eq!(s, vec!["hello world", "another string here"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn wide_strings_are_found() {
        let mut data = Vec::new();
        for ch in "C:\\Windows\\System32".chars() {
            data.push(ch as u8);
            data.push(0);
        }
        let s = wide_strings_of(&data, 8);
        assert_eq!(s, vec!["C:\\Windows\\System32"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn entropy_separates_text_from_random() {
        let zeros = vec![0u8; 4096];
        assert!(entropy(&zeros) < 0.01);
        let random: Vec<u8> = (0..4096).map(|i| ((i * 7919) % 256) as u8).collect();
        assert!(entropy(&random) > 7.0, "pseudo-random data should look packed");
    }
}
```

## `crates/forge-core/src/http.rs`

```rust
//! Small HTTP/1.1 server built on `std::net` (no hyper/axum: crates.io blocked).
//!
//! Scope is deliberate: one request per connection, `Connection: close`, hard limits on
//! header size and body size. Responses are either buffered (`Content-Length`) or streamed
//! with **chunked transfer encoding** (`Reply::Stream`), which is what the chat stream uses.
//! There is no request chunked decoding: request bodies must carry a `Content-Length`.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read, Write};
use std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

pub const MAX_HEADER_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;
pub const DEFAULT_MAX_BODY: usize = 32 * 1024 * 1024; // 32 MiB uploads (PDF etc.)

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Request {
    pub method: String,
    pub path: String,
    pub query: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub headers: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
    pub peer: String,
}

impl Request {
    pub fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.headers.get(&name.to_ascii_lowercase()).map(|s| s.as_str())
    }
    pub fn body_str(&self) -> String {
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&self.body).to_string()
    }
    pub fn query_get(&self, k: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.query.get(k).map(|s| s.as_str())
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Response {
    pub status: u16,
    pub content_type: String,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl Response {
    pub fn new(status: u16, content_type: &str, body: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Response {
        Response { status, content_type: content_type.to_string(), body: body.into(), headers: Vec::new() }
    }

    pub fn json(status: u16, v: &crate::json::Value) -> Response {
        Response::new(status, "application/json; charset=utf-8", crate::json::to_string(v).into_bytes())
    }

    pub fn text(status: u16, s: impl Into<String>) -> Response {
        Response::new(status, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", s.into().into_bytes())
    }

    pub fn html(s: impl Into<String>) -> Response {
        Response::new(200, "text/html; charset=utf-8", s.into().into_bytes())
    }

    pub fn with_header(mut self, k: &str, v: &str) -> Response {
        self.headers.push((k.to_string(), v.to_string()));
        self
    }

    fn reason(status: u16) -> &'static str {
        match status {
            200 => "OK",
            201 => "Created",
            204 => "No Content",
            304 => "Not Modified",
            400 => "Bad Request",
            401 => "Unauthorized",
            403 => "Forbidden",
            404 => "Not Found",
            405 => "Method Not Allowed",
            409 => "Conflict",
            413 => "Payload Too Large",
            415 => "Unsupported Media Type",
            422 => "Unprocessable Entity",
            429 => "Too Many Requests",
            500 => "Internal Server Error",
            501 => "Not Implemented",
            _ => "Unknown",
        }
    }

    fn common_headers() -> String {
        let mut h = String::new();
        h.push_str("X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff\r\n");
        h.push_str("Cache-Control: no-store\r\n");
        h.push_str("Referrer-Policy: no-referrer\r\n");
        h.push_str(
            "Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'\r\n",
        );
        h
    }

    pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut head = format!(
            "HTTP/1.1 {} {}\r\nContent-Type: {}\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n",
            self.status,
            Response::reason(self.status),
            self.content_type,
            self.body.len()
        );
        head.push_str(&Response::common_headers());
        for (k, v) in &self.headers {
            head.push_str(&format!("{}: {}\r\n", k, v));
        }
        head.push_str("\r\n");
        let mut out = head.into_bytes();
        out.extend_from_slice(&self.body);
        out
    }
}


/// What a handler returns. Most routes are `Full` (buffered, `Content-Length`); the chat
/// stream is `Stream` (framed, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`).
pub enum Reply {
    Full(Response),
    Stream(StreamReply),
}

impl From<Response> for Reply {
    fn from(r: Response) -> Reply {
        Reply::Full(r)
    }
}

/// A chunked response that is written frame by frame.
///
/// `on_finish` is called exactly once with `complete = true` only if the terminating
/// zero-length chunk was accepted by the socket. That is what lets the API persist a chat
/// turn **after** delivery: a stream the client aborted never becomes part of the
/// conversation, so "Stop" has a real effect rather than a cosmetic one.
pub struct StreamReply {
    pub status: u16,
    pub content_type: String,
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub frames: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
    /// Diagnostic pacing between frames (see `maybe_pace`). `None` means "as fast as the
    /// socket accepts", which is what the UI uses.
    pub pace: Option<Duration>,
    pub on_finish: Option<Box<dyn FnOnce(bool) + Send + Sync>>,
}

impl StreamReply {
    pub fn new(status: u16, content_type: &str, frames: Vec<Vec<u8>>) -> StreamReply {
        StreamReply {
            status,
            content_type: content_type.to_string(),
            headers: Vec::new(),
            frames,
            pace: None,
            on_finish: None,
        }
    }

    /// Diagnostic pacing between frames, in milliseconds. Off by default; it exists so a test
    /// (or a person debugging the UI) can observe progressive delivery on a fast local answer.
    /// It adds delay and nothing else ‚Äî no content depends on it.
    pub fn maybe_pace(mut self, pace: Option<Duration>) -> StreamReply {
        self.pace = pace;
        self
    }

    pub fn with_header(mut self, k: &str, v: &str) -> StreamReply {
        self.headers.push((k.to_string(), v.to_string()));
        self
    }

    pub fn on_finish(mut self, f: impl FnOnce(bool) + Send + Sync + 'static) -> StreamReply {
        self.on_finish = Some(Box::new(f));
        self
    }

    fn head(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut head = format!(
            "HTTP/1.1 {} {}\r\nContent-Type: {}\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nConnection: close\r\n",
            self.status,
            Response::reason(self.status),
            self.content_type
        );
        head.push_str(&Response::common_headers());
        // Proxies must not buffer a stream; nothing between us and the browser is allowed
        // to sit on frames until the answer is finished.
        head.push_str("X-Accel-Buffering: no\r\n");
        for (k, v) in &self.headers {
            head.push_str(&format!("{}: {}\r\n", k, v));
        }
        head.push_str("\r\n");
        head.into_bytes()
    }
}

/// True when the peer has closed its side of the connection.
///
/// `read` on a socket whose peer sent FIN returns `Ok(0)`; a timeout (the normal case, since
/// the request body is already consumed) returns an error and means "still connected".
fn peer_gone(stream: &TcpStream) -> bool {
    let mut probe = match stream.try_clone() {
        Ok(s) => s,
        Err(_) => return false,
    };
    let _ = probe.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_millis(1)));
    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];
    matches!(probe.read(&mut byte), Ok(0))
}

/// Write a chunked response. Returns true only if every frame and the terminator were
/// accepted. Aborts (peer gone, EPIPE, write timeout) stop the loop immediately.
pub fn write_stream(stream: &mut TcpStream, mut sr: StreamReply) -> bool {
    let mut complete = stream.write_all(&sr.head()).is_ok() && stream.flush().is_ok();
    if complete {
        for (idx, frame) in sr.frames.iter().enumerate() {
            if idx > 0 {
                if let Some(p) = sr.pace {
                    std::thread::sleep(p);
                }
            }
            if peer_gone(stream) {
                complete = false;
                break;
            }
            let mut buf = format!("{:X}\r\n", frame.len()).into_bytes();
            buf.extend_from_slice(frame);
            buf.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
            if stream.write_all(&buf).is_err() || stream.flush().is_err() {
                complete = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        if complete && (stream.write_all(b"0\r\n\r\n").is_err() || stream.flush().is_err()) {
            complete = false;
        }
    }
    if let Some(f) = sr.on_finish.take() {
        f(complete);
    }
    complete
}

pub fn parse_request(raw: &[u8], peer: &str, max_body: usize) -> Result<Request, (u16, String)> {
    // Split head from body at the first CRLFCRLF.
    let sep = find(raw, b"\r\n\r\n").ok_or((400u16, "no header terminator".to_string()))?;
    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw[..sep]).to_string();
    let mut lines = head.split("\r\n");
    let request_line = lines.next().ok_or((400u16, "empty request".to_string()))?;
    let mut parts = request_line.split_whitespace();
    let method = parts.next().ok_or((400u16, "no method".to_string()))?.to_string();
    let target = parts.next().ok_or((400u16, "no target".to_string()))?.to_string();
    let version = parts.next().unwrap_or("HTTP/1.1").to_string();
    if !version.starts_with("HTTP/1.") {
        return Err((400, format!("unsupported version {}", version)));
    }

    let (path, query) = match target.split_once('?') {
        Some((p, q)) => (p.to_string(), parse_query(q)),
        None => (target, BTreeMap::new()),
    };

    let mut headers = BTreeMap::new();
    for line in lines {
        if line.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let (k, v) = line.split_once(':').ok_or((400u16, "bad header".to_string()))?;
        headers.insert(k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim().to_string());
    }

    let mut body = raw[sep + 4..].to_vec();
    if let Some(len_s) = headers.get("content-length") {
        let len: usize = len_s.parse().map_err(|_| (400u16, "bad content-length".to_string()))?;
        if len > max_body {
            return Err((413, format!("body {} exceeds limit {}", len, max_body)));
        }
        if body.len() > len {
            body.truncate(len);
        }
    }

    Ok(Request { method, path, query, headers, body, peer: peer.to_string() })
}

fn find(hay: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    if needle.len() > hay.len() {
        return None;
    }
    (0..=hay.len() - needle.len()).find(|&i| &hay[i..i + needle.len()] == needle)
}

fn parse_query(q: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
    let mut map = BTreeMap::new();
    for pair in q.split('&') {
        if pair.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let (k, v) = pair.split_once('=').unwrap_or((pair, ""));
        map.insert(percent_decode(k), percent_decode(v));
    }
    map
}

pub fn percent_decode(s: &str) -> String {
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        match bytes[i] {
            b'%' if i + 2 < bytes.len() => {
                let hex = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[i + 1..i + 3]).unwrap_or("");
                match u8::from_str_radix(hex, 16) {
                    Ok(b) => {
                        out.push(b);
                        i += 3;
                    }
                    Err(_) => {
                        out.push(bytes[i]);
                        i += 1;
                    }
                }
            }
            b'+' => {
                out.push(b' ');
                i += 1;
            }
            b => {
                out.push(b);
                i += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).to_string()
}

/// Read one request from a stream honouring the declared content length.
pub fn read_request(stream: &mut TcpStream, peer: &str, max_body: usize) -> Result<Request, (u16, String)> {
    let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream.try_clone().map_err(|e| (400u16, e.to_string()))?);
    let mut head = Vec::new();
    let mut line = String::new();
    loop {
        line.clear();
        let n = reader
            .read_line(&mut line)
            .map_err(|e| (400u16, e.to_string()))?;
        if n == 0 {
            return Err((400, "connection closed before headers".to_string()));
        }
        head.extend_from_slice(line.as_bytes());
        if head.len() > MAX_HEADER_BYTES {
            return Err((413, "headers too large".to_string()));
        }
        if line == "\r\n" || line == "\n" {
            break;
        }
    }

    let head_str = String::from_utf8_lossy(&head).to_string();
    let mut lines = head_str.split("\r\n");
    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or("");
    let mut parts = request_line.split_whitespace();
    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let target = parts.next().unwrap_or("/").to_string();
    if method.is_empty() {
        return Err((400, "empty request line".to_string()));
    }
    let (path, query) = match target.split_once('?') {
        Some((p, q)) => (p.to_string(), parse_query(q)),
        None => (target, BTreeMap::new()),
    };
    let mut headers = BTreeMap::new();
    for line in lines {
        if line.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(':') {
            headers.insert(k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim().to_string());
        }
    }
    let len: usize = headers
        .get("content-length")
        .and_then(|s| s.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    if len > max_body {
        return Err((413, format!("body {} exceeds limit {}", len, max_body)));
    }
    let mut body = vec![0u8; len];
    if len > 0 {
        reader
            .read_exact(&mut body)
            .map_err(|e| (400u16, format!("short body: {}", e)))?;
    }
    Ok(Request { method, path, query, headers, body, peer: peer.to_string() })
}

/// Serve forever, one thread per connection.
pub fn serve<F>(listener: TcpListener, handler: F, max_body: usize) -> std::io::Result<()>
where
    F: Fn(&Request) -> Reply + Send + Sync + 'static,
{
    let handler = Arc::new(handler);
    for incoming in listener.incoming() {
        let stream = match incoming {
            Ok(s) => s,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };
        let h = Arc::clone(&handler);
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let _ = stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(30)));
            let _ = stream.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(30)));
            handle_conn(stream, &*h, max_body);
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn handle_conn(mut stream: TcpStream, handler: &dyn Fn(&Request) -> Reply, max_body: usize) {
    let peer = stream
        .peer_addr()
        .map(|a| a.to_string())
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| "unknown".into());
    match read_request(&mut stream, &peer, max_body) {
        Ok(req) => match handler(&req) {
            Reply::Full(response) => {
                let _ = stream.write_all(&response.encode());
                let _ = stream.flush();
            }
            Reply::Stream(sr) => {
                write_stream(&mut stream, sr);
            }
        },
        Err((code, msg)) => {
            let response = Response::json(
                code,
                &crate::obj! { "error" => msg.as_str(), "status" => code as u64 },
            );
            let _ = stream.write_all(&response.encode());
            let _ = stream.flush();
        }
    }
}

pub fn mime_for(path: &str) -> &'static str {
    let lower = path.to_ascii_lowercase();
    if lower.ends_with(".html") || lower.ends_with(".htm") {
        "text/html; charset=utf-8"
    } else if lower.ends_with(".js") || lower.ends_with(".mjs") {
        "text/javascript; charset=utf-8"
    } else if lower.ends_with(".css") {
        "text/css; charset=utf-8"
    } else if lower.ends_with(".json") || lower.ends_with(".webmanifest") {
        "application/json; charset=utf-8"
    } else if lower.ends_with(".svg") {
        "image/svg+xml"
    } else if lower.ends_with(".png") {
        "image/png"
    } else if lower.ends_with(".ico") {
        "image/x-icon"
    } else if lower.ends_with(".woff2") {
        "font/woff2"
    } else {
        "application/octet-stream"
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn responses_carry_security_headers() {
        let raw = String::from_utf8(Response::json(200, &crate::json::Value::Null).encode()).unwrap();
        assert!(raw.contains("X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff"));
        assert!(raw.contains("Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'"));
        assert!(raw.contains("Referrer-Policy: no-referrer"));
        assert!(!raw.to_lowercase().contains("access-control-allow-origin: *"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_query_and_percent_encoding() {
        let raw = b"GET /api/x?a=1&b=hello%20world&c=%E2%9C%93 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n";
        let req = parse_request(raw, "127.0.0.1:1", 1024).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(req.method, "GET");
        assert_eq!(req.path, "/api/x");
        assert_eq!(req.query_get("a"), Some("1"));
        assert_eq!(req.query_get("b"), Some("hello world"));
        assert_eq!(req.query_get("c"), Some("‚úì"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn encodes_response_with_content_length() {
        let r = Response::text(200, "hello");
        let raw = String::from_utf8(r.encode()).unwrap();
        assert!(raw.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 200 OK"));
        assert!(raw.contains("Content-Length: 5"));
        assert!(raw.ends_with("hello"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_oversized_body() {
        let raw = b"POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 999999\r\n\r\n";
        let err = parse_request(raw, "p", 1024).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.0, 413);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_malformed() {
        assert!(parse_request(b"garbage", "p", 100).is_err());
        assert!(parse_request(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nBadHeader\r\n\r\n", "p", 100).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_complete_stream_uses_chunked_framing_and_reports_delivery() {
        use std::io::Read as _;
        use std::net::TcpListener;
        use std::sync::mpsc;

        let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<bool>();
        let client = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut s = std::net::TcpStream::connect(addr).unwrap();
            s.write_all(b"GET /api/notebooks/x/chat/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n")
                .unwrap();
            let mut raw = Vec::new();
            s.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5))).unwrap();
            let _ = s.read_to_end(&mut raw);
            raw
        });

        let mut server = listener.accept().unwrap().0;
        let _ = read_request(&mut server, "test", 1024);
        let ok = write_stream(
            &mut server,
            StreamReply::new(
                200,
                "application/x-ndjson",
                vec![b"{\"event\":\"start\"}\n".to_vec(), b"{\"event\":\"done\"}\n".to_vec()],
            )
            .on_finish(move |c| {
                let _ = tx.send(c);
            }),
        );
        assert!(ok, "an accepted stream must report completion");
        assert!(rx.recv().unwrap(), "on_finish must see complete = true");
        std::mem::drop(server); // close, so the client's read_to_end returns

        let raw = client.join().unwrap();
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw).to_string();
        assert!(text.contains("Transfer-Encoding: chunked"));
        assert!(!text.contains("Content-Length"));
        // Each frame is its own chunk: hex length, CRLF, payload, CRLF.
        let start = format!("{:X}\r\n{{\"event\":\"start\"}}\n\r\n", "{\"event\":\"start\"}\n".len());
        let done = format!("{:X}\r\n{{\"event\":\"done\"}}\n\r\n", "{\"event\":\"done\"}\n".len());
        assert!(text.contains(&start), "raw: {}", text);
        assert!(text.contains(&done), "raw: {}", text);
        assert!(text.ends_with("0\r\n\r\n"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_aborted_stream_is_not_reported_as_delivered() {
        use std::net::TcpListener;
        use std::sync::mpsc;

        let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
        let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap();
        let client = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let s = std::net::TcpStream::connect(addr).unwrap();
            std::mem::drop(s); // hang up without reading a byte
        });

        let mut server = listener.accept().unwrap().0;
        server.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_millis(200))).unwrap();
        client.join().unwrap();
        // let the FIN land before the writer starts probing
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));

        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<bool>();
        let ok = write_stream(
            &mut server,
            StreamReply::new(200, "application/x-ndjson", vec![b"{\"event\":\"x\"}\n".to_vec()])
                .on_finish(move |c| {
                    let _ = tx.send(c);
                }),
        );
        assert!(!ok, "a hung-up client must not count as delivery");
        assert!(!rx.recv().unwrap(), "on_finish must see complete = false");
    }

    #[test]
    fn mime_types() {
        assert_eq!(mime_for("a.html"), "text/html; charset=utf-8");
        assert_eq!(mime_for("a.js"), "text/javascript; charset=utf-8");
        assert_eq!(mime_for("a.weird"), "application/octet-stream");
    }
}
```
