```rust
// ---------------------------------------------------------------- requests
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct Credentials {
    /// Full `Cookie:` header value from an authenticated browser session.
    pub cookies: String,
    /// `at` token (SNlM0e) scraped from the app page.
    pub at: String,
}

pub struct WireRequest {
    pub method: &'static str,
    pub url: String,
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub body: String,
}

/// Percent-encode as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (space as %20 is accepted
/// by the endpoint; we use %20 rather than '+', which is what the web client sends).
fn form_encode(v: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(v.len() * 3);
    for b in v.as_bytes() {
        match *b {
            b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' | b'0'..=b'9' | b'-' | b'_' | b'.' | b'~' => out.push(*b as char),
            b' ' => out.push_str("%20"),
            other => out.push_str(&format!("%{:02X}", other)),
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Build the `f.req` body for a batchexecute call.
pub fn batchexecute_body(rpc: Rpc, params: &Value) -> String {
    let inner = json::to_string(params);
    // Canonical batchexecute envelope: f.req = [[[rpcid, params_json, null, "generic"]]]
    // i.e. a list of calls; each call is a 4-element array.
    let call = a(vec![s(rpc.id), s(&inner), null(), s("generic")]);
    let envelope = a(vec![a(vec![call])]);
    format!("f.req={}", form_encode(&json::to_string(&envelope)))
}

pub fn batchexecute_request(rpc: Rpc, params: &Value, creds: &Credentials) -> WireRequest {
    WireRequest {
        method: "POST",
        url: format!("{}{}?rpcids={}&rt=c", ORIGIN, BATCH_PATH, rpc.id),
        headers: vec![
            ("Content-Type".into(), "application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8".into()),
            ("X-Same-Domain".into(), "1".into()),
            ("Origin".into(), ORIGIN.into()),
            ("Referer".into(), format!("{}/", ORIGIN)),
            ("Cookie".into(), creds.cookies.clone()),
        ],
        body: batchexecute_body(rpc, params),
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------- source builders
/// `izAoDd` params for a web URL source.
pub fn add_url_source(notebook_id: &str, url: &str) -> Value {
    let mut slots = [null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), n(1)];
    slots[2] = a(vec![s(url)]);
    a(vec![
        a(vec![source_spec(slots)]),
        s(notebook_id),
        request_options(),
    ])
}

/// `izAoDd` params for pasted text. Content-type slot 3 = 2 (pasted text).
pub fn add_text_source(notebook_id: &str, title: &str, content: &str) -> Value {
    let mut slots = [null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), n(1)];
    slots[1] = a(vec![s(title), s(content)]);
    slots[3] = n(2);
    a(vec![
        a(vec![source_spec(slots)]),
        s(notebook_id),
        request_options(),
    ])
}

/// `izAoDd` params for a YouTube video. Position 7 carries the URL ‚Äî different
/// from a regular web URL, which sits at position 2.
pub fn add_youtube_source(notebook_id: &str, url: &str) -> Value {
    let mut slots = [null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), n(1)];
    slots[7] = s(url);
    a(vec![
        a(vec![source_spec(slots)]),
        s(notebook_id),
        request_options(),
    ])
}

/// `o4cbdc` params that register an upload and return a resumable upload URL.
pub fn register_file_source(notebook_id: &str, filename: &str) -> Value {
    let mut slots = [null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), null(), n(1)];
    slots[0] = s(filename);
    a(vec![
        s(notebook_id),
        a(vec![source_spec(slots)]),
        request_options(),
    ])
}

// ----------------------------------------------------- artifact builders
fn id_list_pair(source_ids: &[String]) -> (Value, Value) {
    let triple = a(source_ids.iter().map(|id| a(vec![a(vec![s(id)])])).collect());
    let double = a(source_ids.iter().map(|id| a(vec![s(id)])).collect());
    (triple, double)
}

pub struct ArtifactRequest<'a> {
    pub kind: ArtifactKind,
    pub notebook_id: &'a str,
    pub source_ids: &'a [String],
    /// Free-text focus/instructions.
    pub instructions: &'a str,
    /// Audio only.
    pub audio_length: AudioLength,
    /// Type 4 only.
    pub study_variant: StudyVariant,
    /// Type 4 only: 1 = fewer, 2 = standard, 3 = more.
    pub quantity: i64,
    /// Type 4 only: 1 = easy, 2 = medium, 3 = hard.
    pub difficulty: i64,
}

impl<'a> ArtifactRequest<'a> {
    pub fn new(kind: ArtifactKind, notebook_id: &'a str, source_ids: &'a [String]) -> Self {
        ArtifactRequest {
            kind,
            notebook_id,
            source_ids,
            instructions: "",
            audio_length: AudioLength::Default,
            study_variant: StudyVariant::Flashcards,
            quantity: 2,
            difficulty: 2,
        }
    }

    pub fn params(&self) -> Value {
        let (triple, double) = id_list_pair(self.source_ids);
        let spec = match self.kind {
            ArtifactKind::Audio => a(vec![
                null(),
                null(),
                n(ArtifactKind::Audio.code()),
                triple.clone(),
                null(),
                null(),
                a(vec![
                    null(),
                    a(vec![
                        s(self.instructions),
                        n(self.audio_length.code()),
                        null(),
                        double.clone(),
                    ]),
                ]),
            ]),
            ArtifactKind::QuizFlashcards => {
                // slots 6 = flashcards [qty, difficulty], 7 = quiz [qty, difficulty]
                let pair = a(vec![n(self.quantity), n(self.difficulty)]);
                let (fb, qz) = match self.study_variant {
                    StudyVariant::Flashcards => (pair, null()),
                    StudyVariant::Quiz => (null(), pair),
                };
                a(vec![
                    null(),
                    null(),
                    n(ArtifactKind::QuizFlashcards.code()),
                    triple.clone(),
                    null(),
                    null(),
                    null(),
                    null(),
                    a(vec![
                        n(self.study_variant.code()),
                        null(),
                        s(self.instructions),
                        null(),
                        null(),
                        null(),
                        fb,
                        qz,
                    ]),
                ])
            }
            other => a(vec![
                null(),
                null(),
                n(other.code()),
                triple.clone(),
                null(),
                null(),
                null(),
                null(),
                a(vec![null(), s(self.instructions)]),
            ]),
        };
        a(vec![
            create_artifact_options(),
            s(self.notebook_id),
            a(vec![
                spec,
                null(),
                a(self.source_ids.iter().map(|id| s(id)).collect()),
            ]),
        ])
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------- chat request
pub fn chat_request(notebook_id: &str, question: &str, creds: &Credentials) -> WireRequest {
    let params = a(vec![
        a(vec![
            null(),
            null(),
            null(),
            null(),
            null(),
            null(),
            null(),
            a(vec![s(question)]),
        ]),
        s(notebook_id),
        request_options(),
    ]);
    WireRequest {
        method: "POST",
        url: format!("{}{}", ORIGIN, CHAT_PATH),
        headers: vec![
            ("Content-Type".into(), "application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8".into()),
            ("X-Same-Domain".into(), "1".into()),
            ("Cookie".into(), creds.cookies.clone()),
        ],
        body: format!(
            "f.req={}&at={}",
            form_encode(&json::to_string(&params)),
            form_encode(&creds.at)
        ),
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------ response parsing
/// The response body starts with an anti-XSSI prefix and is framed as
/// `<length>\n<json row>\n` records. Returns the decoded `wrb.fr` payloads.
pub fn parse_frames(raw: &str) -> Result<Vec<Value>, String> {
    let body = raw.trim_start_matches(")]}'").trim_start();
    let mut out: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    let mut lines = body.lines().peekable();
    while let Some(line) = lines.next() {
        let t = line.trim();
        if t.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let is_len = !t.is_empty() && t.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit());
        if is_len {
            if let Some(payload) = lines.next() {
                if let Ok(v) = json::parse(payload.trim()) {
                    collect_frames(&v, &mut out);
                }
            }
            continue;
        }
        if let Ok(v) = json::parse(t) {
            collect_frames(&v, &mut out);
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

fn collect_frames(v: &Value, out: &mut Vec<Value>) {
    let Value::Arr(items) = v else { return };
    for item in items {
        let Value::Arr(inner) = item else { continue };
        if inner.first().and_then(|x| x.as_str()) != Some("wrb.fr") {
            continue;
        }
        // ["wrb.fr", rpcid, "<json string>", ...]
        if let Some(payload) = inner.get(2).and_then(|x| x.as_str()) {
            if let Ok(parsed) = json::parse(payload) {
                out.push(parsed);
            }
        }
        // some frames carry the payload as a direct array at index 2
        if let Some(Value::Arr(_)) = inner.get(2) {
            out.push(inner[2].clone());
        }
    }
}

/// Streaming chat frames are cumulative; `envelope[4] == true` marks the final one.
pub fn parse_stream_answer(raw: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let frames = parse_frames(raw)?;
    let mut best: Option<(bool, usize, String)> = None;
    for f in frames {
        let Value::Arr(env) = &f else { continue };
        let is_final = env.get(4).and_then(|x| x.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false);
        let answer = env
            .first()
            .and_then(|a0| a0.as_arr())
            .and_then(|row| row.iter().find_map(|x| x.as_str()))
            .map(|s| s.to_string());
        if let Some(text) = answer {
            let better = match &best {
                None => true,
                Some((was_final, len, _)) => (!*was_final && is_final) || (!*was_final && !is_final && text.len() > *len),
            };
            if better {
                best = Some((is_final, text.len(), text));
            }
        }
    }
    best.map(|(_, _, t)| t)
        .ok_or_else(|| "no answer frame in response".to_string())
}

/// Artifact kickoff result: `[[artifact_id, title, type, null(), status, ...]]`.
pub fn parse_artifact_kickoff(frame: &Value) -> Option<(String, String, i64, i64)> {
    let row = frame.as_arr()?.first()?.as_arr()?;
    let id = row.first()?.as_str()?.to_string();
    let title = row.get(1).and_then(|x| x.as_str()).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let kind = row.get(2).and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as i64;
    let status = row.get(4).and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as i64;
    Some((id, title, kind, status))
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------- transport seam
/// Everything network-shaped lives behind this trait.
pub trait Transport {
    fn send(&self, req: &WireRequest) -> Result<String, String>;
}

/// The only transport this build can offer: none, and it says why.
pub struct NoTransport;

impl Transport for NoTransport {
    fn send(&self, _req: &WireRequest) -> Result<String, String> {
        Err(UNAVAILABLE.into())
    }
}

pub const UNAVAILABLE: &str = "NotebookLM cannot be reached from this build: the sandbox has no route to notebooklm.google.com (verified: HTTP 000) and no TLS client is available. The protocol is implemented and unit-tested; only a Transport is missing.";

pub struct NotebookLmClient<T: Transport> {
    pub creds: Credentials,
    pub transport: T,
}

impl<T: Transport> NotebookLmClient<T> {
    pub fn new(creds: Credentials, transport: T) -> Self {
        NotebookLmClient { creds, transport }
    }

    pub fn available(&self) -> bool {
        false
    }

    pub fn call(&self, rpc: Rpc, params: &Value) -> Result<Vec<Value>, String> {
        let req = batchexecute_request(rpc, params, &self.creds);
        let raw = self.transport.send(&req)?;
        parse_frames(&raw)
    }

    pub fn ask(&self, notebook_id: &str, question: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        let req = chat_request(notebook_id, question, &self.creds);
        let raw = self.transport.send(&req)?;
        parse_stream_answer(&raw)
    }
}

/// Machine-readable status for the API and the UI.
pub fn status() -> Value {
    let _ = n(0);
    let mut catalogue: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    for rpc in [
        RPC_LIST_NOTEBOOKS,
        RPC_CREATE_NOTEBOOK,
        RPC_GET_NOTEBOOK,
        RPC_ADD_SOURCE,
        RPC_ADD_SOURCE_FILE,
        RPC_DELETE_SOURCE,
        RPC_CREATE_ARTIFACT,
        RPC_LIST_ARTIFACTS,
        RPC_GENERATE_MIND_MAP,
        RPC_SUMMARIZE,
        RPC_CREATE_NOTE,
        RPC_GET_NOTES,
        RPC_LIST_LABELS,
        RPC_RETRIEVE_CHUNKS,
    ] {
        catalogue.push(crate::obj! {
            "id" => rpc.id,
            "name" => rpc.name,
            "corroboration" => rpc.corroboration as u64,
        });
    }
    crate::obj! {
        "service" => "Google Gemini Notebook (notebooklm.google.com)",
        "status" => "protocol_implemented_target_unreachable",
        "implemented" => obj_bool(true),
        "reachable" => obj_bool(false),
        "reason" => UNAVAILABLE,
        "rpc_count" => catalogue.len() as u64,
        "rpc" => Value::Arr(catalogue),
        "artifact_types" => Value::Arr(vec![
            crate::obj!{"code" => 1u64, "kind" => "audio_overview"},
            crate::obj!{"code" => 2u64, "kind" => "report"},
            crate::obj!{"code" => 3u64, "kind" => "video_overview"},
            crate::obj!{"code" => 4u64, "kind" => "quiz_or_flashcards"},
            crate::obj!{"code" => 5u64, "kind" => "mind_map"},
            crate::obj!{"code" => 6u64, "kind" => "fantasy_map"},
            crate::obj!{"code" => 7u64, "kind" => "infographic"},
            crate::obj!{"code" => 8u64, "kind" => "slide_deck"},
            crate::obj!{"code" => 9u64, "kind" => "data_table"},
            crate::obj!{"code" => 10u64, "kind" => "file"},
        ]),
        "provenance" => "public reverse engineering: teng-lin/notebooklm-py@956400a docs/rpc-reference.md, cross-checked against jacob-bd/gemini-notebook-mcp-cli and jackwener/OpenCLI",
    }
}

fn obj_bool(b: bool) -> Value {
    Value::from(b)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn ids() -> Vec<String> {
        vec!["src-1".to_string(), "src-2".to_string()]
    }

    #[test]
    fn batchexecute_envelope_is_the_documented_shape() {
        let body = batchexecute_body(RPC_LIST_NOTEBOOKS, &a(vec![]));
        assert!(body.starts_with("f.req="), "body must be form-encoded f.req");
        let decoded = body.trim_start_matches("f.req=");
        // percent-decoded copy of the envelope
        let raw = crate::http::percent_decode(decoded);
        let parsed = json::parse(&raw).expect("envelope must be valid JSON");
        let outer = parsed.as_arr().expect("outer array");
        let calls = outer[0].as_arr().expect("list of calls");
        let call = calls[0].as_arr().expect("call array");
        assert_eq!(call[0].as_str(), Some("wXbhsf"), "RPC id first");
        assert_eq!(call.len(), 4, "rpc id, params string, null(), 'generic'");
        assert_eq!(call[1].as_str(), Some("[]"), "params are a JSON string");
        assert!(matches!(call[2], Value::Null));
        assert_eq!(call[3].as_str(), Some("generic"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn request_has_rpc_scoped_url_and_headers() {
        let creds = Credentials { cookies: "SID=abc".into(), at: "AT123".into() };
        let req = batchexecute_request(RPC_ADD_SOURCE, &add_url_source("nb1", "https://example.com/x"), &creds);
        assert_eq!(req.method, "POST");
        assert_eq!(
            req.url,
            "https://notebooklm.google.com/_/LabsTailwindUi/data/batchexecute?rpcids=izAoDd&rt=c"
        );
        let names: Vec<&str> = req.headers.iter().map(|(k, _)| k.as_str()).collect();
        assert!(names.contains(&"X-Same-Domain"));
        assert!(names.contains(&"Cookie"));
        assert!(req.headers.iter().any(|(k, v)| k == "Cookie" && v == "SID=abc"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn url_source_puts_the_url_at_slot_two() {
        let p = add_url_source("nb1", "https://example.com/page");
        let specs = p.as_arr().unwrap()[0].as_arr().unwrap();
        let spec = specs[0].as_arr().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(spec.len(), 11, "11-element source spec");
        let urls = spec[2].as_arr().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(urls[0].as_str(), Some("https://example.com/page"));
        assert_eq!(spec[10].as_f64(), Some(1.0), "trailing marker is 1");
        assert_eq!(p.as_arr().unwrap()[1].as_str(), Some("nb1"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn text_source_carries_title_content_and_type_code() {
        let p = add_text_source("nb1", "Notes", "hello world");
        let spec = p.as_arr().unwrap()[0].as_arr().unwrap()[0].as_arr().unwrap();
        let pair = spec[1].as_arr().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(pair[0].as_str(), Some("Notes"));
        assert_eq!(pair[1].as_str(), Some("hello world"));
        assert_eq!(spec[3].as_f64(), Some(2.0), "pasted-text type code");
    }

    #[test]
    fn youtube_source_uses_slot_seven() {
        let p = add_youtube_source("nb1", "https://youtu.be/xyz");
        let spec = p.as_arr().unwrap()[0].as_arr().unwrap()[0].as_arr().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(spec[7].as_str(), Some("https://youtu.be/xyz"));
        assert!(spec[2].is_null(), "slot 2 stays empty for YouTube");
    }

    #[test]
    fn audio_artifact_uses_type_1_and_length_code() {
        let ids = ids();
        let mut req = ArtifactRequest::new(ArtifactKind::Audio, "nb1", &ids);
        req.audio_length = AudioLength::Long;
        req.instructions = "focus on evaluation";
        let p = req.params();
        let spec = p.as_arr().unwrap()[2].as_arr().unwrap()[0].as_arr().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(spec[2].as_f64(), Some(1.0), "AUDIO type code");
        // config block carries instructions + length + the id list
        let cfg = spec[6].as_arr().unwrap();
        let inner = cfg[1].as_arr().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(inner[0].as_str(), Some("focus on evaluation"));
        assert_eq!(inner[1].as_f64(), Some(3.0), "LONG == 3");
        assert_eq!(inner[3].as_arr().unwrap().len(), 2, "one entry per source id");
    }

    #[test]
    fn quiz_and_flashcards_differ_only_by_variant_slot() {
        let ids = ids();
        let mut fb = ArtifactRequest::new(ArtifactKind::QuizFlashcards, "nb1", &ids);
        fb.study_variant = StudyVariant::Flashcards;
        let mut qz = ArtifactRequest::new(ArtifactKind::QuizFlashcards, "nb1", &ids);
        qz.study_variant = StudyVariant::Quiz;

        let fb_spec = fb.params();
        let qz_spec = qz.params();
        let fb_opts = fb_spec.as_arr().unwrap()[2].as_arr().unwrap()[0].as_arr().unwrap()[8]
            .as_arr()
            .unwrap()
            .clone();
        let qz_opts = qz_spec.as_arr().unwrap()[2].as_arr().unwrap()[0].as_arr().unwrap()[8]
            .as_arr()
            .unwrap()
            .clone();
        assert_eq!(fb_opts[0].as_f64(), Some(1.0), "variant 1 = flashcards");
        assert_eq!(qz_opts[0].as_f64(), Some(2.0), "variant 2 = quiz");
        assert!(!fb_opts[6].is_null() && fb_opts[7].is_null(), "flashcards pair at slot 6");
        assert!(qz_opts[6].is_null() && !qz_opts[7].is_null(), "quiz pair at slot 7");
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_artifact_kind_has_a_distinct_code() {
        let kinds = [
            ArtifactKind::Audio,
            ArtifactKind::Report,
            ArtifactKind::Video,
            ArtifactKind::QuizFlashcards,
            ArtifactKind::MindMap,
            ArtifactKind::FantasyMap,
            ArtifactKind::Infographic,
            ArtifactKind::SlideDeck,
            ArtifactKind::DataTable,
            ArtifactKind::File,
        ];
        let mut codes: Vec<i64> = kinds.iter().map(|k| k.code()).collect();
        codes.sort_unstable();
        codes.dedup();
        assert_eq!(codes.len(), 10);
        assert_eq!(ArtifactKind::from_code(1), Some(ArtifactKind::Audio));
        assert_eq!(ArtifactKind::from_code(99), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn chat_request_targets_the_streamed_endpoint_with_at_token() {
        let creds = Credentials { cookies: "SID=abc".into(), at: "AT 123".into() };
        let req = chat_request("nb1", "what is grounding?", &creds);
        assert!(req.url.contains("GenerateFreeFormStreamed"));
        assert!(req.body.starts_with("f.req="));
        assert!(req.body.contains("&at="), "at token is form-encoded alongside f.req");
        assert!(req.body.contains("AT%20123"), "space must be percent-encoded");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_length_framed_wrb_fr_responses() {
        // Shape taken from the documented framing: ')]}\'' prefix, len line, JSON row.
        let inner = json::to_string(&a(vec![s("hello")]));
        let escaped = json::to_string(&s(&inner));
        let row = format!(r#"[["wrb.fr","wXbhsf",{},null,null,null,"generic"]]"#, escaped);
        let raw = format!(")]}}'\n\n{}\n{}\n", row.len(), row);
        let frames = parse_frames(&raw).expect("frames");
        assert_eq!(frames.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(frames[0].as_arr().unwrap()[0].as_str(), Some("hello"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn streaming_chat_takes_the_final_cumulative_chunk() {
        let mk = |text: &str, final_chunk: bool| {
            let inner = json::to_string(&a(vec![
                a(vec![s(text)]),
                null(),
                null(),
                null(),
                Value::from(final_chunk),
            ]));
            let escaped = json::to_string(&s(&inner));
            format!(r#"[["wrb.fr","chat",{},null,null,null,"generic"]]"#, escaped)
        };
        let c1 = mk("The answer is", false);
        let c2 = mk("The answer is grounding.", true);
        let raw = format!(
            ")]}}'\n\n{}\n{}\n{}\n{}\n",
            c1.len(),
            c1,
            c2.len(),
            c2
        );
        assert_eq!(parse_stream_answer(&raw).unwrap(), "The answer is grounding.");
    }

    #[test]
    fn artifact_kickoff_is_decoded() {
        let frame = a(vec![a(vec![
            s("art-123"),
            s("Audio Overview"),
            n(1),
            null(),
            n(1),
        ])]);
        let (id, title, kind, status) = parse_artifact_kickoff(&frame).expect("kickoff");
        assert_eq!(id, "art-123");
        assert_eq!(title, "Audio Overview");
        assert_eq!(kind, 1);
        assert_eq!(status, 1, "1 == pending/initialized");
    }

    #[test]
    fn transport_is_unavailable_and_says_why() {
        let client = NotebookLmClient::new(
            Credentials { cookies: String::new(), at: String::new() },
            NoTransport,
        );
        assert!(!client.available(), "must never claim reachability");
        let err = client.call(RPC_LIST_NOTEBOOKS, &a(vec![])).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("no route") && err.contains("TLS"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn corroboration_counts_match_the_measured_evidence() {
        // Measured with docs/rea/ + scripts/fetch_notebooklm_evidence.sh:
        // occurrences of each id across the three independent codebases.
        for rpc in [
            RPC_ADD_SOURCE,
            RPC_ADD_SOURCE_FILE,
            RPC_LIST_NOTEBOOKS,
            RPC_CREATE_NOTEBOOK,
            RPC_GET_NOTEBOOK,
            RPC_CREATE_ARTIFACT,
            RPC_SUMMARIZE,
            RPC_DELETE_SOURCE,
            RPC_LIST_ARTIFACTS,
            RPC_CREATE_NOTE,
            RPC_GET_NOTES,
            RPC_GENERATE_MIND_MAP,
        ] {
            assert!(
                rpc.corroboration >= 2,
                "{} ({}) must be confirmed in >=2 independent implementations, got {}",
                rpc.name,

                rpc.corroboration
            );
        }
        assert_eq!(RPC_ADD_SOURCE.corroboration, 3, "izAoDd is in all three codebases");
    }

    #[test]
    fn status_reports_protocol_implemented_but_unreachable() {
        let st = status();
        assert_eq!(st.str_of("status"), Some("protocol_implemented_target_unreachable"));
        assert_eq!(st.get("reachable").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()), Some(false));
        assert_eq!(st.get("implemented").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()), Some(true));
        assert!(st.get("rpc").and_then(|v| v.as_arr()).unwrap().len() >= 10);
        assert!(st.str_of("provenance").unwrap().contains("notebooklm-py"));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Model-provider seam (bring-your-own-key) and the always-available local engine.
//!
//! Design contract:
//! * `Answerer` is the only way answers are produced.
//! * The **extractive** answerer always exists and needs no key or network.
//! * A remote provider can be *configured*, but it is only *used* when it reports
//!   itself available. In this build HTTPS is unavailable, so a configured
//!   provider is reported as configured-but-unusable instead of being silently
//!   ignored or faked. The fallback is stated in every response (`engine`,
//!   `engine_note`).
//!
//! API keys are never returned by any endpoint; only `key_set` is exposed.

use crate::domain::{Chunk, Source};
use crate::grounded::{self, Answer};
use crate::json::Value;
use crate::obj;
use std::path::PathBuf;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum ProviderKind {
    Extractive,
    OpenAiCompatible,
}

impl ProviderKind {
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            ProviderKind::Extractive => "extractive",
            ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => "openai_compatible",
        }
    }
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<ProviderKind> {
        match s {
            "extractive" => Some(ProviderKind::Extractive),
            "openai_compatible" | "openai" | "byok" => Some(ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ProviderConfig {
    pub id: String,
    pub kind: String,
    pub base_url: String,
    pub model: String,
    pub created_at: String,
}

impl ProviderConfig {
    pub fn to_json(&self, key_set: bool) -> Value {
        obj! {
            "id" => self.id.as_str(),
            "kind" => self.kind.as_str(),
            "base_url" => self.base_url.as_str(),
            "model" => self.model.as_str(),
            "created_at" => self.created_at.as_str(),
            "key_set" => key_set,
            // Honest availability, computed rather than assumed.
            "available" => false,
            "reason" => "this build has no TLS client, so https providers cannot be contacted",
        }
    }
}

/// Validate user-supplied provider settings. https is mandatory: sending an API
/// key in cleartext is never acceptable, even to a "local" model.
pub fn validate(kind: &str, base_url: &str, model: &str, api_key: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let k = ProviderKind::parse(kind).ok_or_else(|| format!("unknown provider kind '{}'", kind))?;
    if k == ProviderKind::Extractive {
        return Ok(());
    }
    if !base_url.starts_with("https://") {
        return Err("base_url must start with https:// (refusing to send a key in cleartext)".into());
    }
    if base_url.len() > 512 {
        return Err("base_url is too long".into());
    }
    if model.trim().is_empty() {
        return Err("model name is required".into());
    }
    if api_key.trim().len() < 8 {
        return Err("api key looks too short".into());
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub trait Answerer {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn available(&self) -> bool;
    fn reason(&self) -> String;
    fn answer(&self, question: &str, chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], max: usize) -> Result<Answer, String>;
}

/// The default engine: composes an answer only from retrieved source sentences.
pub struct ExtractiveAnswerer;

impl Answerer for ExtractiveAnswerer {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        "extractive"
    }
    fn available(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }
    fn reason(&self) -> String {
        "local extractive engine: answers are sentences quoted from your sources".into()
    }
    fn answer(&self, question: &str, chunks: &[Chunk], sources: &[Source], max: usize) -> Result<Answer, String> {
        Ok(grounded::answer(question, chunks, sources, max))
    }
}

/// Remote OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. Kept behind the same trait so a
/// future build with TLS can switch engines without touching the API layer.
pub struct RemoteAnswerer {
    pub cfg: ProviderConfig,
    pub api_key: String,
}

impl Answerer for RemoteAnswerer {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        "openai_compatible"
    }
    fn available(&self) -> bool {
        // Availability is a property of the build, not of the configuration.
        false
    }
    fn reason(&self) -> String {
        "provider configured, but this build cannot make TLS requests; using the local extractive engine".into()
    }
    fn answer(&self, _q: &str, _c: &[Chunk], _s: &[Source], _m: usize) -> Result<Answer, String> {
        Err("TLS/HTTPS is not available in this build; remote answering is impossible".into())
    }
}

/// Pick the engine to use. Never returns "none": there is always a local engine.
pub fn select(cfg: Option<&ProviderConfig>, key: Option<&str>) -> (Box<dyn Answerer>, String) {
    if let Some(c) = cfg {
        let remote = RemoteAnswerer { cfg: c.clone(), api_key: key.unwrap_or("").to_string() };
        if remote.available() {
            return (Box::new(remote), String::new());
        }
        let note = remote.reason();
        return (Box::new(ExtractiveAnswerer), note);
    }
    let e = ExtractiveAnswerer;
    (Box::new(e), String::new())
}

/// Secrets live outside the document database, with 0600 permissions.
pub fn secrets_path(data_dir: &std::path::Path) -> PathBuf {
    data_dir.join("secrets.json")
}

pub fn write_secret(data_dir: &std::path::Path, id: &str, key: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let path = secrets_path(data_dir);
    let mut map = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|s| crate::json::parse(&s).ok())
        .and_then(|v| match v {
            Value::Obj(m) => Some(m),
            _ => None,
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    map.insert(id.to_string(), Value::from(key));
    let tmp = path.with_extension("json.tmp");
    std::fs::write(&tmp, crate::json::to_string(&Value::Obj(map)))?;
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        let _ = std::fs::set_permissions(&tmp, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600));
    }
    std::fs::rename(&tmp, &path)
}

pub fn read_secret(data_dir: &std::path::Path, id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let s = std::fs::read_to_string(secrets_path(data_dir)).ok()?;
    let v = crate::json::parse(&s).ok()?;
    v.str_of(id).map(|x| x.to_string())
}

pub fn delete_secret(data_dir: &std::path::Path, id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let path = secrets_path(data_dir);
    let s = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).ok()?;
    let mut v = crate::json::parse(&s).ok()?;
    let removed = v.str_of(id).map(|x| x.to_string());
    if removed.is_some() {
        if let Value::Obj(ref mut m) = v {
            m.remove(id);
        }
        let _ = std::fs::write(&path, crate::json::to_string(&v));
    }
    removed
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn rejects_cleartext_endpoints_and_short_keys() {
        assert!(validate("openai_compatible", "http://api.example.com", "gpt", "sk-12345678").is_err());
        assert!(validate("openai_compatible", "https://api.example.com", "", "sk-12345678").is_err());
        assert!(validate("openai_compatible", "https://api.example.com", "m", "short").is_err());
        assert!(validate("openai_compatible", "https://api.example.com", "m", "sk-12345678").is_ok());
        assert!(validate("magic", "https://x", "m", "sk-12345678").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn extractive_engine_is_always_selected() {
        let (a, note) = select(None, None);
        assert_eq!(a.name(), "extractive");
        assert!(a.available());
        assert!(note.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn configured_remote_provider_states_its_limitation() {
        let cfg = ProviderConfig {
            id: "p1".into(),
            kind: "openai_compatible".into(),
            base_url: "https://api.example.com".into(),
            model: "m".into(),
            created_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z".into(),
        };
        let (a, note) = select(Some(&cfg), Some("sk-12345678"));
        assert_eq!(a.name(), "extractive", "must fall back, never pretend");
        assert!(note.contains("TLS"));
        let json = cfg.to_json(true);
        assert_eq!(json.get("available").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()), Some(false));
        assert!(!crate::json::to_string(&json).contains("sk-12345678"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn secrets_are_private_and_removable() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("forge-secret-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        write_secret(&dir, "p1", "sk-secret-value").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read_secret(&dir, "p1").as_deref(), Some("sk-secret-value"));
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            let mode = std::fs::metadata(secrets_path(&dir)).unwrap().permissions().mode();
            assert_eq!(mode & 0o777, 0o600, "secrets file must be owner-only");
        }
        assert_eq!(delete_secret(&dir, "p1").as_deref(), Some("sk-secret-value"));
        assert!(read_secret(&dir, "p1").is_none());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    }
}
```

## `crates/forge-core/src/retrieve.rs`

```rust
//! Lexical retrieval (BM25) over evidence chunks.
//!
//! Lexical retrieval is the backbone, not a fallback: exact terms, identifiers,
//! names and numbers are precisely what embeddings blur. Semantic retrieval can
//! be added as a second ranker later (docs/FEATURE_BACKLOG.md) without changing
//! this contract.

use crate::domain::Chunk;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap, HashSet};

const K1: f64 = 1.2;
const B: f64 = 0.75;

pub const STOPWORDS: &[&str] = &[
    "a", "an", "and", "are", "as", "at", "be", "been", "but", "by", "for", "from", "has", "have",
    "how", "i", "in", "is", "it", "its", "of", "on", "or", "that", "the", "their", "then", "there",
    "these", "they", "this", "to", "was", "were", "what", "when", "where", "which", "who", "why",
    "will", "with", "you", "your", "do", "does", "did", "can", "could", "should", "would", "about",
    "into", "than", "so", "if", "we", "our", "us", "me", "my",
];

pub fn tokenize(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    for ch in text.chars() {
        if ch.is_alphanumeric() {
            cur.extend(ch.to_lowercase());
        } else if !cur.is_empty() {
            out.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
        }
    }
    if !cur.is_empty() {
        out.push(cur);
    }
    out
}

/// Conservative suffix normaliser so "citation" matches "citations" and
/// "validated" matches "validate". Deliberately shallow: no dictionary, no
/// Porter stemmer, because over-stemming hurts precision on identifiers.
pub fn stem(term: &str) -> String {
    let t = term;
    if t.len() > 5 && t.ends_with("ies") {
        return format!("{}y", &t[..t.len() - 3]);
    }
    if t.len() > 5 && (t.ends_with("ses") || t.ends_with("xes") || t.ends_with("ches") || t.ends_with("shes") || t.ends_with("zes")) {
        return t[..t.len() - 2].to_string();
    }
    if t.len() > 3 && t.ends_with('s') && !t.ends_with("ss") && !t.ends_with("us") && !t.ends_with("is") {
        return t[..t.len() - 1].to_string();
    }
    if t.len() > 6 && t.ends_with("ing") {
        return t[..t.len() - 3].to_string();
    }
    if t.len() > 5 && t.ends_with("ed") {
        return t[..t.len() - 2].to_string();
    }
    t.to_string()
}

pub fn terms(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    tokenize(text)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|t| t.len() > 1 && !STOPWORDS.contains(&t.as_str()))
        .collect()
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Hit {
    pub chunk_index: usize,
    pub score: f64,
    pub matched_terms: Vec<String>,
}

/// BM25 over an in-memory chunk slice. Returns hits sorted by descending score.
pub fn search(chunks: &[Chunk], query: &str, limit: usize) -> Vec<Hit> {
    if chunks.is_empty() {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let q_terms: Vec<String> = {
        let mut seen = HashSet::new();
        terms(query)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|t| stem(&t))
            .filter(|t| seen.insert(t.clone()))
            .collect()
    };
    if q_terms.is_empty() {
        return Vec::new();
    }

    let docs: Vec<Vec<String>> = chunks
        .iter()
        .map(|c| tokenize(&c.text).iter().map(|t| stem(t)).collect())
        .collect();
    let n = docs.len() as f64;
    let avgdl = docs.iter().map(|d| d.len() as f64).sum::<f64>() / n;
    let avgdl = if avgdl <= 0.0 { 1.0 } else { avgdl };

    // document frequency per query term
    let mut df: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for t in &q_terms {
        let count = docs.iter().filter(|d| d.iter().any(|w| w == t)).count();
        df.insert(t.as_str(), count);
    }

    let mut hits = Vec::new();
    for (i, doc) in docs.iter().enumerate() {
        let dl = doc.len() as f64;
        let mut tf: BTreeMap<&str, usize> = BTreeMap::new();
        for w in doc {
            if let Some(t) = q_terms.iter().find(|t| *t == w) {
                *tf.entry(t.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
            }
        }
        if tf.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut score = 0.0;
        let mut matched = Vec::new();
        for t in &q_terms {
            let f = *tf.get(t.as_str()).unwrap_or(&0) as f64;
            if f == 0.0 {
                continue;
            }
            let dfi = *df.get(t.as_str()).unwrap_or(&0) as f64;
            let idf = ((n - dfi + 0.5) / (dfi + 0.5) + 1.0).ln();
            let denom = f + K1 * (1.0 - B + B * dl / avgdl);
            score += idf * (f * (K1 + 1.0)) / denom;
            matched.push(t.clone());
        }
        // Exact phrase bonus: query appearing verbatim is strong evidence.
        if chunks[i].text.to_lowercase().contains(&query.trim().to_lowercase())
            && !query.trim().is_empty()
        {
            score *= 1.5;
        }
        hits.push(Hit { chunk_index: i, score, matched_terms: matched });
    }
    hits.sort_by(|a, b| b.score.partial_cmp(&a.score).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
    hits.truncate(limit);
    hits
}

/// Best-matching sentences from a passage, used to build precise quotes.
/// Split text into candidate sentences, scoring each by stem-aware overlap with
/// the query. Returns `(overlap_ratio, sentence)` sorted best-first; sentences are
/// never invented, only sliced out of `text`.
/// Abbreviations whose trailing period does not end a sentence.
const ABBREVIATIONS: &[&str] = &[
    "e.g", "i.e", "etc", "vs", "cf", "al", "fig", "figs", "no", "vol", "pp", "p", "ch", "sec",
    "dr", "mr", "mrs", "ms", "prof", "sr", "jr", "st", "inc", "ltd", "co", "approx", "dept",
    "est", "min", "max", "avg", "ref", "eq", "art", "para", "ed", "eds",
];

fn is_abbreviation(word: &str) -> bool {
    let w = word.trim_matches(|c: char| !c.is_alphabetic()).to_ascii_lowercase();
    if w.is_empty() {
        return false;
    }
    ABBREVIATIONS.contains(&w.as_str()) || w.chars().count() == 1 // initials: "J. Smith", "U.S.A."
}

/// Split prose into sentences without breaking decimals ("0.42"), abbreviations
/// ("e.g.", "Dr.") or initials. Newlines always end a sentence; `;` does not.
///
/// A citation is only as good as the span it quotes, so this deliberately errs
/// towards keeping a sentence whole: a wrongly split sentence loses the number
/// the user asked about.
pub fn split_sentences(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < chars.len() {
        let ch = chars[i];
        if ch == '\n' {
            let t = cur.trim();
            if !t.is_empty() {
                out.push(t.to_string());
            }
            cur.clear();
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        cur.push(ch);
        if matches!(ch, '.' | '!' | '?') {
            let next = chars.get(i + 1).copied();
            let next_is_space = next.map(|c| c.is_whitespace()).unwrap_or(true);
            // a period inside a number (0.42) or a URL is not a boundary
            let prev_is_digit = cur
                .chars()
                .rev()
                .nth(1)
                .map(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
                .unwrap_or(false);
            let next_is_digit = next.map(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(false);
            let word_before: String = cur
                .trim_end_matches(|c: char| c == '.' || c == '!' || c == '?')
                .rsplit(|c: char| c.is_whitespace() || c == '(' || c == '"' || c == '\'')
                .next()
                .unwrap_or("")
                .to_string();
            let is_break = ch != '.'
                || (!(prev_is_digit && next_is_digit)
                    && !is_abbreviation(&word_before)
                    && next_is_space);
            if is_break {
                let t = cur.trim();
                if !t.is_empty() {
                    out.push(t.to_string());
                }
                cur.clear();
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let t = cur.trim();
    if !t.is_empty() {
        out.push(t.to_string());
    }
    out
}

pub fn scored_sentences(text: &str, query: &str, max: usize) -> Vec<(f64, String)> {
    let q: HashSet<String> = terms(query).into_iter().map(|t| stem(&t)).collect();
    // Single-word "sentences" (headings, page titles) are not evidence.
    let sentences: Vec<String> = split_sentences(text)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|t| t.len() > 20 && t.split_whitespace().count() > 3)
        .collect();
    if sentences.is_empty() {
        let t = text.trim();
        if !t.is_empty() {
            return vec![(0.0, t.chars().take(400).collect())];
        }
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let mut scored: Vec<(f64, String)> = sentences
        .into_iter()
        .map(|s| {
            let st: HashSet<String> = terms(&s).into_iter().map(|t| stem(&t)).collect();
            let overlap = if q.is_empty() {
                0.0
            } else {
                q.intersection(&st).count() as f64 / q.len() as f64
            };
            (overlap, s)
        })
        .collect();
    scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
    scored.truncate(max);
    scored
}

/// Best-scoring sentences, ignoring the score.
pub fn best_sentences(text: &str, query: &str, max: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    scored_sentences(text, query, max)
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(_, s)| s)
        .collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::domain::Locator;

    fn chunk(id: &str, text: &str) -> Chunk {
        Chunk {
            id: id.into(),
            source_id: "s1".into(),
            notebook_id: "nb".into(),
            ordinal: 0,
            text: text.into(),
            locator: Locator::paragraph(0, 0, 1),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn ranks_the_relevant_chunk_first() {
        let chunks = vec![
            chunk("a", "The weather in Kerala is humid during the monsoon season."),
            chunk("b", "Forge validates every citation against an indexed evidence span."),
            chunk("c", "Unrelated text about gardening and soil."),
        ];
        let hits = search(&chunks, "citation evidence span", 3);
        assert!(!hits.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(chunks[hits[0].chunk_index].id, "b");
        assert!(hits[0].score > 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn exact_identifiers_are_found() {
        let chunks = vec![
            chunk("a", "The configuration key is FORGE_DATA_DIR and it controls storage."),
            chunk("b", "Something else entirely about storage of grain."),
        ];
        let hits = search(&chunks, "FORGE_DATA_DIR", 2);
        assert_eq!(chunks[hits[0].chunk_index].id, "a");
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_match_returns_empty() {
        let chunks = vec![chunk("a", "apples and oranges")];
        assert!(search(&chunks, "kubernetes ingress", 5).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn stopword_only_query_returns_nothing() {
        let chunks = vec![chunk("a", "the quick brown fox")];
        assert!(search(&chunks, "the of and to", 5).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn sentence_selection_prefers_overlap() {
        let text = "The sky is blue. Forge citations point at exact evidence spans. \
                    Bananas are yellow.";
        let best = best_sentences(text, "where do citations point", 1);
        assert_eq!(best.len(), 1);
        assert!(best[0].contains("citations"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn tokenizer_handles_unicode_and_punctuation() {
        let t = tokenize("Caf√©, na√Øve ‚Äî 42% done");
        assert!(t.contains(&"caf√©".to_string()));
        assert!(t.contains(&"42".to_string()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn sentence_splitter_keeps_decimals_and_abbreviations_intact() {
        let s = split_sentences(
            "The evidence floor is 0.42 in this build. Anything below it is ignored. \
             See e.g. the retrieval notes for details. Dr. Rao wrote section 3.5 of the report.",
        );
        assert!(s[0].contains("0.42"), "decimal must not split: {:?}", s);
        assert_eq!(s.len(), 4, "got {:?}", s);
        assert!(s[2].contains("e.g. the retrieval notes"), "abbreviation split: {:?}", s);
        assert!(s[3].starts_with("Dr. Rao"), "title abbreviation split: {:?}", s);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sentence_splitter_ends_on_newlines_and_question_marks() {
        let s = split_sentences("What is grounding?\nIt is evidence-bound.\nSecond paragraph.");
        assert_eq!(s.len(), 3, "{:?}", s);
        assert_eq!(s[0], "What is grounding?");
        assert_eq!(s[1], "It is evidence-bound.");
    }

    #[test]
    fn scored_sentences_returns_the_sentence_containing_the_number() {
        let text = "Version 1.5 shipped earlier. The retry budget is 2.75 attempts per request.";
        let best = scored_sentences(text, "what is the retry budget", 1);
        assert_eq!(best.len(), 1);
        assert!(best[0].1.contains("2.75"), "got {:?}", best[0].1);
    }
}
```

## `crates/forge-core/src/security.rs`

```rust
//! Security helpers: URL/SSRF policy, path safety, size limits, output escaping.

use std::net::{IpAddr, ToSocketAddrs};

pub const MAX_SOURCE_BYTES: usize = 25 * 1024 * 1024;
pub const MAX_TEXT_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;
pub const MAX_URL_LEN: usize = 2048;
/// Rows kept per worksheet. Beyond this the grid is truncated and aggregations refuse
/// to run, because a total over a partial sheet would be a wrong number stated confidently.
pub const MAX_TABLE_ROWS: usize = 20_000;

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum UrlVerdict {
    Allowed(String),
    Rejected(String),
}

/// Validate a URL for ingestion.
///
/// Policy: only http/https; never localhost, link-local, private, CGNAT,
/// multicast or unspecified addresses; hostnames are resolved and ALL resolved
/// addresses must be public (defeats DNS-rebinding to an internal service).
pub fn check_url(raw: &str) -> UrlVerdict {
    let raw = raw.trim();
    if raw.is_empty() {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("empty url".into());
    }
    if raw.len() > MAX_URL_LEN {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("url too long".into());
    }
    let lower = raw.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let (scheme, rest) = match lower.split_once("://") {
        Some(v) => v,
        None => return UrlVerdict::Rejected("missing scheme (http/https)".into()),
    };
    if scheme != "http" && scheme != "https" {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected(format!("scheme '{}' is not allowed", scheme));
    }
    let authority = rest.split(['/', '?', '#']).next().unwrap_or("");
    if authority.is_empty() {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("missing host".into());
    }
    let host_port = authority.rsplit('@').next().unwrap_or(authority); // strip userinfo
    let host = if host_port.starts_with('[') {
        // IPv6 literal
        host_port
            .split(']')
            .next()
            .unwrap_or("")
            .trim_start_matches('[')
            .to_string()
    } else {
        host_port.split(':').next().unwrap_or("").to_string()
    };
    if host.is_empty() {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("missing host".into());
    }
    let host_lower = host.to_ascii_lowercase();
    if host_lower == "localhost" || host_lower.ends_with(".localhost") || host_lower.ends_with(".local") {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("localhost/.local hosts are blocked".into());
    }
    if host_lower == "metadata" || host_lower.contains("metadata.google.internal") {
        return UrlVerdict::Rejected("cloud metadata hosts are blocked".into());
    }
    if let Ok(ip) = host_lower.parse::<IpAddr>() {
        if !is_public_ip(&ip) {
            return UrlVerdict::Rejected(format!("address {} is not public", ip));
        }
        return UrlVerdict::Allowed(lower);
    }
    // resolve and check every address
    match (host_lower.as_str(), 80u16).to_socket_addrs() {
        Ok(addrs) => {
            let ips: Vec<IpAddr> = addrs.map(|a| a.ip()).collect();
            if ips.is_empty() {
                return UrlVerdict::Rejected("host did not resolve".into());
            }
            for ip in ips {
                if !is_public_ip(&ip) {
                    return UrlVerdict::Rejected(format!(
                        "host resolves to non-public address {}",
                        ip
                    ));
                }
            }
            UrlVerdict::Allowed(lower)
        }
        Err(e) => UrlVerdict::Rejected(format!("dns resolution failed: {}", e)),
    }
}

/// The pieces of an http(s) URL that matter for a safe fetch.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct ParsedUrl {
    pub scheme: String,
    pub host: String,
    pub port: u16,
    /// Path plus query, always starting with `/`.
    pub path_query: String,
}

impl ParsedUrl {
    pub fn authority(&self) -> String {
        let default = if self.scheme == "https" { 443 } else { 80 };
        if self.port == default {
            self.host.clone()
        } else {
            format!("{}:{}", self.host, self.port)
        }
    }

    /// Rebuild the URL we will actually request.
    pub fn to_url(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}://{}{}", self.scheme, self.authority(), self.path_query)
    }

    /// A normalised identity for de-duplication: lower-cased scheme/host, default
    /// port dropped, fragment removed, empty path ‚Üí "/", trailing "." removed.
    pub fn canonical(&self) -> String {
        let mut host = self.host.trim_end_matches('.').to_ascii_lowercase();
        if host.is_empty() {
            host = self.host.clone();
        }
        let default = if self.scheme == "https" { 443 } else { 80 };
        let auth = if self.port == default {
            host
        } else {
            format!("{}:{}", host, self.port)
        };
        let mut path = self.path_query.clone();
        if path.is_empty() {
            path = "/".to_string();
        }
        format!("{}://{}{}", self.scheme, auth, path)
    }
}

/// Parse an absolute http(s) URL without pulling in a URL crate.
///
/// Rejects: non-http(s) schemes, missing host, embedded credentials
/// (`user:pass@host`) ‚Äî the spec forbids forwarding userinfo ‚Äî and control
/// characters. Percent-encoding is preserved verbatim.
pub fn parse_url(raw: &str) -> Result<ParsedUrl, String> {
    let raw = raw.trim();
    if raw.is_empty() {
        return Err("empty url".into());
    }
    if raw.len() > MAX_URL_LEN {
        return Err("url too long".into());
    }
    if raw.chars().any(|c| c.is_control()) {
        return Err("url contains control characters".into());
    }
    let lower = raw.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let (scheme, _rest) = lower
        .split_once("://")
        .ok_or_else(|| "missing scheme (http/https)".to_string())?;
    if scheme != "http" && scheme != "https" {
        return Err(format!("scheme '{}' is not allowed", scheme));
    }
    let default_port: u16 = if scheme == "https" { 443 } else { 80 };

    // strip fragment; keep path+query from the *original* string to preserve case
    let no_frag = raw.split('#').next().unwrap_or("");
    let after_scheme = &no_frag[scheme.len() + 3..];
    let authority_end = after_scheme
        .find(|c| c == '/' || c == '?')
        .unwrap_or(after_scheme.len());
    let authority = &after_scheme[..authority_end];
    let path_query = match after_scheme[authority_end..].is_empty() {
        true => "/".to_string(),
        false => {
            let pq = &after_scheme[authority_end..];
            if pq.starts_with('/') { pq.to_string() } else { format!("/{}", pq) }
        }
    };
    if authority.is_empty() {
        return Err("missing host".into());
    }
    if authority.contains('@') {
        return Err("credentials embedded in the URL are refused".into());
    }

    let (host, port) = if authority.starts_with('[') {
        let close = authority.find(']').ok_or_else(|| "malformed IPv6 host".to_string())?;
        let host = authority[1..close].to_string();
        let rest = &authority[close + 1..];
        let port = if let Some(p) = rest.strip_prefix(':') {
            p.parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| "bad port".to_string())?
        } else {
            default_port
        };
        (host, port)
    } else if let Some((h, p)) = authority.rsplit_once(':') {
        (h.to_string(), p.parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| "bad port".to_string())?)
    } else {
        (authority.to_string(), default_port)
    };
    if host.is_empty() {
        return Err("missing host".into());
    }
    if port == 0 {
        return Err("port 0 is not allowed".into());
    }
    Ok(ParsedUrl { scheme: scheme.to_string(), host, port, path_query })
}

/// Why a name could not be turned into a usable address. Separating these matters:
/// a blocked address is a policy decision (4xx), an unresolvable name is a network
/// condition (5xx) and must not be reported as "refused by policy".
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum ResolveError {
    Blocked(String),
    Dns(String),
}

/// Resolve a host to public addresses only. Every returned address is
/// guaranteed to pass `is_public_ip`, so a fetcher can pin to one of them.
///
/// `FORGE_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1` disables the public-only rule. It exists so the
/// test suite can drive a loopback fixture server; the capability page reports
/// when it is on so it cannot be enabled silently.
pub fn resolve_public(host: &str, port: u16) -> Result<Vec<IpAddr>, ResolveError> {
    let literal = host.trim_start_matches('[').trim_end_matches(']');
    if let Ok(ip) = literal.parse::<IpAddr>() {
        return if is_public_ip(&ip) || allow_private() {
            Ok(vec![ip])
        } else {
            Err(ResolveError::Blocked(format!("address {} is not public", ip)))
        };
    }
    let addrs = (host, port)
        .to_socket_addrs()
        .map_err(|e| ResolveError::Dns(format!("cannot resolve {}: {}", host, e)))?;
    let ips: Vec<IpAddr> = addrs.map(|a| a.ip()).collect();
    if ips.is_empty() {
        return Err(ResolveError::Dns(format!("{} did not resolve", host)));
    }
    if !allow_private() {
        for ip in &ips {
            if !is_public_ip(ip) {
                return Err(ResolveError::Blocked(format!(
                    "{} resolves to non-public address {}",
                    host, ip
                )));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(ips)
}

/// True when the operator explicitly opted into private-network fetching.
pub fn allow_private() -> bool {
    std::env::var("FORGE_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE")
        .map(|v| v == "1" || v.eq_ignore_ascii_case("true"))
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

pub fn is_public_ip(ip: &IpAddr) -> bool {
    match ip {
        IpAddr::V4(v4) => {
            let o = v4.octets();
            !(v4.is_private()
                || v4.is_loopback()
                || v4.is_link_local()
                || v4.is_broadcast()
                || v4.is_multicast()
                || v4.is_unspecified()
                || (o[0] == 100 && (64..=127).contains(&o[1])) // CGNAT 100.64/10
                || (o[0] == 169 && o[1] == 254) // link-local / metadata
                || o[0] == 0)
        }
        IpAddr::V6(v6) => {
            !(v6.is_loopback()
                || v6.is_unspecified()
                || v6.is_multicast()
                || (v6.segments()[0] & 0xfe00) == 0xfc00 // unique local
                || (v6.segments()[0] & 0xffc0) == 0xfe80) // link local
        }
    }
}

/// Resolve a name inside a root directory, refusing traversal and absolute paths.
pub fn safe_join(root: &std::path::Path, rel: &str) -> Option<std::path::PathBuf> {
    if rel.contains('\0') {
        return None;
    }
    let cleaned = rel.trim_start_matches('/');
    let mut out = root.to_path_buf();
    for part in cleaned.split('/') {
        if part.is_empty() || part == "." {
            continue;
        }
        if part == ".." || part.contains('\\') || part.contains(':') {
            return None;
        }
        out.push(part);
    }
    // canonicalise to be sure (the target must exist for this check)
    let canon = out.canonicalize().ok()?;
    let root_canon = root.canonicalize().ok()?;
    if canon.starts_with(&root_canon) {
        Some(canon)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

pub fn escape_html(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '<' => out.push_str("&lt;"),
            '>' => out.push_str("&gt;"),
            '&' => out.push_str("&amp;"),
            '"' => out.push_str("&quot;"),
            '\'' => out.push_str("&#39;"),
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Restrict an uploaded filename to something safe for display only.
pub fn clean_filename(name: &str) -> String {
    let base = name.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or(name);
    let cleaned: String = base
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '-' | '_' | ' ' | '(' | ')'))
        .take(120)
        .collect();
    if cleaned.trim().is_empty() {
        "upload".to_string()
    } else {
        cleaned
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn blocks_ssrf_targets() {
        for bad in [
            "http://localhost/admin",
            "http://127.0.0.1:8080/",
            "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/",
            "http://10.0.0.5/",
            "http://192.168.1.1/",
            "http://[::1]/",
            "http://100.64.1.1/",
            "ftp://example.com/x",
            "file:///etc/passwd",
            "http://metadata.google.internal/",
            "not-a-url",
        ] {
            assert!(
                matches!(check_url(bad), UrlVerdict::Rejected(_)),
                "should reject {}",
                bad
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn allows_public_http() {
        // 93.184.216.34 is a public address; no DNS needed for the literal.
        assert!(matches!(check_url("http://93.184.216.34/page"), UrlVerdict::Allowed(_)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn ip_classification() {
        assert!(!is_public_ip(&"127.0.0.1".parse().unwrap()));
        assert!(!is_public_ip(&"10.1.2.3".parse().unwrap()));
        assert!(!is_public_ip(&"172.16.0.1".parse().unwrap()));
        assert!(is_public_ip(&"8.8.8.8".parse().unwrap()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn path_traversal_is_refused() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("forge-sec-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(root.join("ok.txt"), b"x").unwrap();
        assert!(safe_join(&root, "ok.txt").is_some());
        assert!(safe_join(&root, "../etc/passwd").is_none());
        assert!(safe_join(&root, "/etc/passwd").is_none());
        assert!(safe_join(&root, "a/../../etc/passwd").is_none());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root).ok();
    }

    #[test]
    fn html_escaping_prevents_markup() {
        assert_eq!(escape_html("<script>x</script>"), "&lt;script&gt;x&lt;/script&gt;");
    }

    #[test]
    fn filenames_are_sanitised() {
        assert_eq!(clean_filename("../../etc/passwd"), "passwd");
        assert_eq!(clean_filename("a/b/c.pdf"), "c.pdf");
        assert_eq!(clean_filename(""), "upload");
    }
}
```

## `crates/forge-core/src/store.rs`

```rust
//! Durable state: an in-memory `Db` written through to JSON on disk.
//!
//! Why not SQLite: crates.io is unreachable (docs/DECISIONS.md D1), and the
//! Rust standard library has no database. A single JSON document with atomic
//! replace (write temp + rename) is what we can verify end-to-end. See
//! docs/DECISIONS.md D2 for the scale limit this implies.

use crate::domain::*;
use crate::json::{self, Value};
use crate::obj;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct Db {
    pub notebooks: Vec<Notebook>,
    pub sources: Vec<Source>,
    pub chunks: Vec<Chunk>,
    pub conversations: Vec<Conversation>,
    pub notes: Vec<Note>,
    pub artifacts: Vec<Artifact>,
    /// Structured grids parsed from spreadsheet/CSV sources, stored verbatim so an
    /// aggregation after a restart uses the same cells it used before one.
    pub tables: Vec<crate::tables::Table>,
}

/// `Clone` is cheap and shares the same in-memory database (`Arc<Mutex<Db>>`). It exists so a
/// streaming response can take a handle it will use *after* the request handler returns, when
/// the answer has actually reached the client (see `http::StreamReply::on_finish`).
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Store {
    pub dir: PathBuf,
    inner: Arc<Mutex<Db>>,
}

impl Store {
    pub fn open(dir: impl AsRef<Path>) -> std::io::Result<Store> {
        let dir = dir.as_ref().to_path_buf();
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir)?;
        fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("backups"))?;
        let db = match fs::read_to_string(dir.join("db.json")) {
            Ok(text) => decode_db(&text).unwrap_or_default(),
            Err(_) => Db::default(),
        };
        let s = Store { dir, inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(db)) };
        if !s.path().exists() {
            s.save()?;
        }
        Ok(s)
    }

    pub fn path(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.dir.join("db.json")
    }

    pub fn read<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&Db) -> R) -> R {
        let guard = self.inner.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        f(&guard)
    }

    /// Mutate + persist. The write is atomic (tmp + rename) so a crash cannot
    /// leave a half-written database.
    pub fn write<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Db) -> R) -> std::io::Result<R> {
        let mut guard = self.inner.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        let out = f(&mut guard);
        let text = json::to_pretty(&encode_db(&guard));
        let tmp = self.dir.join("db.json.tmp");
        fs::write(&tmp, text.as_bytes())?;
        fs::rename(&tmp, self.path())?;
        Ok(out)
    }

    pub fn save(&self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.write(|_| ())
    }

    /// Rolling backup used by the export/backup workflow and manual recovery.
    pub fn backup(&self) -> std::io::Result<PathBuf> {
        let name = format!("backups/db-{}.json", now_iso().replace([':', 'T', 'Z'], "-"));
        let dest = self.dir.join(&name);
        let text = self.read(|db| json::to_pretty(&encode_db(db)));
        fs::write(&dest, text.as_bytes())?;
        Ok(dest)
    }
}

fn encode_db(db: &Db) -> Value {
    let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
    m.insert("schema".into(), Value::from("forge.db/1"));
    m.insert("notebooks".into(), Value::Arr(db.notebooks.iter().map(nb_json).collect()));
    m.insert("sources".into(), Value::Arr(db.sources.iter().map(source_json).collect()));
    m.insert("chunks".into(), Value::Arr(db.chunks.iter().map(chunk_json).collect()));
    m.insert(
        "conversations".into(),
        Value::Arr(db.conversations.iter().map(conv_json).collect()),
    );
    m.insert("notes".into(), Value::Arr(db.notes.iter().map(note_json).collect()));
    m.insert("artifacts".into(), Value::Arr(db.artifacts.iter().map(artifact_json).collect()));
    m.insert("tables".into(), Value::Arr(db.tables.iter().map(table_json).collect()));
    Value::Obj(m)
}

fn decode_db(text: &str) -> Option<Db> {
    let v = json::parse(text).ok()?;
    let arr = |key: &str| v.get(key).and_then(|x| x.as_arr()).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    Some(Db {
        notebooks: arr("notebooks").iter().map(nb_from).collect(),
        sources: arr("sources").iter().map(source_from).collect(),
        chunks: arr("chunks").iter().map(chunk_from).collect(),
        conversations: arr("conversations").iter().map(conv_from).collect(),
        notes: arr("notes").iter().map(note_from).collect(),
        artifacts: arr("artifacts").iter().map(artifact_from).collect(),
        tables: arr("tables").iter().filter_map(table_from).collect(),
    })
}

fn nb_json(n: &Notebook) -> Value {
    let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
    m.insert("id".into(), Value::from(n.id.as_str()));
    m.insert("title".into(), Value::from(n.title.as_str()));
    m.insert("description".into(), Value::from(n.description.as_str()));
    m.insert("instructions".into(), Value::from(n.instructions.as_str()));
    m.insert("tags".into(), json_str_list(&n.tags));
    m.insert("archived".into(), Value::Bool(n.archived));
    m.insert("created_at".into(), Value::from(n.created_at.as_str()));
    m.insert("updated_at".into(), Value::from(n.updated_at.as_str()));
    Value::Obj(m)
}

fn nb_from(v: &Value) -> Notebook {
    Notebook {
        id: s(v, "id"),
        title: s(v, "title"),
        description: s(v, "description"),
        instructions: s(v, "instructions"),
        tags: parse_str_list(v.get("tags")),
        archived: v.get("archived").and_then(|b| b.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),
        created_at: s(v, "created_at"),
        updated_at: s(v, "updated_at"),
    }
}

fn source_json(sr: &Source) -> Value {
    let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
    m.insert("id".into(), Value::from(sr.id.as_str()));
    m.insert("notebook_id".into(), Value::from(sr.notebook_id.as_str()));
    m.insert("title".into(), Value::from(sr.title.as_str()));
    m.insert("kind".into(), Value::from(sr.kind.as_str()));
    m.insert("origin".into(), Value::from(sr.origin.as_str()));
    m.insert("byte_len".into(), Value::from(sr.byte_len));
    m.insert("status".into(), Value::from(sr.status.as_str()));
    m.insert("error".into(), Value::from(sr.error.as_str()));
    m.insert("warnings".into(), json_str_list(&sr.warnings));
    m.insert("added_at".into(), Value::from(sr.added_at.as_str()));
    m.insert("page_count".into(), Value::from(sr.page_count as u64));
    m.insert("chunk_count".into(), Value::from(sr.chunk_count as u64));
    m.insert("content_hash".into(), Value::from(sr.content_hash.as_str()));
    m.insert("canonical_url".into(), Value::from(sr.canonical_url.as_str()));
    m.insert("fetched_at".into(), Value::from(sr.fetched_at.as_str()));
    m.insert("labels".into(), json_str_list(&sr.labels));
    let mut meta = BTreeMap::new();
    for (k, v) in &sr.meta {
        meta.insert(k.clone(), Value::from(v.as_str()));
    }
    m.insert("meta".into(), Value::Obj(meta));
    Value::Obj(m)
}

fn source_from(v: &Value) -> Source {
    Source {
        id: s(v, "id"),
        notebook_id: s(v, "notebook_id"),
        title: s(v, "title"),
        kind: s(v, "kind"),
        origin: s(v, "origin"),
        byte_len: v.get("byte_len").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as usize,
        status: s(v, "status"),
        error: s(v, "error"),
        warnings: parse_str_list(v.get("warnings")),
        added_at: s(v, "added_at"),
        page_count: v.get("page_count").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u32,
        chunk_count: v.get("chunk_count").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u32,
        content_hash: s(v, "content_hash"),
        canonical_url: s(v, "canonical_url"),
        fetched_at: s(v, "fetched_at"),
        labels: parse_str_list(v.get("labels")),
        meta: v
            .get("meta")
            .and_then(|m| m.as_obj())
            .map(|m| {
                m.iter()
                    .map(|(k, val)| (k.clone(), val.as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string()))
                    .collect()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default(),
    }
}

fn chunk_json(c: &Chunk) -> Value {

    m.insert("id".into(), Value::from(c.id.as_str()));
    m.insert("source_id".into(), Value::from(c.source_id.as_str()));

}

fn chunk_from(v: &Value) -> Chunk {

        source_id: s(v, "source_id"),
        notebook_id: s(v, "notebook_id"),
        ordinal: v.get("ordinal").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u32,
        text: s(v, "text"),
        locator: v.get("locator").map(Locator::from_json).unwrap_or(Locator::paragraph(0, 0, 0)),
    }

pub fn table_json(t: &crate::tables::Table) -> Value {
    use crate::tables::CellValue;
    let rows: Vec<Value> = t
        .rows
        .iter()
        .map(|r| {
            let cells: Vec<Value> = r
                .cells
                .iter()
                .map(|c| {
                    let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
                    m.insert("col".into(), Value::from(c.col as u64));
                    m.insert("header".into(), Value::from(c.header.as_str()));
                    m.insert("text".into(), Value::from(c.text.as_str()));
                    m.insert("ref".into(), Value::from(c.reference.as_str()));
                    m.insert("unit".into(), Value::from(c.unit.as_str()));
                    if let CellValue::Number(n) = c.value {
                        m.insert("num".into(), Value::from(n));
                    }
                    if let Some(f) = &c.formula {
                        m.insert("formula".into(), Value::from(f.as_str()));
                    }
                    Value::Obj(m)
                })
                .collect();
            obj! { "row" => r.number as u64, "cells" => Value::Arr(cells) }
        })
        .collect();
    obj! {
        "id" => t.id.as_str(),
        "source_id" => t.source_id.as_str(),
        "notebook_id" => t.notebook_id.as_str(),
        "sheet" => t.sheet.as_str(),
        "hidden" => t.hidden,
        "truncated" => t.truncated,
        "headers" => Value::Arr(t.headers.iter().map(|h| Value::from(h.as_str())).collect()),
        "warnings" => Value::Arr(t.warnings.iter().map(|w| Value::from(w.as_str())).collect()),
        "rows" => Value::Arr(rows),
    }
}

pub fn table_from(v: &Value) -> Option<crate::tables::Table> {
    use crate::tables::{Cell, CellValue, Row, Table};
    let id = s(v, "id");
    if id.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let headers: Vec<String> = v
        .get("headers")
        .and_then(|x| x.as_arr())
        .map(|a| a.iter().map(|h| h.as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string()).collect())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let rows = v
        .get("rows")
        .and_then(|x| x.as_arr())
        .map(|arr| {
            arr.iter()
                .map(|r| {
                    let cells = r
                        .get("cells")
                        .and_then(|x| x.as_arr())
                        .map(|ca| {
                            ca.iter()
                                .map(|c| {
                                    let text = s(c, "text");
                                    let num = c.get("num").and_then(|x| x.as_f64());
                                    let value = match num {
                                        Some(n) => CellValue::Number(n),
                                        None if text.is_empty() => CellValue::Empty,
                                        None => CellValue::Text(text.clone()),
                                    };
                                    Cell {
                                        col: c.get("col").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(1.0) as u32,
                                        header: s(c, "header"),
                                        value,
                                        text,
                                        reference: s(c, "ref"),
                                        unit: s(c, "unit"),
                                        formula: c.str_of("formula").map(|f| f.to_string()),
                                    }
                                })
                                .collect()
                        })
                        .unwrap_or_default();
                    Row {
                        number: r.get("row").and_then(|x| x.as_f64()).unwrap_or(0.0) as u32,
                        cells,
                    }
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    Some(Table {
        id,
        source_id: s(v, "source_id"),
        notebook_id: s(v, "notebook_id"),
        sheet: s(v, "sheet"),
        hidden: v.get("hidden").and_then(|b| b.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),
        truncated: v.get("truncated").and_then(|b| b.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false),
        headers,
        rows,
        warnings: v
            .get("warnings")
            .and_then(|x| x.as_arr())
            .map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|w| w.as_str().map(|x| x.to_string())).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default(),
    })
}

fn conv_json(c: &Conversation) -> Value {

fn note_json(n: &Note) -> Value {
```
