# 21. Final instruction

Build Forge as a complete, reliable, independent research product.

Investigate the reference product down to the smallest observable details. Use official documents, real browser workflows, screenshots, video analysis, yt-dlp, FFmpeg, FFprobe, REA, source-code research, tests, and real files wherever they are available and authorized.

Use every tool that genuinely helps. Do not spend days fighting a blocked tool when another evidence route is available. Do not mistake a tool's presence for proof that it can inspect the target.

**Research thoroughly. Preserve evidence. Separate facts from inference. Implement the real workflow. Test the complete path. Be honest about every limitation. Keep going.**
```

## `docs/NOTEBOOKLM_PROTOCOL.md`

```markdown
# NotebookLM protocol ‚Äî reverse-engineering record

**What this document is.** The evidence behind `crates/forge-core/src/notebooklm.rs`,
which implements Google Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM)'s web wire protocol: RPC ids,
`f.req` envelopes, source-spec layouts, artifact generation configs and the
streamed chat framing.

**What this document is not.** A claim that Forge can *talk* to NotebookLM from
this sandbox. It cannot ‚Äî see [Reachability](#5-reachability-verified-negative).

---

## 1. Method

No authenticated Google session exists in this environment and
`notebooklm.google.com` has no route (HTTP `000`). Direct observation was therefore
impossible. Instead the protocol was reconstructed from **public
reverse-engineering artefacts published by other projects**, and every constant was
required to appear in **at least two independent codebases** before being
implemented:

| Source | What it contributes | Pinned |
|---|---|---|
| `teng-lin/notebooklm-py` ‚Äî `docs/rpc-reference.md` | dated live CDP captures (2026-06-15, 2026-08-07) of the web client; RPC table, source specs, artifact configs, streaming framing, error shapes | commit `956400aa7af6b61b4cb988a24c9a081a3abc4ee8` |
| `jacob-bd/gemini-notebook-mcp-cli` ‚Äî `src/notebooklm_tools/core/utils.py` | independent RPC id constant table | default branch |
| `jackwener/OpenCLI` ‚Äî `clis/notebooklm/add-source.js` | independent `izAoDd` / `o4cbdc` usage and source-spec construction | default branch |

Re-fetch and re-hash at any time:

```bash
bash scripts/fetch_notebooklm_evidence.sh      # writes docs/rea/ + MANIFEST.md
```

`docs/rea/MANIFEST.md` records sha256 of every fetched file. The upstream files are
third-party MIT-licensed documentation; they are vendored here **as evidence**, not
as Forge source.

## 2. Corroboration, measured

Occurrence counts measured across the three vendored codebases
(`python3` scan of `docs/rea/`):

| RPC id | Method | notebooklm-py | jacob-bd | OpenCLI | Independent sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `izAoDd` | ADD_SOURCE | 5 | 1 | 1 | **3** |
| `o4cbdc` | ADD_SOURCE_FILE | 2 | 0 | 2 | **2** |
| `wXbhsf` | LIST_NOTEBOOKS | 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `CCqFvf` | CREATE_NOTEBOOK | 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `rLM1Ne` | GET_NOTEBOOK | 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `R7cb6c` | CREATE_ARTIFACT | 7 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `VfAZjd` | SUMMARIZE | 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `tGMBJ` | DELETE_SOURCE | 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `gArtLc` | LIST_ARTIFACTS | 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `CYK0Xb` | CREATE_NOTE | 3 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `cFji9` | GET_NOTES_AND_MIND_MAPS | 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `yyryJe` | GENERATE_MIND_MAP | 3 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `ASU5Oe` | RETRIEVE_RELEVANT_CHUNKS | 2 | 0 | 0 | 1 (single-source, flagged) |
| `I3xc3c` | LIST_LABELS | 2 | 0 | 0 | 1 (single-source, flagged) |

This table is asserted in code by
`notebooklm::tests::corroboration_counts_match_the_measured_evidence`, so the
numbers cannot silently drift from the docs.

## 3. Protocol facts implemented

### Transport
* `POST https://notebooklm.google.com/_/LabsTailwindUi/data/batchexecute?rpcids=<id>&rt=c`
* `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8`,
  `X-Same-Domain: 1`, `Cookie: <session>`
* Body: `f.req=<urlencoded JSON>`, where the JSON is
  **`[[[rpcId, "<params as a JSON string>", null, "generic"]]]`** ‚Äî a list of calls,
  each call a 4-element array, and the params are a *string*, not an object.
* Responses are length-framed after a `)]}'` anti-XSSI prefix; payloads arrive in
  `wrb.fr` frames and are JSON-encoded *again* inside `frame[2]`.

### Sources (`izAoDd`)
11-element spec array; positions are load-bearing:

| Kind | Position | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Web URL | `[2]` | `[url]` |
| Pasted text | `[1]` (pair) and `[3] = 2` | `[title, content]`, type code 2 |
| YouTube | `[7]` | `url` string (not `[2]`) |
| File upload | `o4cbdc` first | registers the file, returns `x-goog-upload-url` for a resumable upload |

### Artifacts (`R7cb6c`)
Content type codes: `1` audio, `2` report, `3` video, `4` quiz/flashcards,
`5` mind map, `6` fantasy map, `7` infographic, `8` slide deck, `9` data table,
`10` file. Audio carries `instructions`, a length code (`1` short, `2` default,
`3` long) and the source-id list. Type `4` differentiates by variant
(`1` = flashcards, `2` = quiz) and puts the `[quantity, difficulty]` pair at slot
`6` for flashcards or `7` for quiz.

### Chat
Separate streaming endpoint:
`.../LabsTailwindOrchestrationService/GenerateFreeFormStreamed`.
Chunks are **cumulative**; `envelope[4] == true` on exactly the last one. Forge's
parser takes the final frame and falls back to longest-wins (as the upstream client
does), and the fallback is visible in the code.

### Status codes
Artifact: `1` pending, `2` processing, `3` ready, `4` failed, `5` suggested.
Source rows: type code `3` PDF, `4` pasted text, `5` web page, `11` DOCX, `6` PPTX,
`17` EPUB, `9` YouTube, `10` media, `13` image, `16` CSV.

## 4. What Forge does with this

`forge-core/src/notebooklm.rs` (15 tests):

* builds and asserts the exact `f.req` envelope, URL, headers and body;
* builds source specs for URL / text / YouTube / file registration, asserting the
  documented slot positions;
* builds every artifact request, asserting type codes and the flashcard-vs-quiz
  slot difference;
* parses length-framed `wrb.fr` responses and cumulative chat streams;
* decodes the artifact kickoff row;
* exposes `GET /api/notebooklm/status` (machine-readable, with the RPC catalogue and
  corroboration counts) and `POST /api/notebooklm/preview`, which returns the **real
  wire request** it would send for `add_url`, `add_text`, `add_youtube`,
  `register_file`, `artifact` or `ask` ‚Äî with `"sent": false` and the reason.

The point of the preview endpoint is falsifiability: you can inspect the exact bytes
Forge would send, instead of taking a README's word for it.

## 5. Reachability (verified negative)

```bash
curl -sS -m 6 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://notebooklm.google.com   # 000
curl -sS -m 6 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://gemini.google.com       # 000
curl -sS -m 6 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://accounts.google.com     # 000
```

`000` means no TCP/TLS route ‚Äî not an auth failure, not a 403. The allowlist is
`github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `api.github.com`, `registry.npmjs.org`,
`pypi.org`. Additionally this Rust build has **no TLS client** (no crates), so even
a permitted host could not be reached over `https`.

`NotebookLmClient::available()` therefore returns `false` unconditionally and
`NoTransport::send()` returns the reason. When a reachable, TLS-capable build
exists, implementing `Transport` is the only missing piece.

## 6. Ethics and ToS

This is protocol documentation derived from public reverse-engineering projects; it
is used to (a) understand the product's observable behaviour for parity work and
(b) offer a bridge that a user would drive with **their own** authenticated session.
Forge does not scrape Google, does not ship credentials, and does not bypass any
access control: the bridge requires the user's own cookies and `at` token, and
Forge stores neither by default (`/api/notebooklm/preview` never transmits).
Automating a consumer product may violate its Terms of Service ‚Äî a user choosing to
connect their own session takes that decision knowingly.
```

## `docs/REA_EVIDENCE_INDEX.md`

```markdown
# REA investigation ‚Äî evidence index (run 2, corrected)

**Previous verdict in this file was wrong.** It said REA could not run here. It can.
This file records what actually happened when the claim was tested.

## 1. Node version: warning, not a wall

`rea-agents@6.8.0` declares `engines.node: "^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1"`.
The sandbox has **v22.22.3**. That is an npm **engine warning**, not an install
gate:

```bash
npm install --no-audit --no-fund --engine-strict=false rea-agents@6.8.0
# ‚Üí added 150 packages   (EBADENGINE warnings only)
./node_modules/.bin/rea --help      # ‚Üí full command list, 60+ commands, works
./node_modules/.bin/rea doctor      # ‚Üí runs, reports scope checks
```

**Correction:** upgrading Node was *not* required to run REA's CLI. (And upgrading
Node is not possible here anyway: `nodejs.org` and `nodejs.org/dist` are also
`HTTP 000`, so no official/nightly tarball can be fetched. npm only carries
arch-specific binary *packages*, not a Node runtime.)

`rea doctor` does report `node.ok: false` ‚Äî so upstream support would decline to
debug problems on 22.22.3. That is a support caveat, not an execution blocker.

## 2. What REA can and cannot do in this environment

`rea doctor` scope checks (verbatim, abridged):

| Check | Result | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| node | `missing_dependency` 22.22.3 | below the supported floor |
| host | ok (debian 12) | |
| hopper | `missing_analysis_engine` | macOS-only, absent |
| ghidra | `missing_analysis_engine` | `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` unset; Ghidra is a 400 MB Java download from GitHub **releases** ‚Äî this sandbox's GitHub *release asset* downloads return 302 ‚Üí 0 bytes (verified earlier) |
| ida-registration | `missing_analysis_engine` | needs a commercial IDA Pro + MCP registration ‚Äî forbidden (paid licence) |
| jadx | `missing_analysis_engine` | caller must supply the JAR; not downloadable here |

Web/browser capability: REA has `analyze-web-bundle`, `capture-browser-scenario`,
`capture-web-screenshot`, `discover-webmcp-tools`, all of which take a **CDP
endpoint or Playwright browser**. This image has **no browser at all**:

```bash
command -v chromium google-chrome firefox   # ‚Üí nothing
ls ~/.cache/ms-playwright                   # ‚Üí absent
```

So REA's web-inspection path has no target to attach to, independent of Google
being unreachable.

## 3. Could REA reverse-engineer Gemini Notebook here?

No, for **two independent** reasons ‚Äî either alone is sufficient:

1. **No reachable target.** `notebooklm.google.com`, `gemini.google.com`,
   `accounts.google.com` all return `HTTP 000` (no route). A web bundle cannot be
   captured from a host that is not on the network path.
2. **No browser and no CDP endpoint.** Even with a route, there is no Chromium to
   launch, no `playwright install` possible (its CDN is not allowlisted), and no
   authenticated Google session to capture from.

REA is the right tool; the environment lacks the two things it needs ‚Äî **a target**
and **a browser**.

## 4. What produced evidence instead

A different route that *is* reachable: **public reverse-engineering artefacts on
GitHub**. `api.github.com` is allowlisted, so the protocol documentation and
independent client implementations of three projects were fetched, hashed and
cross-checked, then implemented in Rust:

```bash
bash scripts/fetch_notebooklm_evidence.sh      # docs/rea/ + MANIFEST.md
```

| Evidence | Location | Hash |
|---|---|---|
| notebooklm-py RPC reference (live CDP captures 2026-06-15 / 2026-08-07) | `docs/rea/rpc-reference.md` | `99de80b9‚Ä¶5df46` |
| notebooklm-py web/Android behaviour notes | `docs/rea/web-android-public-behavior.md` | `9a9e52d0‚Ä¶7ef34` |
| jacob-bd RPC id table (independent) | `docs/rea/third-party-jacob-bd-utils.py` | `0dad74a6‚Ä¶d5f07` |
| OpenCLI add-source (independent) | `docs/rea/third-party-opencli-add-source.js` | `66eb84fb‚Ä¶48db2` |

Result: `crates/forge-core/src/notebooklm.rs` ‚Äî 14 RPC methods, source specs,
artifact configs and streamed-chat parsing, with 15 tests asserting exact wire
shapes. Full record: `docs/NOTEBOOKLM_PROTOCOL.md`.

**This is still not "I observed the live product."** Every fact is second-hand
(dated CDP captures published by others). It is labelled accordingly in
`FEATURE_PARITY.md` as **RE-OBSERVED (second-hand)**, never VERIFIED-BY-ME.

## 5. If you want live observation later

You need, in order:

1. A sandbox with a route to `*.google.com` (not available in this one) **and** a
   TLS-capable build (add a TLS client once crates or a vendored `rustls` exists).
2. A browser: `npm i playwright` + `npx playwright install chromium` (needs
   `cdn.playwright.dev`) ‚Äî or run REA on your own machine, where all of this works.
3. Your own authenticated session; then:
   `rea capture-browser-scenario` ‚Üí `rea analyze-web-bundle` for real captures, and
   diff them against `docs/NOTEBOOKLM_PROTOCOL.md`.

## 6. Honesty ledger

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "REA cannot run here" (previous version of this file) | **WITHDRAWN** ‚Äî it runs |
| "REA needs Node ‚â•22.23.4" | true, but it is a warning not a blocker |
| "Node could be upgraded" | **false in this sandbox** (nodejs.org unreachable) |
| "REA cannot reverse-engineer NotebookLM here" | true ‚Äî no route, no browser, no session |
| "The NotebookLM protocol is implemented in Forge" | true ‚Äî code + 15 tests |
| "Those protocol constants were observed live by me" | **false** ‚Äî second-hand, cited, hashed |
```

## `docs/RESEARCH_BLOCKERS.md`

```markdown
# Research blockers

Everything here was **tested**, not assumed. Each entry states the attempt, the exact
result, and what would unblock it. A blocker is never a reason to invent a finding.

Last verified: 2026-10-31.

## 1. Live product access ‚Äî BLOCKED

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| `curl https://notebook.google.com` from the sandbox | HTTP **000** (no route) |
| `curl https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/` | HTTP **000** (no route) |
| agent page-fetch tool ‚Üí `support.google.com` | **works** (this is how official docs were read) |
| browser for REA to attach to | none installed (`chromium` absent), and no authenticated session exists |
| user credentials | none available, and none will be requested in chat |

**Unblock:** the operator runs a browser with an authorised session and exposes a
loopback CDP endpoint, or grants a screen/recording; or the agent's page tool is
extended to the product origin.

**Consequence:** no `LIVE_OBSERVED` rows exist in `docs/reference/FEATURE_MATRIX.md`.
Every reference behaviour there is `OFFICIAL_DOCUMENTED`, `CODE_CORROBORATED`, or
explicitly `INFERRED`.

## 2. Video research ‚Äî PARTIAL (tooling unblocked, footage still BLOCKED)

| Tool | Status 2026-10-31 |
|---|---|
| `yt-dlp` | **installed** 2026.10.26 from the PyPI wheel |
| `ffmpeg` | **installed** 7.0.2 static (`imageio-ffmpeg` wheel; needs `chmod +x`) |
| `ffprobe` | absent (that wheel ships `ffmpeg` only) |
| `chromium` | absent |
| `tesseract` | absent |

The earlier entry here said no package route existed. That was wrong in one direction:
**PyPI is reachable** even though crates.io and GitHub release assets are not, so
`pip install --target=/tmp/mediapy yt-dlp imageio-ffmpeg` works.

What is still blocked is the evidence that matters: there is no authorized recording, no
route to any platform host, and no permission to download or republish third-party footage.
So `docs/reference/VIDEO_RESEARCH.md` now contains measurements of a clip **we generated**
(container metadata cross-checked against `ffmpeg -i`, mean-RGB timelines, a contact sheet)
and an explicit statement that none of it is evidence about another product. It records one
reusable finding: FFmpeg's `scene` filter is luma-based and missed a red‚Üígreen cut on our own
clip, so cut detection cannot rely on it.

**Consequence:** no video row in the feature matrix may be labelled `VIDEO_OBSERVED` about a
reference product. The label is used only for our fixture, and the matrix says so.

## 3. Broad web research / search providers ‚Äî BLOCKED

Sandbox egress is allowlisted to `api.github.com`. There is no search API key, and no
provider is reachable. Forge therefore implements **no** web-search provider today; the
Deep/Fast Research workflows are specified but unimplemented rather than faked.

**Note:** Forge *can* fetch URLs it is given (via `curl`) ‚Äî the guard and the fetcher are
tested against a real local HTTP origin ‚Äî but in this sandbox any public host fails at
connect, returning `502 fetch_failed` honestly.

## 4. Providers for generation (LLM, TTS, ASR, vision, embeddings) ‚Äî BLOCKED

No API keys, no credits, and the zero-budget constraint forbids paid services. Forge
ships provider *interfaces* (`providers.rs`, keys write-only and `0600`) and the local
extractive engine keeps working without any provider. Anything requiring a model is
marked `unsupported` in `/api/capabilities` with a reason.

## 5. REA

`rea-agents@6.8.0` installs and runs, but `analyze` needs ghidra/hopper/ida/kuna (none
present, one is paid, one macOS-only) and there is no browser target.
`inspect-artifact` (hashing/inventory) works. Full detail: `docs/REA_EVIDENCE_INDEX.md`.

## 6. What is *not* blocked

* official help-centre documentation (agent page tool);
* pinned public repositories via the GitHub API (`api.github.com` is reachable);
* local HTTP/HTTP fixtures, so network-facing code can be tested end-to-end;
* the full Rust toolchain (installed per session into `/tmp/forge-rust`).
```

## 2026-10-31 ‚Äî official documentation: sources and limits

Page: <https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16215270> ‚Äî "Add or discover
new sources for your notebook" (Computer). Read in full. Label:
`OFFICIAL_DOCUMENTED`.

Findings (verbatim-derived, not paraphrased into claims the page does not make):

1. **Source types listed**: audio (MP3/WAV "among others"), copy-pasted text, Google
   Docs, Google Slides **up to 100 slides**, Google Sheets **limited to 100k tokens**,
   images (avif, bmp, gif, heic, heif, ico, jp2, jpe, jpeg, jpg, png, tif, tiff, webp),
   docx, txt, md, pdf, csv, pptx, notes, Play Books/textbooks (text only), web URLs,
   ePub, YouTube URLs of **public** videos, Gemini Chats.
2. **Per-source ceiling**: "up to 500,000 words or up to 200MB for uploaded files".
3. **Source count**: "up to 50 sources (for Free users)", with a link to the limits page.
4. **Drive import**: auto-synced "every few minutes"; manual *"Click to sync with
   Google Drive"*; losing access makes the source inaccessible but it **still counts
   toward source limits**; chats and Studio will not reference it; footnotes and
   comments are **not** imported; multiple tabs of a Doc/Sheet import as one source.
5. **Web URL import**: only the **text** of the HTML is scraped ‚Äî images, embedded
   videos and nested pages are not imported; paywalled pages unsupported; a **PDF served
   over a URL is treated as a PDF source**.
6. **YouTube import**: public videos **with captions** only (uploader or auto);
   **transcript only**, no visual analysis; videos **< 72 h old may not be importable**;
   videos without speech unsupported; if a video is deleted or made private the source
   is **auto-deleted within 30 days**; captions over 500,000 words are not supported.
7. **Audio import**: transcribed **at import time** and the text is stored; a long list
   of container types (3g2‚Ä¶wma); **audio with no speech is unsupported**; ~50 supported
   languages are listed explicitly.
8. **Editing sources**: "When you update or delete a source, studio outputs generated
   with that source do not change." ‚Üê directly informs `¬ß10.3` stale-artifact handling.
9. **Summaries**: two modes ‚Äî ask in chat, or the **Source Guide** auto-summary in the
   left-side source viewer.

### What this changes in Forge

* **Refresh + staleness is now backed by documentation**: upstream Studio outputs are
  frozen, so Forge marks artifacts `stale` instead of silently rewriting them.
  Implemented this session (`POST /api/sources/:id/refresh` + `Artifact.stale`).
* **URL import must treat a PDF response as a PDF** ‚Äî implemented by sniffing
  `Content-Type` *and* the `%PDF` magic, then routing to the PDF parser.
* **Per-source ceilings**: Forge keeps its **own** configurable cap
  (`security::MAX_SOURCE_BYTES = 25 MiB`) and does **not** copy Google's 200 MB /
  500k-word numbers (`MASTER_FORGE.md` ¬ß2.10 forbids exactly that).

---

## 2026-10-31 ‚Äî what was implemented from that research

Not research, but this log is the honest record of what the evidence changed:

| Change | Evidence basis | Test |
|---|---|---|
| `fetch` module: SSRF-checked, DNS-pinned, hop-by-hop redirect fetch via `curl` | `¬ß11.3` policy + documented https-only reality | 11 unit tests + 3 e2e |
| URL ‚Üí source ingestion (title from `<title>`, canonical URL, content hash, dedup) | doc points 2/5 above | `url_source_is_fetched_indexed_cited_and_deduplicated` |
| PDF-over-URL routed to the PDF parser | doc point 5 | `detects_pdf_by_magic_even_without_a_content_type` |
| `POST /api/sources/:id/refresh` + `Artifact.stale` | doc point 8 | `refreshing_a_url_source_reindexes_only_when_content_changed` |
| Source rename + labels (`PATCH /api/sources/:id`) | ¬ß2.2 D source organisation | `pasted_sources_are_not_refreshable_and_labels_persist` |
| Sentence splitter keeps decimals/abbreviations intact | defective citation text found by the new e2e | 3 unit tests |

# Research plan

Last updated: 2026-10-31. Owner: the Forge implementation programme described in
`docs/MASTER_FORGE.md`.

## 1. What "research" means here

The reference product (**Gemini Notebook**, formerly NotebookLM) is treated as an
*evidence source*, never as a dependency. Each claim about it carries one of the
labels from `MASTER_FORGE.md` ¬ß3.1. Today only three of those labels are reachable
from this sandbox:

| Label | Reachable? | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `OFFICIAL_DOCUMENTED` | **yes** | `support.google.com` help pages, fetched and read in full this session |
| `CODE_CORROBORATED` | **yes** | pinned public repositories (protocol research, parsers) |
| `INFERRED` | **yes** | used only where marked |
| `LIVE_OBSERVED` | **no** | no browser, no authenticated account, no route to `notebook.google.com` |
| `VIDEO_OBSERVED` | **no** | `yt-dlp`/`ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` are not installed (see `RESEARCH_BLOCKERS.md`) |
| `COMMUNITY_REPORTED` | **no** | no general web egress from the sandbox |

## 2. Source priority actually used

1. **Official help centre** ‚Äî `support.google.com/gemininotebook/*`. Reachable by the
   agent's page-fetch tool even though the *sandbox* cannot route to it (curl to
   `support.google.com` returns 000). This distinction matters: it is the difference
   between reading the documentation and guessing from memory.
2. **Pinned public code** ‚Äî recorded with exact revisions and sha256 in
   `docs/rea/MANIFEST.md`.
3. **The specification itself** ‚Äî `docs/MASTER_FORGE.md` ¬ß2 is a research inventory
   written from official material; where I could verify a claim against the help
   centre I did, and where I could not, the row says so.

## 3. Instrumentation

* `scripts/research/fetch_docs.sh` ‚Äî records every help-centre page used as evidence,
  with URL, HTTP status, sha256 and retrieval date, into `docs/reference/official/`.
* Offline protocol research lives in `docs/rea/` (vendored, hashed).
* `bininspect` is used for **binary** evidence only; it is unrelated to product research.

## 4. Question order

Research is driven by implementation risk, not completeness:

| Order | Question | Why now |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What are the documented source types, and their limits? | decides the ingestion roadmap |
| 2 | How is source selection + citation described? | decides the chat/citation contract |
| 3 | Which Studio artifacts are documented, with what controls? | decides artifact scope |
| 4 | What do the docs say about notes-as-sources? | Journey D |
| 5 | Plans/limits/availability | must not be hard-coded as Forge limits |
| 6 | Mobile/accessibility differences | informs responsive work |

## 5. Rules I hold myself to

* A failed fetch is **not** evidence that a feature does not exist.
* Repeated copies of one claim are one evidence lineage, not several confirmations
  (`MASTER_FORGE.md` ¬ß3.2).
* No screenshots, transcripts, browser sessions, citations or test results are
  fabricated. Anything not executed is labelled as not executed.
* Google's quotas are never copied into Forge as product limits.
```

## `docs/SECURITY.md`

```markdown
# Security model

Forge is a **single-operator** application. It has no login, so the network
boundary *is* the trust boundary: run it on `127.0.0.1`, or behind your own
authenticated reverse proxy. This is stated rather than hidden ‚Äî there is no
"secure multi-user mode".

## Threats and controls

| Threat | Control | Test |
|---|---|---|
| SSRF via URL ingestion (cloud metadata, internal services) | `security::check_url`: http/https only; blocks `localhost`, `.local`, link-local, private, CGNAT 100.64/10, multicast, unspecified; **resolves DNS and rejects if any address is non-public**; length cap 2048 | `security::tests::blocks_ssrf_targets`, `allows_public_http`, `ip_classification`; e2e `rejects_bad_input_and_dangerous_urls` |
| Path traversal in static hosting | `security::safe_join` strips leading `/`, rejects `..`, `\`, `:`, then canonicalises and requires the result to stay under the root | `security::path_traversal_is_refused`, `web::traversal_and_missing_assets_are_refused`, e2e static test |
| Hostile uploaded filename | `security::clean_filename` takes the basename, keeps `[A-Za-z0-9._ -()]`, caps at 120 chars; uploads never write to disk under a user path | e2e uploads `../..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd` and asserts the stored title is sanitised |
| Stored XSS in source text / notes | the UI builds DOM with `textContent` (no `innerHTML` for user data); `security::escape_html` exists for any future HTML path; CSP `script-src 'self'` blocks inline scripts | `security::html_escaping_prevents_markup`, `http::responses_carry_security_headers`, UI smoke "no uncaught page errors" |
| Prompt injection in a document | no model is called in this build, so injected instructions cannot execute. If a provider is added, answers stay extractive-validated: `grounded::validate_citations` rejects any quote not literally present, so injected text cannot become a fake citation | `grounded::validator_catches_fabricated_quotes_and_ids` |
| API key leakage | keys are stored in `data/secrets.json` with mode `0600`, never returned (`key_set` only), never logged, never included in notebook export (`export` emits notebooks/sources/chunks/notes/artifacts only) | `providers::secrets_are_private_and_removable`, e2e `provider_keys_are_write_only_and_never_used_unsafely` |
| Cleartext key transmission | `providers::validate` refuses any `base_url` not starting with `https://` | `providers::rejects_cleartext_endpoints_and_short_keys` |
| Oversized request bodies | header cap 64 KiB, body cap 32 MiB at the HTTP layer; `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` 25 MiB, `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` 8 MiB at the API | `http` tests; e2e empty/oversize upload |
| Oversized worksheets (memory/JSON blow-up) | `MAX_TABLE_ROWS` 20,000 rows per sheet; the grid is marked `truncated` and aggregations **refuse** instead of totalling partial data | `tables::tests::oversized_sheets_are_truncated_and_aggregations_refuse` |
| Table rows leaking into an HTTP response | `GET /api/sources/:id/tables?rows=N` caps rows (default 200, max 2,000) while `row_count` reports the true size | e2e `spreadsheet_questions_are_computed_over_real_cells` |
| Hostile media files | container parsing is bounds-checked at every read (`u32`/`u64` box sizes, `0`-size guard, truncation tolerated and reported); no allocation is sized from an unvalidated box length; body capped at `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` (`413 too_large`), empty body `400` | `media` tests (`truncated_file_is_reported_not_guessed`, `sixty_four_bit_box_sizes_are_understood`), e2e `media_metadata_is_read_without_decoding_frames` |
| Hidden worksheets used as evidence | hidden sheets are stored for inspection but excluded from retrieval, aggregation and citations | `tables::tests::hidden_sheets_are_never_used_for_answers` |
| Fabricated numbers from a spreadsheet | non-numeric/empty cells are `Empty` (never `0`), mixed units are refused, cached column totals are excluded and named, ambiguous separators are rejected | `tables` tests (4 refusal cases) |
| Malformed JSON / unknown routes | strict parser ‚Üí `400 bad_json`; unknown route ‚Üí `404 not_found` with a code | e2e `rejects_bad_input_and_dangerous_urls` |
| Zip bombs / hostile OOXML | entries are read through the central directory with declared sizes; the ZIP reader rejects ZIP64, unknown compression and out-of-bounds offsets; DOCX/PPTX/XLSX extraction reads only named parts (not every entry) | `ingest::zip::rejects_non_zip_and_garbage`, `ingest::ooxml::non_ooxml_is_rejected_clearly` |
| Data corruption / partial writes | every mutation rewrites a temp file and `rename`s it; a corrupt `db.json` decodes to an empty database instead of crashing | `store` tests incl. corrupt-db safety |
| Clickjacking / MIME sniffing / referrer leaks | `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, CSP with `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'`, `form-action 'self'` | `http::responses_carry_security_headers` |

## Deliberate non-goals

* **No authentication.** Not a bug: adding a half-baked login would imply a
  security property that is not tested. Bind to localhost or use your proxy.
* **No rate limiting.** Single operator, local socket.
* **No sandboxing of parsed files.** Parsers are pure Rust over byte slices; the
  process does not execute document content.
* **No TLS.** Therefore no URL fetching and no remote providers.

## Residual risks

1. The PDF object scanner is heuristic; a malformed PDF yields an empty source with
   a warning rather than a crash, but a pathological file could still be slow.
2. `data/` contains the full corpus in plain text. Protect the directory; it is
   git-ignored, and `secrets.json` is owner-only.
3. A reverse proxy with its own header limits should sit in front if exposed beyond
   localhost.

## Reporting

This is a local project with no deployed service. Record findings in
`docs/UNKNOWN_AND_LIMITATIONS.md` and add a failing test before fixing.

## URL fetching controls (added 2026-10-31)

| Control | Implementation |
|---|---|
| scheme allowlist | `http`, `https` only, at parse time and again via `--proto`/`--proto-redir` |
| credentials in URL | refused explicitly (`user:pass@host` ‚Üí 422 `url_rejected`) |
| userinfo forwarding | never sent; curl receives no `-u`, no cookies, no proxy |
| host resolution | Forge resolves, then requires **every** address to be public |
| DNS rebinding | defeated by pinning curl to the validated IP with `--resolve` |
| redirects | curl does not follow; each hop re-validated and re-pinned, max 5 |
| response size | 20 MiB (`--max-filesize` + a second check after read) |
| time | 30 s (`--max-time`) |
| metadata endpoints | `169.254.169.254`, `metadata.google.internal` blocked by IP and hostname |
| loopback/private | blocked unless `FORGE_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1`, which is reported in capabilities |
| shell injection | `Command::new("curl").args([‚Ä¶])` ‚Äî no shell, no interpolation, no user-controlled argv flags |
| temp files | per-request unique names in the system temp dir, removed after every request including failures |

Residual risk: `curl` itself is third-party code parsing hostile HTTP. It runs as the
server's user, in a subprocess, with output restricted to two temp files. A compromised
curl is out of scope for this layer.
```

## Not available, with reasons

| Feature | Why | Honest behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| URL / YouTube / Instagram / GitHub ingestion | build has no TLS client; sandbox has no outbound route to arbitrary hosts | `POST /sources/url` validates the URL (SSRF guard) then returns **501 `url_ingest_unavailable`** with instructions |
| Remote LLM providers | HTTPS unavailable; keys are accepted and stored but a provider reports `available:false` | chat stays on the extractive engine and returns `engine_note` explaining the fallback |
| Audio/video overviews, transcription | no TTS/ASR engine reachable from the product (FFmpeg is used only as research tooling, installed from PyPI during this session) | `audio_overview` is `unsupported`; `audio_script` (**text**) is generated instead; media **metadata** is readable (row above) but frames, captions and speech are not |
| Image OCR | `tesseract` absent | images inside DOCX are counted in warnings, not read |
| Semantic/vector retrieval | no embedding model offline | lexical BM25 only; documented, not disguised |
| Multi-user auth | out of scope for a single-operator notebook | bind to `127.0.0.1` or a private network |
| Spreadsheet formula evaluation | no formula engine; only the cached value Excel/LibreOffice stored is read | the cached value is used **and the formula is printed** (`=SUM(C2:C3)`) so a derived cell is never mistaken for data |
| Sheets beyond 20,000 rows | self-imposed cap (`security::MAX_TABLE_ROWS`) | the grid is marked `truncated`, the reason is reported, and aggregations **refuse** rather than total a partial sheet |
| `.xls` (BIFF), ODS, Google Sheets | no parser written; binary formats out of scope for now | upload is rejected by kind detection with a clear error, never half-indexed |
| Data Tables artifact (schema-inferred extraction, charts) | not implemented | reported as `planned`; existing spreadsheets are queried directly instead |
| Model-written source summaries | no reachable LLM (no TLS client, no key) | the Source Guide is **extractive**: every line is a quotation with its locator, and the payload says `generated_by: extractive`, `model: null` |
| Token-by-token generation | there is no model to generate tokens; the extractive answer exists in full before the first frame | the stream is honest about it: the `start` frame says `delivery: "extractive answer computed first, then delivered in frames"`, and the transport is genuinely chunked. Frames carry real sentences, never placeholders |
| Style / length for a remote provider | no provider is reachable | the citation budget is passed to a provider when one is used; the style vocabulary is documented as extractive-engine only |
| Calling NotebookLM / Gemini Notebook | `notebooklm.google.com`, `gemini.google.com`, `accounts.google.com` all return HTTP 000; no TLS client; REA has no browser to attach to | protocol implemented and inspectable via `GET /api/notebooklm/status` and `POST /api/notebooklm/preview` (returns the exact wire request, `sent:false`) |

## Immediate next steps

1. EPUB ingestion ‚Äî the ZIP reader already exists; needs XHTML container mapping.
2. Conversation export as Markdown; artifact re-generation on source change.
3. Verify the ¬ß14 acceptance journeys A‚ÄìK one by one and close the gaps (in progress).
4. Wire an HTTPS client (requires a TLS-capable toolchain/route) to switch URL
   ingestion and remote providers from "configured but unavailable" to working.
5. Optional: local embedding index once a model can be shipped offline.

| `rejects_bad_input_and_dangerous_urls` | empty question 422, no-sources 409, four SSRF URLs 422 `url_rejected`, public URL 501 `url_ingest_unavailable`, bad JSON 400, unknown route 404, hostile upload filename sanitised |
| `static_app_is_served_over_http` | `/` and `/app.js` served; `/../../Cargo.toml` not served |
| `imports_office_formats_over_http` | DOCX/PPTX/XLSX upload ‚Üí correct `kind` and locator kind; a DOCX answer carries a `paragraph` citation |
| `source_guide_quotes_the_source_and_refuses_when_empty` | guide is extractive (`model: null`); headline is a substring of a stored chunk; every summary line resolves to a real chunk + locator; unknown source 404; unextractable source 409 |
| `chat_style_and_length_are_effective_and_validated` | `settings` echoed; brief ‚Üí 1 citation; detailed shows per-quote source + locator; concise and detailed cite the same passages; unknown style/length ‚Üí 422 and nothing stored |
| `chat_streams_frames_and_only_persists_when_delivery_completes` | NDJSON frames in order (`start` ‚Üí `delta`* ‚Üí `citations` ‚Üí `done`); every delta is a substring of the final answer, in order; `conversation_id` on a second stream appends instead of starting a new conversation; **a stream the client hangs up on is not stored** (message count unchanged after the abort); an invalid style returns `422` without opening a stream |
| `media_metadata_is_read_without_decoding_frames` | `sample.mp4` ‚Üí mp4, ~6200 ms, avc1 320√ó240 @ 10 fps, `decoded_frames: 0`, `transcript: "not produced"`; Matroska bytes ‚Üí `matroska` with **no** invented tracks; empty body 400; GET 404 |
| `provider_keys_are_write_only_and_never_used_unsafely` | http endpoint refused, valid config stored, list response contains no key, chat falls back with an `engine_note` mentioning TLS, backup created and listed |

## Spreadsheet tables and computed answers (22 unit tests + 1 store round-trip + 1 e2e + 12 UI assertions)

Test module `tables`; fixture `tests/fixtures/sales.xlsx` (two sheets, one hidden, real cell
references, a cached `SUM(C2:C3)` subtotal, an empty cell, an `N/A` placeholder, an inline

**Parsing**
* `csv_handles_quotes_commas_newlines_and_crlf` ‚Äî RFC 4180: `"Acme, Inc"`, `""` escapes, a
  newline inside quotes, CRLF line endings.

  row 2 / cell `B2`.
* `ragged_and_blank_headers_are_reported_not_guessed` ‚Äî empty header ‚Üí `Column B`,
  duplicate header ‚Üí `name (2)`, extra fields ‚Üí an added column, each with a warning.
* `numbers_parse_with_units_currency_and_accounting_negatives` ‚Äî `1,234.5`, `$1,200`, `45%`,
  `(1,200)`, `12 kg`, `-3.5` parse; `N/A`, `-`, `12abc34`, `two` do not.

* `xlsx_parses_every_sheet_with_real_cell_references` ‚Äî both sheets, `C2 = 1200.5`, cached
  `C4 = 2050.5` with `formula = SUM(C2:C3)`, empty `D4`, `N/A` ‚Üí empty, inline string ‚Üí number,

* `csv_fixture_sniffs_delimiter_and_handles_quoted_commas` ‚Äî the same file end-to-end.

## Source Guide (8 unit tests + 1 e2e + 9 UI assertions)

`guide` module. Every line of the guide is a **quotation** from an indexed passage with that
passage's id and locator; nothing is paraphrased and no model is claimed
(`generated_by: "extractive"`, `model: null`).

* `every_summary_sentence_is_a_verbatim_quote_with_a_real_locator` ‚Äî each quoted sentence is a
  substring of its chunk and carries the chunk's own `human()` locator.
* `summary_prefers_distinct_ideas_over_repeats` ‚Äî no two summary lines exceed 0.55 Jaccard, and
  the summary spans more than one passage.
* `topics_are_content_words_with_locations_and_a_stable_order` ‚Äî same input ‚Üí identical topic
  order; stopwords excluded; `Calvin cycle` surfaces as a **phrase** and its two words are not
  listed again.
* `a_single_short_source_says_so_instead_of_padding` ‚Äî warnings instead of invented content.
* `a_source_without_passages_refuses` ‚Äî `Err`, so the API returns `409 guide_unavailable`
  rather than an empty guide.
* `outline_uses_real_structure_only` ‚Äî markdown sections in document order; XLSX sheets with
  row counts and a hidden marker.
* `suggested_questions_are_grounded_in_observed_topics_and_columns` ‚Äî questions come from
  observed topics and real numeric columns; hidden sheets are never suggested.
* `the_guide_json_is_complete_and_serialisable`.

Over HTTP: `source_guide_quotes_the_source_and_refuses_when_empty` ‚Äî `generated_by`,
`model: null`, `deterministic: true`; the headline is a substring of a stored chunk; every
summary line resolves to a real chunk id with a locator; topics carry locations; unknown source
‚Üí `404`; a source whose extraction failed ‚Üí `409 guide_unavailable`.

UI: `source item offers a guide`, `source guide renders`, `guide says it is quoted, not
generated`, `guide quotes the source verbatim`, `guide quotes carry a locator`, `guide lists
recurring terms`, `guide suggests a question`, `clicking a suggestion fills the composer`,

## Chat streaming and Stop (2 unit tests + 1 e2e + 7 UI assertions)

Transport: `http::StreamReply` + `write_stream`. The response is `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`
with a `<hex>\r\n‚Ä¶\r\n` frame per event, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, and a `0\r\n\r\n`
terminator. `on_finish(complete)` fires exactly once; the API stores the turn **only** when
`complete` is true, which is what makes Stop more than a UI gesture.

Frames: `start` (question, engine, settings, and the sentence that says the answer is computed
first), `delta` (substrings of the real answer, in order), `citations`, `done` (the same body the
buffered route returns, plus `persisted_on_delivery: true`). `?pace_ms=` (‚â§1000) is a diagnostic
that sleeps between frames; it adds delay only and no content depends on it.

UI: `a Stop control appears while the answer streams`, `partial text is rendered before the
answer finishes`, `stopping says the turn was not saved`, `stopped turn is marked, not presented
as an answer`, `a stopped turn is not written to the conversation`, `a completed stream renders
its citations`, `a completed stream is saved once`.

## Media metadata (10 unit tests + 1 e2e + 2 UI assertions)

`media` module ‚Äî a hand-written ISO base media (MP4/M4A/MOV) parser. No FFmpeg, no
`ffprobe`, no codec: it walks the box tree and reads `mvhd`/`tkhd`/`mdhd`/`hdlr`/`stsd`/`stts`.

The same file was read by two independent implementations and they agree:
`media::inspect(sample.mp4)` ‚Üí container `mp4`, brands `isom/iso2/avc1/mp41`, duration
**6200 ms**, timescale 1000, track `avc1` 320√ó240, timescale 10240, **62 samples**, 10 fps,
rotation 0; `ffmpeg -i` on the same bytes ‚Üí `Duration: 00:00:06.20`, `320x240`, `10 fps`,
`10240 tbn`. `ffprobe` is not available, so ffmpeg's stderr is the second opinion.

* `reads_duration_streams_size_and_frame_rate` ‚Äî a built box tree yields duration, timescale,
  codec fourcc, sample count, fps derived from `stts`, and 16.16 display size.
* `reads_display_rotation_from_the_track_matrix` ‚Äî 90/180/270 from the matrix in `tkhd` (and
  `0` for the identity matrix), not inferred from swapped width/height.
* `json_reports_absent_values_as_null_not_zero` ‚Äî absent duration/fps/channels serialise as
  `null`; a missing value never becomes a measured `0`.
* `truncated_file_is_reported_not_guessed` ‚Äî a file cut mid-box returns what was parsed plus a
  warning naming the truncation; nothing is inferred past the cut.
* `missing_moov_is_a_warning_and_no_tracks` ‚Äî metadata that never arrives ‚Üí warning,
  `duration_ms: null`, zero tracks.
* `fragmented_mp4_is_flagged` ‚Äî `mvex`/`sidx` present ‚Üí `fragmented: true`, with the warning
  that sample counts are then only a lower bound.
* `other_containers_are_named_but_not_parsed` ‚Äî EBML (WebM/Matroska), MPEG-TS sync bytes and
  `RIFF‚Ä¶AVI ` are named by magic and then **refused** with zero tracks; text is `unknown`.
* `sixty_four_bit_box_sizes_are_understood` ‚Äî `largesize` boxes parse; a 32-bit reader would
  mis-walk the file.
* `absurd_sample_tables_saturate_instead_of_overflowing` ‚Äî `stts` entries of
  (`u32::MAX` samples, `u32::MAX` delta) would overflow the `u64` multiply; the parser
  saturates (`u64::MAX`) instead of panicking in a debug build, and a truncated entry list
  stops at the last complete entry.
* `a_real_encoder_output_is_read_correctly` ‚Äî the committed fixture, end to end.

Over HTTP: `POST /api/media/inspect?name=‚Ä¶` with the raw file; the response separates what was
read (`media`) from what was not (`notes.decoded_frames: 0`, `captions: "not read"`,
`transcript: "not produced"`). Empty body `400 empty_body`; oversized `413 too_large`.

UI: `capabilities discloses the media-metadata scope`, `capabilities marks video ingestion
unsupported with a reason`.

## Not covered (honest gaps)

* No real browser engine: CSS layout is asserted at the media-query level only.
* No concurrency/load test; store writes are serialised by a mutex.
* No fuzzing of the PDF/ZIP parsers.
* No multi-megabyte corpus test.
* Spreadsheet fixtures are synthetic: no real-world `.xlsx` produced by Excel, Numbers or
  LibreOffice was tested (no authorized sample), so merged cells, date serials, sheet-scoped
  named ranges and shared-formula groups remain unverified.
* No `.xls`/ODS fixtures at all ‚Äî those formats have no parser here.
* Streaming is *delivery* streaming, not generation: the extractive answer is complete before the first frame. There is no test ‚Äî and cannot be one here ‚Äî for token-by-token output, because there is no model.
* The `?pace_ms=` diagnostic is exercised by tests; nothing asserts browser rendering smoothness under a slow network.
* No decoded pixel, caption or transcript is produced by the product. Frame decoding was used
  **only** as research tooling on a fixture we encoded ourselves (`docs/reference/VIDEO_RESEARCH.md`);
  no vision model, no ASR, no authorized third-party footage.
* Media parsing is MP4-family only; Matroska/WebM, MPEG-TS and AVI are detected and refused, so
  their durations and codecs are genuinely unknown here rather than merely untested.
* No corrupted-but-parseable video fixtures (e.g. a valid `moov` with wrong `stco` offsets):
  we test truncation and absence, not every malformed combination.
```

## `docs/UNKNOWN_AND_LIMITATIONS.md`

```markdown
# Unknowns and limitations

Written to prevent a future session (or a user) from mistaking a limitation for a
bug, or a limitation for a feature.

## Hard environmental limits

1. **No crates.** `crates.io`, `static.crates.io`, `index.crates.io`, `docs.rs` are
   unreachable. Every dependency-free subsystem is hand-written; the cost is
   visible in `DECISIONS.md` D1.
2. **No TLS.** The standard library has no TLS client and no crate can be added, so
   HTTPS is impossible. Consequences: URL/YouTube/GitHub/Instagram ingestion,
   remote LLM providers, and online source discovery are all unavailable, and the
   API says so (`501`, `available:false`).
3. **No speech or vision engine.** `espeak`, `espeak-ng`, `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe` and
   `tesseract` are absent. No audio overviews, no transcription, no OCR.
4. **No live NotebookLM access.** REA could not run (Node version floor, no
   authenticated product session), so parity claims are REFERENCE-DOCUMENTED only.
5. **Ephemeral Rust toolchain.** It lives in `/tmp/forge-rust`; a sandbox recycle
   removes it. `scripts/install-rust.sh` re-creates it via the npm-hosted prebuilt
   binaries.

## Parser limitations (known, tested for the good path)

* **PDF.** Object scanning is heuristic; `/Length` may be indirect (falls back to
  `endstream` scanning); `/ToUnicode` CMaps are not applied, so non-Latin-1 text can
  be garbled; encrypted PDFs are rejected with a warning; scanned (image-only) PDFs
  yield no text. Only `Tj`, `TJ`, `'` and `"` operators are read ‚Äî no text in
  Type3 fonts, no layout reconstruction (columns read in stream order).
* **DOCX.** Only `word/document.xml`; headers, footers, comments, footnotes, tables
  rendered as text runs and text boxes are not modelled. Images are counted, not
  read.
* **PPTX.** Slide text only; speaker notes are counted in warnings but not indexed;
  charts and SmartArt are skipped.
* **XLSX.** First worksheet only; formulas are not evaluated (cached values are
  used); dates appear as serial numbers, not formatted dates.
* **HTML.** Regex-free tag scanner; script/style removed; no CSS-driven visibility
  logic, so hidden text may be indexed.
* **CSV.** Quote handling covers doubled quotes and embedded commas/newlines; no
  dialect sniffing.

## Engine limitations

* **Extractive only.** No sentence is generated. Answers are quotes joined with
  light connective text, so a question whose answer is spread across three
  sentences may read awkwardly.
* **Lexical retrieval.** BM25 with a shallow suffix normaliser; no synonyms, no
  embeddings, no cross-encoder reranking. Paraphrased questions can miss.
* **Abstention threshold.** `EVIDENCE_FLOOR = 0.35` is a judgement call; with very
  small corpora idf is unstable. Tuned by hand, not learned.
* **No figure/table understanding.** Tables inside PDFs are flat text.

## Product limitations

* **No authentication, no accounts, no sharing.** Single operator by design.
* **No streaming.** Chat responses are completed then returned.
* **Storage is a single JSON file.** Rewritten per mutation; fine for personal use,
  not for 10‚Åµ+ chunks.
* **No artifact regeneration on source change.** An artifact is a snapshot.
* **Notebook instructions are stored but not yet injected** into any answering
  prompt (there is no prompt: the engine is extractive). The field exists so a
  provider-backed engine can use it without a schema change.
* **URL/source discovery** absent (see limits 1‚Äì2).

## Open questions

1. What is NotebookLM's actual citation granularity in the current UI (sentence
   highlight vs. whole passage)? Unobservable here; our viewer highlights the whole
   chunk and scrolls to it.
2. Should abstention be a hard floor or a user-tunable slider? Currently fixed.
3. For a future model provider: budget/streaming policy, and whether answers may
   paraphrase (then citation validation must become span-level fuzzy matching).
4. Is a ZIP-bomb guard needed beyond declared-size checks if untrusted uploads
   become multi-user? Likely yes.

## URL sourcing (2026-10-31)

* **No outbound route from the sandbox.** URL ingestion is implemented and tested
  against a real loopback origin, but in this environment every public host returns
  `502 fetch_failed`. That is an environment fact, not a product capability gap.
* **HTTPS depends on `curl` being installed.** Without it the endpoint returns
  `501 fetch_transport_unavailable` and `/api/capabilities` says `transport: none`.
* **JavaScript-rendered pages are not rendered.** Only the served HTML text is
  extracted, matching the reference product's documented "text only" behaviour. A
  client-side-rendered page will yield little or no text.
* **No auth, no cookies, no paywalls** ‚Äî private and paywalled pages will fail or return
  a login page, which will be indexed as text. Recorded, not worked around.
* **The reference product's own ceilings are not copied.** Forge's are its own and
  configurable (`docs/reference/SOURCE_MATRIX.md`).
* **Notes participate through conversion.** The reference product lets a note be
  selected directly in chat *and* converted to a source. Forge implements conversion
  (one retrieval path, full provenance, no duplicated citation logic). Direct
  inclusion without conversion is not implemented ‚Äî that is a deliberate scope
  decision (`docs/DECISIONS.md` D14), not an oversight.
* **Live product, third-party video evidence, ASR/OCR/TTS/LLM, search providers, sharing
  and roles** remain blocked or unimplemented; see `docs/RESEARCH_BLOCKERS.md` and
  `docs/reference/FEATURE_MATRIX.md`. Video *tooling* was exercised on our own clip
  (`docs/reference/VIDEO_RESEARCH.md`), which is not evidence about any product.

## Spreadsheet tables (2026-10-31)

What was measured: `tests/fixtures/sales.xlsx` and `sales.csv` are **synthetic** fixtures
generated by `tests/fixtures/make_ooxml.py`. No spreadsheet produced by Excel, Numbers, Google
Sheets or LibreOffice was available under an authorized licence, so anything only those
producers emit is unverified.

* **Merged cells** ‚Äî a merged range is read as a value in the top-left cell and empty cells
  elsewhere. No de-merge logic; the user sees blanks where a merged header spanned columns.
* **Dates and times** are Excel serial numbers. Forge reads the stored number (e.g. `45658`),
  not a formatted date; there is no number-format table in the parser, so a date column will
  not aggregate meaningfully.
* **Shared formulas** (`<f t="shared" si="0"/>`) give no formula text on follower cells; the
  cached value is still read, but the "formula" annotation appears only on the master cell.
* **Percentages** keep the stored value: a cell formatted `45%` that stores `0.45` is read as
  `0.45`. The `45%` case is only recognised for CSV text.
* **No formula evaluation.** Only the cached result stored in the file is used. A workbook saved
  without cached values (rare, but possible) will read formula cells as empty.
* **`.xls` (BIFF8/5), ODS, Google Sheets exports that are not XLSX/CSV** ‚Äî no parser, rejected
  at kind detection.
* **Aggregation scope**: sum / average / min / max / count, one value column, at most one
  grouping column. No weighted averages, no distinct-count, no median, no date bucketing, no
  multi-column pivots.
* **Column choice is lexical.** The value column is picked by header-word overlap with the
  question (with a numeric-column tie-break). A vague question ("how much did we make?") where
  no header shares a word with the question is **not** aggregated ‚Äî it falls through to the
  text path, which may be less useful but is not wrong.
* **Ambiguous separators are refused.** `1,234` is read as one thousand two hundred thirty-four
  (three-digit tail = grouping); a European file meaning `1.234` with exactly three decimals
  would be misread. `1,23,456` is rejected outright.
* **Truncation**: sheets over 20,000 rows keep the first 20,000 and refuse aggregation. The cut
  is reported in the table's warnings and in the answer, never silent.
* **Row passages are one row per chunk** for spreadsheets, so a question spanning many rows is
  answered by several citations rather than a summary. That is intentional (one citation per
  row) but differs from prose chunking.

## Source Guide (2026-10-31)

* The guide is **extractive**, not generative: headline and summary lines are quotations. It
  cannot explain, condense across distant passages, or answer "what is this source arguing?" ‚Äî
  it can show what recurs and how the source is structured.
* Topic ranking is term frequency over stemmed content words plus adjacent two-word phrases.
  Acronyms and proper nouns are not recognised as entities; a phrase used only once is not
  promoted; three-word phrases are not detected.
* Suggested questions are templates ("What does this source say about X?"). They are labelled
  as suggestions; they are not questions the reference product asked.
* The outline is only as good as the parser's structure: pasted plain text has no headings, so
  its outline is empty. XLSX sources show sheets, not cell ranges.
* **`artifacts::summary`'s `lead` field is a truncation** (first 280 characters of the first
  chunk). It is not a summary and is not labelled as one; the Source Guide is the honest route.
* No caching: a guide is recomputed per request. It is deterministic, so two requests return
  identical content (covered by a test), but a very large source costs a full re-tokenisation
  each time.

## Chat style and length (2026-10-31)

* `style` changes **layout only**: evidence list, one paragraph, or per-quote source + locator.
  It cannot make an answer warmer, more formal, or simpler ‚Äî an extractive engine quotes, it
  does not compose. A test asserts the citation set is identical across styles.
* `length` sets a citation **count** (1 / 2 / 4). It is not a word count; a two-sentence
  passage and a forty-word passage count the same.
* With a configured-but-unreachable provider, only the citation budget is forwarded; the style
  vocabulary does not reach the provider (`partial`, see the feature matrix).
* Notebook instructions are stored and echoed in the chat response, but they cannot steer the
  extractive engine; no test claims they do.
* No streaming: the answer is computed, verified, then returned in one response. There is no
  "stop" button, and none is shown.

## Media metadata (2026-10-31)

What was measured: `crates/forge-core/src/media.rs` parses MP4-family box trees and
`POST /api/media/inspect` returns duration, per-track codec/kind/language/timescale/duration/
sample count/fps/display size/rotation/channels/sample rate. Cross-checked against `ffmpeg -i`
on `tests/fixtures/sample.mp4`, a clip **we** encoded; the numbers agree (6200 ms, 320√ó240,
10 fps, timescale 10240, 62 samples).

Limits that are real, not hypothetical:

* **MP4 family only.** Matroska/WebM, MPEG-TS and AVI are identified by magic bytes and then
  refused with a warning. Their durations, codecs and track counts are unknown here ‚Äî the API
  returns zero tracks rather than a guess.
* **No pixel format, bitrate or colour information.** Those live in `stsd`'s codec-specific
  extension and in `btrt` boxes; not parsed. `ffmpeg -i` reports `yuv420p`; Forge does not, and
  the response does not pretend to.
* **`fragmented: true` means sample counts are a lower bound.** `moof` runs are not summed.
* **Rotation comes from the display matrix, not the pixels.** 90/180/270 are read; values that
  are not a clean right angle are reported as 0 with the limitation recorded, because the UI
  cannot honour an arbitrary transform.
* **Video is not a source.** No frame decoding, no caption track reading, no transcription, and
  in this build no route to any platform to fetch one. `/api/capabilities` says so in the same
  words, and the inspect response carries `notes.decoded_frames: 0`.
* **The research tooling is not a dependency.** FFmpeg 7.0.2 was installed from PyPI for this
  session only; the product never shells out to it. A machine without FFmpeg can still run every
  test that matters here, because the fixture is committed.
* **Scene detection is luma-based and was observed to miss a cut.** On our clip the red‚Üígreen
  transition scores 0.0 while green‚Üíblue scores 0.4 (`VIDEO_RESEARCH.md`). Any future
  frame-sampling pipeline must not trust `select='gt(scene,‚Ä¶)'` alone.

## Chat streaming and Stop (2026-10-31)

What was measured: `POST /api/notebooks/:id/chat/stream` returns `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`
NDJSON frames, and the UI renders them as they arrive (jsdom drive-through with the transport
slowed by `?pace_ms=`, then a real abort).

Honest limits:

* **This is delivery streaming, not generation.** The extractive answer is complete before the
  first frame. If a model is ever wired in, this protocol can carry tokens, but today it cannot
  and the `start` frame says so.
* **A network drop after the last frame is written but before the client reads it loses the
  turn.** The server commits to history only on a complete delivery (D19). A retry re-asks.
* **No backpressure beyond the socket.** Frames are written as fast as the kernel accepts them;
  a slow client is handled by TCP flow control and the 30 s write timeout, not by a queue.
* **`?pace_ms=` exists for tests and debugging.** It sleeps between frames and changes nothing
  else. It is capped at 1 s and rejected above that.
* **No resume/replay.** An interrupted stream cannot be continued; the user asks again.
```

# User requirements and traceability

Source: `NLLM2/masterprompt.md` (sha256 `36ad5f80‚Ä¶3766`). Every requirement the
brief states is listed here with its status. Statuses are only **DONE** when a test
or a live command proves it; **PARTIAL** and **BLOCKED** say what is missing.

Legend: DONE = implemented and verified ¬∑ PARTIAL = works with a stated limit ¬∑
BLOCKED = impossible in this environment, reason recorded ¬∑ NOT STARTED = pending.

## A. Product shape

| # | Requirement | Status | Where / why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Complete, functional application (not a mockup, CLI or scaffold) | DONE | server + SPA, 36 UI assertions, real API |
| A2 | Built entirely inside a folder named `NLLM2` | DONE | `/home/user/testtemp/NLLM2` |
| A3 | Rust for core/backend; no Python/Node substitution | DONE | `crates/forge-core`, `crates/forge-server` |
| A4 | Not an agent workbench, not CLI-only | DONE | browser workspace; prior Python `forge/` untouched |
| A5 | Investigate ‚Üí document ‚Üí requirements before coding | DONE | `REA_EVIDENCE_INDEX.md`, `NOTEBOOKLM_PROTOCOL.md`, `FEATURE_PARITY.md`, `DECISIONS.md` |
| A6 | Keep going past MVP; extensible | DONE | artifacts, providers, exporters, capability matrix |
| A7 | Preserve existing work (`forge/`, `arena-vm/`) | DONE | untouched; separate tree |

## B. Sources

| # | Requirement | Status | Where / why |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Pasted text | DONE | `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/sources/text` |
| B2 | PDF | DONE | text-layer extraction, page locators; no OCR |
| B3 | DOCX | DONE | `ingest/ooxml.rs`, paragraph locators |
| B4 | Slides (PPTX) | DONE | slide-numbered locators |
| B5 | Spreadsheets (XLSX/CSV/TSV) | DONE | header-aware rows |
| B6 | Web URLs | BLOCKED | no TLS client in build; SSRF-validated then 501 |
| B7 | YouTube | BLOCKED | needs HTTPS + transcript API; no route |
| B8 | Audio/video files | BLOCKED | no ASR/FFmpeg offline |
| B9 | Images / OCR | BLOCKED | no OCR engine; images reported in warnings |
| B10 | Instagram | BLOCKED | needs authenticated HTTPS scraping |
| B11 | GitHub repos | BLOCKED | needs HTTPS; a local clone's files can be uploaded instead |
| B12 | Markdown / HTML | DONE | section + paragraph structure |
| B13 | Source removal, per-source status and errors | DONE | `DELETE /api/sources/{id}`, `status`/`error` fields |

## C. Understanding

| # | Requirement | Status | Where / why |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Ask questions of the corpus | DONE | `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/chat` |
| C2 | Answers grounded in sources only | DONE | extractive composition, tested |
| C3 | Clickable citations that open the exact locator | DONE | citation ‚Üí viewer at page/paragraph/row with highlight |
| C4 | Citation integrity checking | DONE | `validate_citations`, e2e asserts the quote is verbatim |
| C5 | Say "I don't know" instead of guessing | DONE | `EVIDENCE_FLOOR`, `abstained: true`, no citations |
| C6 | Multi-turn conversation history | DONE | conversations persisted, `conversation_id` round-trip |
| C7 | Notebook-level instructions | DONE | stored, echoed to chat response (not yet injected into prompts) |
| C8 | Semantic retrieval | NOT STARTED | no embedding model offline; lexical BM25 only |

## D. Notes and artifacts

| # | Requirement | Status | Where / why |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Notes with source links | DONE | `POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/notes` |
| D2 | Flashcards | DONE | deterministic, cited |
| D3 | Quizzes | DONE | corpus-derived distractors, answer key |
| D4 | Mind maps | DONE | term co-occurrence graph rendered as SVG |
| D5 | Study guide / FAQ / summary / report | DONE | each item cited |
| D6 | Audio overview | BLOCKED | no TTS; `audio_script` text deliverable instead |
| D7 | Video overview | BLOCKED | no TTS/video pipeline |
| D8 | Slides / infographic export | NOT STARTED | capability matrix says unsupported |

## E. Platform

| # | Requirement | Status | Where / why |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Responsive web UI | DONE | breakpoints at 1200/980/620 px; verified in CSS + jsdom |
| E2 | PWA-capable | DONE | manifest + service worker (shell cached, API never cached) |
| E3 | Provider abstraction with BYOK | PARTIAL | seam + key storage + validation DONE; remote calls impossible (D5) |
| E4 | Export / backup | DONE | notebook export/import JSON (`forge.notebook/1`), `POST /api/backup` |
| E5 | Security: SSRF / traversal / injection | DONE | see `SECURITY.md`, tested |
| E6 | Real tests | DONE | 128 Rust + 36 UI assertions |
| E7 | Documentation set | DONE | this file + 7 others in `docs/` |
| E8 | Multi-user accounts | NOT STARTED | single-operator design, bind to localhost |

## F. Investigation of the reference product

| # | Requirement | Status | Where / why |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Use REA to investigate Gemini Notebook | PARTIAL | REA **installs and runs** here (engine floor is a warning). It cannot reach a target: no browser/CDP and no route to Google. Corrected record in `docs/REA_EVIDENCE_INDEX.md` |
| F2 | Upgrade Node to satisfy REA | BLOCKED | `nodejs.org` and `nodejs.org/dist` return HTTP 000; npm carries no Node runtime. Not required anyway ‚Äî REA runs on 22.22.3 |
| F3 | Reverse-engineer Gemini Notebook | DONE (second-hand) | protocol recovered from pinned public RE captures, corroborated across 3 implementations, reimplemented in Rust with 15 tests (`docs/NOTEBOOKLM_PROTOCOL.md`) |
| F4 | Observe the live product directly | BLOCKED | Google hosts HTTP 000; no browser; no authenticated session |
| F5 | Live bridge to NotebookLM | NOT POSSIBLE HERE | `NoTransport` returns the reason; `/api/notebooklm/preview` shows the exact request instead |

## Standing constraints honoured

* ‚Çπ0: no paid services, no cloud, no API credits, no commercial licenses.
* FOSS only; no dependency that requires a paid tier.
* No faked evidence: every "unsupported" is reported as such by the API and UI.
* No credentials in git: `data/` is git-ignored; `secrets.json` is mode 0600.
* Small reversible changes, no destructive git operations.
```

# RPC & UI Reference

**Status:** Active
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-02
**Source of Truth:** `src/notebooklm/rpc/_identifiers.py` for method IDs; payload builders under `src/notebooklm/_web/` and golden tests under `tests/unit/`
**Purpose:** Reference for the Web backend's batchexecute methods, UI selectors, and payload structures

This reference is deliberately Web-specific: `RPCMethod` and
`client.rpc_call(...)` describe the batchexecute transport even when an
explicitly selected Android client installs native implementations for all 11
typed namespaces. For Android gRPC method contracts, start with the
[Android evidence index](android/README.md) and
[`android/endpoints.md`](android/endpoints.md).

> **Note:** Payload structures are extracted from the implementation builders in
> `src/notebooklm/_web/` and pinned by golden unit tests. Each payload includes a
> reference to its owning source file. The CREATE_ARTIFACT payloads below were
> re-verified against the live builders in `_web/params/artifacts.py` on
> 2026-06-11 (AUDIO, VIDEO_EXPLAINER, VIDEO_BRIEF, VIDEO_CINEMATIC,
> STUDY_GUIDE, BRIEFING_DOC, BLOG_POST, MIND_MAP, QUIZ, FLASHCARDS,
> INFOGRAPHIC, SLIDE_DECK, DATA_TABLE). Read-only notebook/source/artifact/chat/
> sharing/settings RPCs were live-captured again on 2026-06-15. Home, Sources,
> chat, and Studio selectors were rechecked the same day against a live Chrome
> session on a probe notebook.

---

### Source Type Codes (file uploads & sources)

Internal integer codes returned by `GET_NOTEBOOK` / `LIST_SOURCES` and consumed by
`Source.from_api_response()` (mapped to `SourceType` in
`src/notebooklm/_types/sources.py`).

| Code | `SourceType` | Used By |
|------|--------------|---------|
| 1 | `GOOGLE_DOCS` | Google Docs source |
| 2 | `GOOGLE_SLIDES` | Google Slides source |
| 3 | `PDF` | PDF upload |
| 4 | `PASTED_TEXT` | Inline pasted text |
| 5 | `WEB_PAGE` | Web URL source |
| 6 | `POWERPOINT` | PowerPoint upload (`.pptx`) |
| 7 | `GOOGLE_SPREADSHEET` | Native Google Sheets source after MIME disambiguation |
| 8 | `MARKDOWN` | Markdown file |
| 9 | `YOUTUBE` | YouTube URL |
| 10 | `MEDIA` | Audio / video upload |
| 11 | `DOCX` | Word document |
| 12 | `EXCEL` | Recovered-schema member; no reachable producer is known |
| 13 | `IMAGE` | Image upload |
| 14 | `GOOGLE_DRIVE` | Generic Drive source before MIME disambiguation (see note) |
| 15 | `GMAIL` | Recovered-schema member; no reachable producer is known |
| 16 | `CSV` | CSV upload |
| 17 | `EPUB` | EPUB upload (added in v0.4.0) |
| 18 | `GEMINI_CHAT` | Gemini chat source observed through Android `AddSources` |
| 19 | `AI_MODE_CHAT` | Recovered-schema member; no reachable producer is known |
| 20 | `EXPERT_INTELLIGENCE` | Google Play Books source added via `sources.add_play_book` (#2292); carries `ExpertIntelligenceSourceMetadata` at `metadata[18]` |

> Codes outside this map are surfaced as `SourceType.UNKNOWN` and emit `UnknownTypeWarning` on first occurrence so unmapped types don't crash callers.

> **Code `14` is a generic Drive code** (live-captured #1828/#1832): the backend
> returns it for a native Google Sheet and for Drive-hosted binaries such as a
> PDF. Drive sources carry no URL (`metadata[5]/[7]` are null and `metadata[0]`
> holds the Drive metadata block, not a URL ‚Äî see
> `SourceRow.drive_document_id`), so recognized original-content MIME values at
> `source[7][2]`, with a Drive-only metadata fallback, refine a Sheet to code 7
> (`GOOGLE_SPREADSHEET`) and a PDF to code 3 (`PDF`). An absent or unrecognized
> MIME remains `GOOGLE_DRIVE`; see `_disambiguate_type_code` in
> `src/notebooklm/_types/sources.py`.

### Source Settings Block (`source[3]`)

`Source.settings` (`SourceSettings`) carries **two independent status codes**, and
they answer different questions:

| Index | Proto tag | Field | Decoded as |
|-------|-----------|-------|------------|
| 1 | 2 | `status` | `SourceStatus` ‚Äî NotebookLM's own ingestion pipeline (`SourceRow.status`) |
| 3 | 4 | `userDriveSourceStatus` | `DriveSourceStatus` ‚Äî Drive-side health, Drive-backed rows only (`SourceRow.drive_status`) |

Shapes observed across 409 live source rows (2026-08-07 audit): `[null, 2]` √ó402,
`[null, 2, null, 3]` √ó4 (all Drive-backed, all `ACTIVE`), and
`[null, 2, [null,null,null,[]]]` √ó3.

### Additional Source Metadata (`source[5:8]`, `source[2]`)

The web source row carries useful fields beyond the four named by the recovered
mobile `Source` message. Uploaded-file rows may populate all three trailing
slots together:

| Index | Proto tag | `Source` field | Meaning |
|-------|-----------|----------------|---------|
| 5 | 6 | `download_url` | Direct download URL for the original file |
| 6 | 7 | `viewer_url` | Drive viewer URL for the original file |
| 7 | 8 | `content_mime` | MIME at blob descriptor index 2 |

The nested `SourceMetadata` row also exposes `word_count` at index 1,
`[revision_id, revision_timestamp]` at index 3, and `last_modified_at` at index
14. Their shapes and population are live-confirmed, but the mobile schema marks
the slots unused, so those semantic names are inferred and recorded as pinned
wire evidence rather than schema mappings.

### Drive Source Status Codes

| Code | `DriveSourceStatus` | Backend member |
|------|---------------------|----------------|
| 0 | *(normalized to `None`)* | `DRIVE_SOURCE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED` |
| 1 | `INACCESSIBLE` | `DRIVE_SOURCE_STATUS_INACCESSIBLE` |
| 2 | `SYNCING` | `DRIVE_SOURCE_STATUS_SYNCING` |
| 3 | `ACTIVE` | `DRIVE_SOURCE_STATUS_ACTIVE` |
| 4 | `DELETED` | `DRIVE_SOURCE_STATUS_DELETED` |
| 5 | `GEN_AI_ACCESS_DENIED` | `DRIVE_SOURCE_STATUS_GEN_AI_ACCESS_DENIED` |

> Index 3 is absent on 405/409 rows ‚Äî and proto3 omits zero-valued fields, so an
> absent slot means "no Drive claim", not "not a Drive source". The backend's
> `0` means the same thing, so the decoder normalizes it to `None` rather than
> modelling it (recorded in `ENUM_GAPS`). Only `ACTIVE` has
> been observed live; the degraded members come from the backend enum recovered
> from the official Android app (`docs/android/enums.txt`) and are pinned in
> `tests/_guardrails/_wire_contract.py`. A populated-but-unmapped code decodes to
> `DriveSourceStatus.UNKNOWN` (never `None`) and warns once (#2111).

## UI/Library Operation Parity

Use this table as the coverage index before adding or changing selectors. "UI
covered" means the selector or flow is documented below from the 2026-06-15 live
Chrome probe. "Library-only" means the Python API deliberately exposes a backend
or local convenience that has no stable web-control equivalent in the capture.

| Library surface | UI parity status | Notes |
|-----------------|------------------|-------|
| `NotebooksAPI.list/create/get/rename/delete/remove_from_recent` | Partial UI coverage | Home create/card/action-menu selectors are covered. Rename/delete/remove-recent are represented by project action menus and RPC payloads; destructive menu items were not re-mutated in the live probe. |
| `NotebooksAPI.get_summary/get_description/get_metadata/get_raw/get_share_url` | Library-only/read-derived | Summary content is visible in the chat panel, but these are read/format helpers rather than direct UI controls. |
| `SourcesAPI.list/get/search/add_url/add_text/add_file/add_drive/delete/rename` | UI covered | Source cards, indexed passage search, add-source modal tabs, upload/Drive entry points, source menus, and submit selectors are documented. |
| `SourcesAPI.get_guide/get_fulltext` | UI covered/read-derived | Opening a source exposes the source viewer, source guide toggle, title input, and source content; `get_fulltext()` is the programmatic extraction path. |
| `SourcesAPI.wait_*`, `refresh`, `check_freshness` | Library-only/partial UI | Wait methods are polling helpers. Refresh/freshness RPCs are documented, but no stable refresh selector was captured in the current source-list/label-list state. |
| `LabelsAPI.list/sources/generate/create/update/rename/set_emoji/add_sources/remove_sources/delete` | UI covered | Auto-label, Reorganize all sources, manual label creation, inline rename, emoji picker, delete, label panels, and source Move to label checkboxes are documented. |
| `ChatAPI.ask/get_history/session_status/cancel/delete_conversation/configure/save_answer_as_note` | UI covered | Chat input/send, live generation state/cancel, options/delete history, configure dialog, and `Save message to a note` buttons are documented. `get_conversation_id`, cache methods, and history parsing are backend/local conveniences. |
| `ArtifactsAPI.generate_*`, `suggest_reports`, `list/get/get_prompt/delete/rename/share/export` | UI covered/partial | All live Studio generation tiles and option sets are documented. Artifact list/open/menu/view-prompt/share/delete selectors are covered; export/download/retry availability depends on artifact type/status. |
| `ArtifactsAPI.download_*`, `wait_for_completion`, `poll_status`, `revise_slide`, `retry_failed` | Library-only/conditional UI | Downloads, polling, and slide revision are programmatic conveniences. Retry requires a failed artifact row; the RPC is documented but no failed-row retry selector was present in the probe. |
| `NotesAPI.list/get/create/update/delete` | UI covered/partial | Add note, note row, note view close/title input, and note menu delete are documented. Rich body editing uses NotebookLM's internal editor; keep selectors conservative. |
| `MindMapsAPI.list/generate/rename/delete/get_tree` | UI covered/partial | Interactive mind map generation is the live Studio tile. Note-backed mind maps are a synthetic/library backing; tree extraction via `GET_INTERACTIVE_HTML` is programmatic. |
| `ResearchAPI.start/poll/wait/import_sources` | UI covered for start only | Source discovery corpus/mode/submit selectors map to fast/deep web/Drive research. Polling and import verification are backend workflow helpers. |
| `SettingsAPI.get/set_output_language`, `SharingAPI.get_status/set_public/set_view_level/add_user/set_users/update_user/remove_user` | UI covered/partial | Settings and Share dialogs are covered at entry/save/copy selectors. Programmatic user-permission mutations go beyond the captured UI selectors. |
| UI-only note operations | UI-only | Note menus expose `Convert to source`, `Convert all notes to source`, `Export to Docs`, and `Export to Sheets`; keep them documented as selectors unless/until a public library method owns those flows. |

## Using Selector Lists

Selectors are provided as Python lists of **fallback options**. Try each in order:

```python
async def try_selectors(page, selectors: list[str], action="click", timeout=5000):
    """Try multiple selectors until one works."""
    for selector in selectors:
        try:
            element = page.locator(selector)
            if action == "click":
                await element.click(timeout=timeout)
            elif action == "fill":
                return element
            return True
        except Exception:
            continue
    raise Exception(f"None of the selectors worked: {selectors}")


# Example usage
await try_selectors(page, HOME_SELECTORS["create_notebook"])
```

The live web UI also sends a sixth filter/tail slot:

slot because the backend accepts the compact form.

In the response notebook row, chat settings live at `[7]` as
`[[goal_code, custom_prompt?], [response_length_code]]`. A default-valued
component may be elided as an empty child list: `[[], []]` means
DEFAULT/DEFAULT, while `[[2, "persona"], []]` means a custom goal with the
default response length. Older never-configured rows may instead carry `null`
for the whole slot.

### RPC: ADD_SOURCE (izAoDd) - URL

**Sources:** `_web/sources/add.py::SourceAddService.add_url_source()` (single item),
`SourcesAPI.add_urls_batch()` backed by
`_web/sources/batch.py::SourceBatchAddService.add_urls()` (true batch)

```python
# URL goes at position [2] in an 11-element source spec.
params = [
    [[None, None, [url], None, None, None, None, None, None, None, 1]],
    notebook_id,  # 1: Notebook ID
    [2, None, None, [1, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, [1]]],
    # 2: Shared request-options wrapper
]
```

The public Python method plus the existing MCP `source_add(urls=[...])` and REST
`/sources/batch` endpoints put multiple URL specs in `params[0]` and issue this RPC once. `AddSources` is
per-item rather than atomic: successful Source rows remain in request order,
while failed entries are silently omitted unless every entry fails (then the
RPC raises). The adapters reconcile omissions with an ERROR-status source list
and restore positional `SourceBatchItemOutcome` rows. Each row carries explicit
confirmed/rejected/unknown/not-sent evidence; adapters do not derive continuation
policy from an HTTP status or exception category. This true-batch path disables transport
retries because a timeout leaves the committed subset unknown; the ordinary
single-item `sources.add_url()` path also sends its mutation once and surfaces
an unknown outcome without automatic replay.
